iii
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
he BARI Annual Report for 2024-25 is more than a 
technical record; it is a testament to the resilience and 
ingenuity of our scientific community. As we navigate a 
rapidly shifting global agricultural landscape, this document 
serves as a vital roadmap of our progress.
Over the past year, BARI has pushed the boundaries of 
innovation across our core mandates-from the genetic 
improvement of tubers, oilseeds, and pulses to the 
climate-smart management of our soil and water resources. 
Beyond traditional variety development, our focus has 
sharpened on the "frontiers" of agriculture: biotechnological 
breakthroughs, low-cost mechanization, and high-impact 
strategies for our most challenged landscapes, including hill 
tracts, char lands, and saline-affected belts.
While a single volume cannot capture the full depth of our 
thousand-plus experiments, this report offers a strategic 
window into the milestones narrowing the gap between 
national food demand and sustainable production. For those 
seeking granular technical data, our specialized Center and 
Divisional reports remain an essential companion resource.
We extend our deepest gratitude to the scientists, editors, 
and contributors whose dedication made this publication 
possible. We are confident that these findings will empower 
policymakers, researchers, and stakeholders as we work 
together to secure the nutritional future of our nation.
 Dr. Abdullah Yousuf Akhond
 Director General, BARI

0 1
TUBER CROPS
Tuber Crops viz. potato, sweet potato, aroids, yam 
and cassava are essential food crops. Tuber Crops 
Research Centre (TCRC), BARI deals with these 
crops. The main research thrust of TCRC is on variety 
development considering high yield, short duration, 
biotic-abiotic stress tolerant, good keeping and 
processing quality. Breeding, biotechnology, disease 
& pest management, organic culture, postharvest 
processing and socio-economics are the major concern 
groups to improve tuber crops. Achievements during 
2024-2025 on varietal improvement, biotechnology 
approaches, production technology, soil, water and 
nutrient management, disease management, insect 
management, postharvest technology, organic culture 
and technology transfer have been given below. 
Varietal Improvement
Potato Breeding
Hybridization for high yielding (early bulking 
and early maturity, export quality etc.) Potato 
variety development
A.T.M.T. Islam, M.A. Kawochar, S. Naznin, T. 
Jahan, M. Rahman, M. M. H. Molla and M. M. 
Rahman
Hybridization was done at Debigonj and Gazipur 
using 64 and 52 advanced lines/varieties, respectively 
under 16 hours extended photoperiod to create 
variability, and to select superior genotypes in the 
subsequent generations. For early bulking and early 
mature variety development targeted parents were 
BARI Alu-86, BARI Alu-79, etc. For improving 
natural storage capacity targeted parents were BARI 
Alu-62, BARI Alu-100 (Ottawa) and BARI Alu-
67 (Gorgina) etc. Different high yielding varieties 
were used for high yielding variety development. 
We found several successful crosses by using those 
varieties as male and female parent and collected 
seeds from crosses for developing early bulking, 
early mature, longer natural storage capacity and high 
yielding varieties at both the locations. Those seeds 
will be sown next year for F1 seedling production 
for subsequent variety development process.
Production of Potato seedling tubers from F1 seed 
(F1C0)
M. A. Kawochar, M. Rahman, A.T.M. T. Islam, S. 
Naznin, T. Jahan and M. M. Rahman
Hybrid true seeds which were produced in 2024-25 
at Gazipur and Debiganj were sown at Breeder Seed 
Production Centre, BSPC, Debiganj, Panchagarh 
during this season (2024-25). Around 590 crosses 
were grouped based on pedigree of parents. To 
facilitate field sowing, we used the "plug mix" 
methods. With "plug mix", seed is pre-germinated 
in a prepared soil mix and sown in tray which results 
good germination and seedling establishment. After 
harvesting of all plantlets, 210 single plants and 630 
single tubers of 650 crosses were selected. In total 
100 kg seedling tubers were stored for next year.
Field evaluation of F 1 Potato seedling tubers 
(F1C1)
M. A. Kawochar, A.T.M. T. Islam, S. Naznin, M. 
Rahman, T. Jahan and M. M. Rahman
During the selection process all potato clones are 
examined critically. Each generation materials are 
planted separately. Eight-five single tubers from 
354 crosses were were selected and stored at BSPC, 
Debigonj for further evaluation.
Selection (POT, SOT and AOT) of Potato clones 
in subsequent generations (F1C2, F1C3 and F1C4)
M. A. Kawochar, A.T.M. T. Islam, S. Naznin, M. 
Rahman, T. Jahan and M. M. Rahman
During the selection process all potato clones are 
examined critically. Each generation materials are 
planted separately. From the planted clone's single

Secondary observation trial with Potato 
germplasm (F1C3)
M. A. Kawochar, A.T.M. T. Islam, S. Naznin, M. 
Rahman, T. Jahan and M. M. Rahman
Last year's collected tubers were planted 
individually in the field. During the selection 
process all potato clones are examined critically. 
Each material (F 1C2) was planted separately. 
From the planted 30 single row (F 1C2) a total of 
15 single plot weighing 144 kg were selected. The 
harvested tubers of selected clones stored at BSPC 
cold storage. The selected potato clones will be 
evaluated in the next season. 
Advanced observation trial with Potato 
germplasm (F1C4)
A.T.M.T. Islam, M. A. Kawochar, S. Naznin, M. 
Rahman, T. Jahan and M. M. Rahman
Last year's collected tubers were planted individually 
in the field. During the selection process all potato 
clones are examined critically. Each material (F1C3) 
was planted separately. In advanced observational 
trial (F1C4) 16 potato clones weighing 1450 kg were 
selected and stored at BSPC, Debiganj for further 
evaluation.
Preliminary yield trial with Potato clones (F1C5)
M. A. Kawochar, A.T.M. T. Islam, S. Naznin, M. 
Rahman, T. Jahan and M. M. Rahman
An evaluation study was conducted with 27 clones 
(21.9, 21.10b,21.60, 21.60a, 21.98, 21.99, 21.105, 
21.113, 21.144, 21.146, 21.164, 21.177, 21.178, 
21.185, 21.197, 21.205, 21.213, 21.224, 21.228, 
21.239, 21.250, 21.260, 21.264, 21.273, 21.274, 
21.303, and 21.382) along with four check varieties 
BARI Alu-13, BARI Alu-25, BARI Alu-28 and 
BARI Alu-62 at TCRC, BARI, Gazipur and BSPC, 
Debigonj, Panchagarh during 2024-25. In this study, 
it was noticed that most of the characters viz. days 
to start of emergence, days to 50% emergence, plant 
vigor, plant height, number of stem per hill, tuber 
weight per hill, tuber yield and dry matter (%) varied 
significantly across the environment. The clone 
21.382 gave the highest yield (59.9 t/ha) imitated 
by 21.77 (58.5 t/ha) at Debiganj while the clone 
21.185 gave the highest yield (35.0 t/ha) at Gazipur. 
Considering mean performance over the location, 
the top most result was obtained from the clone 
21.177 (39.9 t/ha). All of the clones showed maturity 
between 85-97 days in Debiganj. Considering the 
performance of all the clones towards the studied 
parameters, the clones may be selected as superior 
for the next year trial. Multi-locational (SYT) trials 
need to be conducted to get performance against 
diverse weather to find out the more stable variety in 
the context of Bangladesh.
Secondary yield trial with clonal Potato hybrids 
(F1C6)
A.T.M.T. Islam, M.A. Kawochar, S. Naznin, 
T. Jahan, M. Rahman, M. Selim, M. K. Alam, 
M. Sultana, M.T. Rahman, M.B. Anwar, K. U. 
Ahammad, M. S. Rahman, M.M Kadir and M. M. 
Rahman
Thirteen genotypes (20.4, 20.7, 20.17, 20.25, 20.27, 
20.34, 20.35, 20.85a, 20.146, 20.215, 20.268, 
20.282 and 20.282a) along with three checks: BARI 
Alu-13 (Granola), BARI Alu-25 (Asterix) and 
BARI Alu 62 were evaluated at six agro-ecological 
locations during 2024-25 cropping season. The 
Clone 20.282 gave the significantly highest tuber 
yield (56.35 t/ha) at Bogura during final harvest. At 
Debigonj, the clone 20.27 produced the statistically 
highest ( 68.26 t/ha) tuber yield followed by 20.4 
(60.71 t/ha), and 20.282 (59.30 t/ha). At Gazipur, 
the highest tuber yield came from the clone 20.35 
(36.30 t/ha) which was statistically similar to the 
clone 20.17 (34.82 t/ha) and 20.282 (34.78 t/ha). At 
Jamalpur, clone 20.282 gave the significantly higher 
yield (54.10 t/ha) while clone 20.215 (35.98 t/ha) 
gave the significantly higher yield at Jashore. At 
Munshiganj, clone 20.17 (48.01 t/ha) provided the 
higher yield. Clone 20.282 gave the average higher 
yield over the location and all tested genotypes. 
The clones 20.4, 20.27, 20.215 and 20.282 can be 
selected for next year AYT due to their higher tuber 
yield potentialities and other yield contributing 
characteristics.

BARI Annual Report 2024-25
Tuber Crops I 3
Regional yield trial with clonal hybrids of Potato
A.T.M.T. Islam, M.A. Kawochar, S. Naznin, 
T. Jahan, M. Rahman, M. Selim, M. K. Alam, 
M. Sultana, M.T. Rahman, M.B. Anwar, K. U. 
Ahammad, M. S. Rahman, M.M Kadir and M. M. 
Rahman
Three hybrids namely 16.62, 17.18 and 18.46 and 
three CIP germaplasm CIP402, CIP444 and CIP449 
along with three check varieties BARI Alu-13 
(Granola), BARI Alu-25 (Asterix) and BARI Alu-
62 were evaluated at six agro-ecological locations 
during 2024-25 cropping season. Clone 18.46 gave 
the statistically highest tuber yield (42.06 t/ha) which 
was statistically similar to the clone 17.18 (38.04 t/
ha), CIP 444 (38.52 t/ha) and BARI Alu-62 (38.16 
t/ha) at Bogura during final harvest. At debigonj, 
clone 17.18 provided the significantly higher 
yield (54.72 t/ha) followed by 18.46 (51.80 t/ha), 
16.62 (49.44 t/ha) and CIP 444 (49.55 t/ha). Clone 
18.46 performed as the highest yielder at Jamalpur, 
Jashore and Munshiganj location providing 50.01 
t/ha, 42.23 t/ha and 39.27 t/ha respectively. The 
average highest yield found in clone 18.46 (41.98 
t/ha). This clone can be recommended for release 
as table varieties due to their higher tuber yield 
potentialities. 
Regional yield trial of nutrient (Fe and Zn) 
enriched Potato variety development (set I)
A.T.M.T. Islam, M.A. Kawochar, S. Naznin, 
T. Jahan, M. Rahman, M. Selim, M. K. Alam, 
M. Sultana, M.T. Rahman, M.B. Anwar, K. U. 
Ahammad, M. S. Rahman, M.M Kadir and M. M. 
Rahman
Eight CIP germplasm namely CIP 405, CIP 408, 
CIP 412, CIP 413, CIP 414, CIP 420, CIP 432, CIP 
442 along with three check varieties BARI Alu-13 
(Granola), BARI Alu-25 (Asterix) and BARI Alu-
62 were evaluated at Bogura, Debigonj, Gazipur, 
Jamalpur, Jashore and Munshiganj during 2024-
2025 cropping season in RCB design with three 
replications. CIP 413 (42.34 t/ha) exhibited the 
highest statistically significant tuber yield, followed 
by CIP 412 (39.13 t/ha), BARI Alu-62 (38.20 t/ha), 
BARI Alu-25 (Asterix) (37.73 t/ha) and BARI Alu-
13 (Granola) (36.26 t/ha) at Bogura during the final 
harvest. At debigonj, CIP 413 (50.50 t/ha) provided 
the significantly higher yield followed by CIP 412 
(39.13 t/ha). The lowest significant yielder was CIP 
405 (7.27 t/ha) at Debigonj. CIP 413 also provided 
the significantly highest yield (34.81 t/ha) followed 
by CIP 412 (32.16 t/ha), CIP 432 (31.41 t/ha), BARI 
Alu-25 (Asterix) (30.13 t/ha and BARI Alu-62 
(27.21 t/ha) at Gazipur location. At Jamalpur, BARI 
Alu-62 gave the statistically higher yield (35.78 t/
ha) followed by CIP 412 (32.79 t/ha), CIP 413 
(34.43 t/ha), CIP 442 (28.19 t/ha) and BARI Alu-25 
(Asterix) (31.44 t/ha). At Jashore, CIP 413 also gave 
the significantly highest yield (40.60 t/ha) which 
was statistically similar to BARI Alu 62 (37.17 t/ha) 
followed by CIP 412 (36.13 t/ha) and BARI Alu-25 
(Asterix) (34.62 t/ha). At Munshigonj, CIP 413 also 
provided the significantly highest yield (40.06 t/ha) 
followed by CIP 412 (37.97 t/ha). The maximum 
average production recorded in CIP 413 (41.46 t/
ha), while the lowest yield was observed in CIP 405 
(10.07 t/ha). Consequently, the genotype CIP 413 
is suggested for release as a variety high in zinc and 
iron.The maximum average production recorded 
in CIP 413 (41.46 t/ha), while the lowest yield was 
observed in CIP 405 (10.07 t/ha). The genotype CIP 
413 is suggested for release as a variety with high in 
zinc and iron. 
Regional yield trial of nutrient (Fe and Zn) 
enriched Potato variety development (set II)
A.T.M.T. Islam, M.A. Kawochar, S. Naznin, 
T. Jahan, M. Rahman, M. Selim, M. K. Alam, 
M. Sultana, M.T. Rahman, M.B. Anwar, K. U. 
Ahammad, M. S. Rahman, M.M Kadir and M. M. 
Rahman
Eight CIP germplasm namely CIP404, CIP421, 
CIP423, CIP424, CIP428, CIP433, CIP438, 
CIP441 along with three check varieties BARI 
Alu-13 (Granola), BARI Alu-25 (Asterix) and 
BARI Alu-62 were evaluated at Bogura, Debigonj, 
Gazipur, Jamalpur, Jashore and Munshiganj during 
2024-2025 cropping season. CIP 433 (49.49 t/
ha) exhibited the highest statistically significant 
tuber yield whereas the lowest yielder was CIP 424 
(20.32 t/ha) at Debigonj during the final harvest. 
At Gazipur, BARI Alu-13 (Granola) (36.97 t/ha) 
provided the significantly higher yield which was 
statistically similar to CIP 433 (36.34 t/ha), CIP 441

germplasm

In February 2022, thirteen sweet potato germplasm 
were acquired from the International Potato Center 
(CIP) in Peru and Mozambique. These germplasms 
were first grown in a tissue culture laboratory to 
ensure their successful propagation and subsequently 
transferred to the field for long-term conservation

research and development efforts in sweet potato 
cultivation. 
Observational yield trial of Sweet potato 
germplasm
M. Rahman, M. A. Ali, M. A. H. Khan, T. Hasan, E. 
H. M. S. Rahaman, D. Chanda, M. M. H. Molla and 
M. M. Rahman
Sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas L.) is an important 
root crop, valued for its high carbohydrate content 
and potential for food security. This study evaluated 
1,006 genotypes derived from seven families 
to assess variation in commercial storage root 
number (CSRN) and commercial storage root 
weight (CSRW) and identify superior genotypes 
for breeding programs. Out of these, 70 genotypes 
were selected based on their performance, with 27 
genotypes common to both CSRN- and CSRW-
based selections. Substantial genotypic variation 
was observed across families. CIP117317 and 
CIP117620 exhibited higher mean CSRN and 
CSRW, while Moz.1.15 showed consistently lower 
values. Heritability estimates were moderate to high 
for both traits, indicating strong genetic control. 
The results highlight significant opportunities for 
selecting genotypes with superior storage root 
number and weight, providing a foundation for 
future sweetpotato improvement programs.

Tuber Crops I 7
Advanced yield trial of Sweet potato germplasm 
(early)
M. A. H. Khan, M. Rahman, M. A. Ali, T. Hasan, M. 
M. H. Molla and M. M. Rahman
Sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas L.) is a climate-resilient 
crop that contributes to food and nutrition security 
in Bangladesh. Developing early bulking genotypes 
with high and stable yield is a breeding priority for 
ensuring timely harvests and increased cropping 
intensity. In this study, six early bulking sweetpotato 
genotypes, including one released variety (BARI 
Misti Alu-12) and five CIP advanced clones, were 
evaluated across five agro-ecological environments 
in Bangladesh during the 2024-25 growing season. 
Data were analyzed using heatmaps, ANOV A, 
regression-based stability (Eberhart-Russell model), 
and genotype × environment interaction (GEI) 
models. Results revealed significant genotypic 
variation for storage root yield (p < 0.001). BARI 
Misti Alu-12 consistently produced the highest mean 
yield (16.2 t ha−1), followed by CIP114410.2020.183 
(12.7 t ha−1), both showing stable performance 
across environments. Gazipur and Jamalpur were 
the most favorable locations, while Debiganj was 
the least productive. Stability analysis confirmed 
that BARI Misti Alu-12 combined high yield with 
wide adaptability, while CIP114410.2020.305 
and CIP114706.2020.22 performed poorly. These 
findings suggest that BARI Misti Alu-12 remains the 
most suitable variety for wide-scale dissemination, 
while CIP114410.2020.183 can also be utilized in 
hybridization programs for its stability.
Regional yield trial of selected Sweet potato 
advanced lines for leafy vegetables
M. A. H. Khan, M. Rahman, S. Parvin, M. A. Ali, T. 
Hasan, M. M. H. Molla and M. M. Rahman
Sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas L.) leaves are 
a nutritious leafy vegetable with potential for 
human consumption, but their sensory quality and 
nutritional composition vary among genotypes 
and growing environments. This study evaluated 
six sweetpotato genotypes, including advanced 
lines and released varieties, across five locations 
during the 2024-25 season (Panchagarh, Jamalpur, 
Chattogram, Bogura, and Gazipur). Leaves were 
collected, cooked under standardized conditions, 
and assessed by a trained sensory panel for full 
mouthfeel, bitterness, and presence of fiber. Results 
revealed significant differences among genotypes 
and locations for all attributes. An/22 consistently 
achieved the highest overall ranking, demonstrating 
superior mouthfeel, low fiber content, and moderate 
bitterness, followed by H16ej/10 and BARI Misty 
Alu 11. In contrast, BARI Misty Alu-17 and 
H9.10/12 were less preferred due to higher fiber 
content and less favorable mouthfeel. Nutritional 
profiling further confirmed the superiority of An/22, 
which recorded the highest vitamin C content (76.92 
mg/100 g), elevated anthocyanin (0.68 mg/100 
g), and higher carbohydrate levels (6.33%). These 
findings highlight the importance of integrating 
sensory and nutritional evaluation in identifying 
sweetpotato genotypes with superior leaf quality, 
providing valuable guidance for breeding programs 
and promoting the utilization of sweetpotato leaves 
as a nutrient-rich food source.
Regional yield trial of selected Sweet potato 
advanced lines
M. A. H. Khan, M. Rahman, M. A. Ali, T. Hasan, E. 
H. M. S. Rahaman, D. Chanda, M. M. H. Molla and 
M. M. Rahman
Sweetpotato (Ipomoea batatas L.) plays a vital 
role in food and nutritional security, particularly in 
developing countries. To enhance productivity and 
identify adaptable, high-yielding cultivars, twelve 
sweetpotato genotypes comprising nine advanced 
candidate lines and three BARI-released varieties 
as checks were evaluated in a Regional Yield Trial 
(RYT) during the 2024-25 season across five 
representative locations in Bangladesh (Gazipur, 
Bogura, Jamalpur, Panchagarh, and Chattogram). 
The trial was conducted in a Randomized Complete 
Block Design (RCBD) with three replications. Data 
were recorded on yield and yield-contributing traits, 
including number and weight of commercial and 
non-commercial roots, foliage weight, dry matter 
content, and storage root yield. Combined ANOV A 
revealed highly significant (p < 0.001) effects of 
location, genotype, and their interaction for most 
traits, highlighting the influence of both genetic 
and environmental factors. Among the locations, 
Bogura and Panchagarh supported the highest 
yields, while Gazipur and Chattogram were less 
favorable. Genotypic differences were evident, with 
BARI Mistialu-18 (24.7 t ha−1), BARI Mistialu-12 
(23.6 t ha−1), and advanced line H16.ej/10 (22.6 t

8 I Tuber Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
ha−1) ranking among the top performers. Fox's TOP 
third analysis confirmed the broad adaptability of 
H16.ej/10 and the BARI checks, while genotypes 
such as H5.ej/10, H9.10/12, and H9.48/11 showed 
potential for specific environments. Conversely, 
Moz. 1.9 and SPM-103 were consistently poor 
performers. The study highlights H16.ej/10 emerged 
as the most promising candidate for wide adaptation 
and future varietal release, while several other lines 
demonstrated potential for specific environments.

Screening of salt-tolerant Sweet potato genotypes 
in saline area
M. Rahman, M. A. Ali, M. A. H. Khan, T. Hasan, S. 
Mondol, E. H. M. S. Rahaman, D. Chanda, M. M. H. 
Molla and M. M. Rahman
An experiment was conducted during the 2024-25 
sweet potato growing season at Shaympur Upazilla, 
Sathkhira, Bangladesh, to evaluate the performance 
of three sweet potato genotypes, H.16.ej/10, 
H.9.7/12, and BARI Sweet Potato-12, under saline 
conditions. The trial was set up in a Randomized 
Complete Block Design (RCBD) with three 
replications. Soil salinity, initially at 1.75 dS/m, 
increased to a peak of 7.15 dS/m in early March 
before declining. Analysis of variance (ANOV A) 
revealed highly significant genotypic differences 
(p < 0.01) for most traits, including yield and yield 
components, confirming genetic variability among 
the genotypes. Genotype H.16.ej/10 emerged as 
the superior performer, consistently showing the 
highest values for all measured traits, including 
length of the main vine (91.85 cm), land coverage 
(92.33%), total biomass (518.67 g), and marketable 
root yield (3106.67 g or 8.32 t/ha). In contrast, the 
check variety BARI Sweet Potato-12 had the lowest 
values for most traits. The superior performance of 
H.16.ej/10 under saline stress highlights its potential 
as a promising candidate for commercial cultivation 
in the coastal saline regions of Bangladesh, 
contributing to enhanced food security and farmer 
livelihoods.

Ghataman kachu
Advanced yield trial of Ghataman kachu in 
relation to spacing
F. Begum, M. S. Alam, M. M. H. Molla, M. K. Alam 
and M. M. Rahman
Three spacing like 60 cm × 60 cm, 75 cm × 60 cm 
and 75 cm × 75 cm on Ghataman Kachu (Alocasia 
sp.) were evaluated during March to December 
2024 at the field of Tuber Crops Research Centre, 
Gazipur. The vegetative growth parameter, yield 
contributing characters and yield were influenced 
significantly. 
The highest weight of individual rhizome (835 g) 
was recorded in the widest spacing of 75 cm × 75 cm 
and the lowest weight of individual rhizome (762.5 
g) was obtained in the closest spacing of 60 cm × 60 
cm. The highest yield (19.95 t/ha) was obtained in 
the closest spacing of 60 cm × 60 cm followed by 
the medium spacing of 75 cm × 60 cm (16.23 t/ha) 
whereas the lowest yield (14.18 t/ha) was recorded in 
the widest spacing of 75 cm × 75 cm. The percentage 
of dry matter was statistically influenced by spacing 
(Table 2). The highest dry matter (24.38%) was 
obtained in the medium spacing of 75 cm × 60 cm 
followed by the widest spacing of 75 cm × 75 cm 
(23.30%) whereas it was the lowest (22.88%) in the 
closest spacing of 60 cm × 60 cm.

Twenty-four yam genotypes, including breeding

5, Jas-6, Jas-7, Jas-8 and Jas-9 were evaluated in

Secondary yield trial of yam
M. H. Rashid, K.A.M. M. Rahman, B. Anwar, F. 
Yasmin, M.M. Molla and M. M. Rahman
Eight yam genotypes-DABN-1, DAG-1, DAG-
2, DAG-3, DAG-4, DAS-1, and DAN-1 were 
evaluated at Gazipur during 2022-2023 cropping 
season. Among the evaluated yam germplasm, 
DAG-2 demonstrated superior overall performance 
with high plant vigor, tuberlet production, and the 
highest yield (35.1 t/ha). DAG-3 and DABN-1 also 
performed well in yield and tuber characteristics. 
Genotypes such as DAG-4 and DAN-1, while 
producing more bulbils, had poor tuber yield and 
may be more suitable for bulbil-focused breeding 
programs. These findings suggest DAG-2 as a 
promising candidate for further multiplication and 
release in yam improvement programs.

Growth and yield performance of sweet potato as 
influenced by mixed fertilizer
M.H.Sarker, S. Parvin, S.S.Kakon, R,Akter, 
M.K.Alam, and M. M. Rahman
A field experiment was conducted at the Tuber Crops 
Research Centre (TCRC), Bangladesh Agricultural 
Research Institute (BARI), Gazipur during rabi 
season 2024-25 with five levels of fertilizer i.e., (F1) 
RDF (FGR, 2021), (F 2) BENGAL mixed fertilizer 
(NPKS =8: 20: 14: 5), (F 3) ACI mixed fertilizer 
(Ratno) (NPKS =8: 20: 14: 5), (F 4) SEMCO mixed 
fertilizer (NPKS =12: 15: 20: 6), (F5) control (native) 
and three varieties namely V1 = BARI Mistialu-12, 
V2 = BARI Mistialu-17 and V3 = BARI Mistialu-18 
with a view to find out the suitable mixed fertilizer 
for higher yield of sweet potato. The experiment 
was laid out in a randomized complete block design 
(RCBD) with three replications. Results revealed 
that among the variety BARI Mistialu-18 performed 
better in respects of tuberous root yield (37.67 t ha -
1) when ACI mixed fertilizer (Ratno) (NPKS =8: 
20: 14: 5) was applied for sweet potato production. 
Therefore, ACI mixed fertilizer (Ratno) (NPKS =8: 
20: 14: 5) may be practiced to cultivate sweet potato 
in our country for higher production.

Effect of different organic manure on the severity 
of common scab disease and yield of Potato 
M. Salim and M. K. Alam
An experiment was conducted at the research field of 
the Tuber Crops Research Sub-Center, Bangladesh 
Agricultural Institute, Munshiganj, during the potato 
growing season of 2024-25 with six treatments viz. 
i. T1 = ACI Organic Fertilizer @3 t/ha ii. T2 = Neem 
oil cake@3 t/ha iii. T 3 = Vermicompost @3 t/ha iv. 
T4 = Cowdung @3 t/ha v. T 5 = Bioderma and vi. 
T6 = Mustard oil cake@3 t/ha. The objective of this 
experiment was to evaluate the impact of organic 
manures for controlling potato common scab and 
yield of potato. Results showed that neem oil cake in 
respects of common scab incidence (%) and mustard 
oil cake in respects of scab severity performed better 
than other treatments . The maximum marketable 
fresh tuber yield was produced obtained from 
mustard oil cake@3 t/ha) . Therefore, considering 
the common scab incidence (%), scab severity 
and fresh marketable tuber yield; organic fertilizer 
namely mustard oil cake@3 t/ha followed by neem 
oil cake@3 t/ha may be applied to minimize potato 
common scab disease as well as to get good fresh 
yield in our country.

Effect of alternative inhibitors on sprout 
suppression of stored Potato in ambient condition
M. Salim and M. K. Alam
An experiment was conducted at the Tuber Crops 
Research Sub-Centre (TCRSC), Bangladesh 
Agricultural Research Institute (BARI), Munshiganj 
during the rabi season of 2024-25 with five treatments 
viz. T1 = Peppermint oil, T 2 = Eucalyptus oil, T 3 = 
Mahogany oil, T4 = Neem oil and T5 = Distilled water 
with a view to find out the superior alternative(s) 
to toxic CIPC for potato sprout control in ambient 
storage condition; and to assess the efficacy of 
botanical sprout inhibitors for extending keeping 
quality of safe organic potato in natural condition. 
The first sprouting was initiated in 9 th week at 56 
days after storage (DAS) when distilled water was 
used as inhibitors on sprout suppression of stored 
potato in ambient condition. Eucalyptus oil provided 
the best performance on sprout suppression of stored 
potato in ambient condition i.e it took 14 th week. 
The highest (2.30) number of sprouts (>3mm) was 
observed in 9th week at 56 days after storage (DAS) 
when distilled water was used as inhibitors on sprout 
suppression of stored potato in ambient condition 
where there was no sprouts were present in all other 
treatments. For the last week of data collection the 
best performance for both number sprouts (>3mm) 
and length of sprouts (cm), respectively were found 
(3.40) and (2.20 cm) when eucalyptus oil was used 
as inhibitors on sprout suppression of stored potato 
in ambient condition. Mahagony oil, peppermint oil 
and neem oil also showed promising performance 
for sprout suppression of stored potato in ambient 
condition. Therefore, considering the start of sprout, 
number of sprouts and length of sprouts eucalyptus 
oil, mahagony oil, peppermint oil and neem oil may 
be used as inhibitors on sprout suppression of stored 
potato in ambient condition in our country.

Biotechnology and seed production 
Production, distribution and in vitro maintenance 
of Potato varieties/germplasm
F. Akhter, S. Islam, M. M. H. Molla and M. M. 
Rahman
This study aimed to produce and maintain virus-
free plantlets of BARI-released potato varieties and 
germplasm through meristem and sprout culture. 
Work was carried out at the Tissue Culture Lab, 
TCRC, BARI, Gazipur. Virus-free tubers confirmed 
by ELISA were cultured in MS medium under 
aseptic conditions at 21-22°C, 75-80% humidity, 
and a 16/8-hour light cycle. Plantlets were hardened 
in sand trays and transplanted to a net house for 
further multiplication. During 2024-25, a total of 
9580 disease-free plantlets from 33 BARI potato 
varieties and 1390 germplasm plantlets were 
distributed to BSPC, Debiganj for G0 generation 
seed production. In total 63080 plantlets were 
produced from BSPC and TCRC together. Mother 
stocks were maintained by subculture for genetic 
preservation and future multiplication. This 
continuous tissue culture-based program supports 
breeder seed production, maintains varietal purity, 
and conserves valuable genetic resources for use in 
future breeding programs.
Improvement of indigenous promising Potato 
cultivars through meristem culture and their yield 
performance study with traditional cultivars
F. Akhter, S. Islam, M. M. H. Molla and M. M. 
Rahman
This experiment was conducted to develop virus-free 
plants of indigenous potato varieties, particularly 
Shilbilati, using meristem culture. Tubers of three 
indigenous cultivars-Shilbilati, Lalpakhri, and 
Sadaguti-were tested for viruses through DAS-
ELISA. Virus-infected tubers were sprouted in 
sterilized sand under greenhouse conditions. 
Meristems (0.2-0.5 mm) were excised under a 
stereomicroscope, surface-sterilized using ethanol 
and Cl2H2O and cultured on hormone-free MS 
medium at 25 ± 2°C under a 16/8-hour photoperiod. 
The meristems developed shoots within 60-65 days 
and were sub-cultured for further growth. Plantlets 
were tested for viral infection, and virus-free 
Shilbilati plantlets were multiplied for minituber 
production. Eighty virus-free plantlets produced 
750 g of minitubers in 2023-24, and replanting in 
2024-25 yielded 3.8 kg of healthy tubers. These 
virus-free lines provide a foundation for producing 
clean, disease-free seeds, enhancing yield potential, 
and preserving indigenous germplasm for future 
breeding and seed programs.
Purification of virus(s) through meristem culture 
of Sweet potato
F. Akhter, S. Islam, M. M. H. Molla and M. M. 
Rahman
This study focused on eliminating viral infections 
from two popular BARI sweet potato varieties, 
BARI Misti Alu-8 and BARI Misti Alu-16, using 
meristem culture. Virus-infected tubers were grown 
in a greenhouse to produce shoots for meristem 
isolation. Shoot tips were excised, washed with 70% 
ethanol and 1% Cl2H2O, and rinsed thoroughly in 
sterile water. Under a stereomicroscope, the outer 
leaf primordia were removed, leaving a 0.2-0.5 
mm meristem with one or two inner leaf primordia. 
These were cultured on Murashige and Skoog (MS) 
medium at 25 ± 2°C under a 16/8-hour light-dark 
photoperiod. The meristems showed growth within 
60-65 days, forming light-green plantlets that were 
sub-cultured and hardened. PCR testing confirmed 
the successful elimination of viruses. Thirty virus-
free plantlets were established, forming a healthy 
source for multiplication and field evaluation. This 
technique ensures clean planting material, protecting 
sweet potato yield and supporting sustainable seed 
production in Bangladesh.

F. Akhter, S. Islam, M. M. H. Molla and M. M.

This study aimed to determine the genetic diversity 
of 83 BARI-released potato varieties using 20

complement molecular data. Clear polymorphic 
bands were obtained for all markers, enabling

Development of Potato populations for late blight 
resistance and biofortification using molecular 
marker-assisted selection (MAS)
S. Islam, F. Akhter, M. M. H. Molla, M. Rahman, 
M.M. Begum and M. M. Rahman
At the TCRC crossing block, 20 hybridizations 
were made among resistant, local, and anthocyanin-
rich potato genotypes to develop late-blight-
resistant and nutrient-dense progenies. From these, 
552 progenies were evaluated for plant height, 
tuber yield, and morphological traits. Average plant

demonstrates that marker-assisted selection (MAS) 
can effectively combine resistance genes with 
quality traits, providing a foundation for developing 
improved varieties that enhance yield, disease 
resistance, and nutritional value in future potato 
breeding programs.
Regional yield trial of marker assisted selection 
(MAS) for late blight resistance Potato lines
S. Islam, F. Akhter, M. M. H. Molla, M. Rahman, E. 
Haque, M. Sultana M.M. Begum and M. M. Rahman 
A regional yield trial was conducted across Rangpur, 
Bogura, and Gazipur during 2024-25 to evaluate 
ten genotypes from TB10 and TB11 families for 
late blight resistance and yield. Field assessments 
measured disease severity using AUDPC and

trials. The combination of field and molecular data 
ensures reliable selection of stable, high-yielding, 
late-blight-resistant potato lines suitable for large-
scale cultivation.

Molecular diagnosis of Potato viruses in 
Bangladesh and sequencing them
S Islam, F. Akhter, M. M. H. Molla., M.M. Begum 
and M. M. Rahman
Forty potato varieties from BSPC G2 breeder 
plots at Debiganj were screened for eight major 
viruses (PVX, PVY , PLRV , PVS, PVM, PV A, 
PVH, and PAMV) using PCR. After two months 
of controlled sprouting, RNA was extracted with 
the FavorPREp Plant RNA Kit and converted to 
cDNA using ABScript II. PCR amplification with 
virus-specific primers was followed by agarose 
gel electrophoresis for virus identification. This 
approach enabled accurate detection of infected 
samples and identification of virus-free tubers for 
seed production. Preliminary results confirmed 
successful RNA and cDNA synthesis from all 
varieties. Subsequent PCR testing will verify virus-
free lines to support clean seed propagation. This 
molecular diagnostic framework improves accuracy 
over traditional methods and ensures the distribution 
of healthy planting materials. 
Molecular diagnosis and field survey of the 
distribution of the Sweet potato infecting viruses 
in Bangladesh
S. Islam, F. Akhter, M. M. H. Molla, M.A. Ahmed, 
M. M. Rahman and M. M. Rahman
Sweet potato samples showing viral symptoms 
were collected from Gazipur, Bogura, Gaibandha, 
Chandpur, Rangpur, and Sherpur to detect major 
viruses using PCR. DNA and RNA were isolated 
from fresh leaf tissues, and cDNA was synthesized 
with GoScriptTM Reverse Transcription System. 
Specific primers targeted SPFMV , SPCSV , SPVG, 
SPMMV , and TMV . Electrophoresis results showed 
clear bands confirming viral presence. SPFMV was 
the most common (16 % of samples), followed 
by SPCSV , SPVG, SPMMV , and TMV , mainly in 
Gazipur and Chandpur. Virus-free plants yielded 
15.5-32.75 t/ha, while infected ones produced 7.33-
17.57 t/ha-representing 28-67 % yield loss. The 
study provides the first comprehensive molecular 
survey of sweet potato viruses in Bangladesh and 
identifies key infection hotspots. Findings highlight 
the urgent need for integrated virus-management 
strategies and the production of virus-free planting 
materials to safeguard sweet potato productivity and 
ensure food security nationwide.

Insect pest management 
Development of bio-rational based management 
post-harvest up to storage condition against 
Potato tuber moth
M.M Khatun, M. M. H. Molla and M. M. Rahman
The entomology laboratory at TCRC, BARI, 
Gazipur, conducted a study on the bio-rational 
management of the potato tuber moth during the 
2025 Robi season using five bio-pesticides, together 
with an untreated control, at room temperature. At 
60 days after storage, the untreated control showed 
a mean infestation of 69.77%. On the other hand, 
Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. kurstaki yielded 
the lowest tuber infestation (7.02%), followed by 
neem seed kernel (7.81%) and rice husk (9.08%). 
These treatments also significantly reduced tuber 
damage compared to the control, with Btk showing 
the greatest decrease (89.94%), followed by neem 
seed kernel (88.82%) and rice husk (86.98%). All 
treatments were reduced infestation intensity of PTM 
compared to the untreated control. B. thuringiensis 
showed the lowest infestation levels across all 
parameter (2.31, 0.87 and 0.18 mean no. of tunnels, 
holes and infested eyes per tuber respectively. 
Significantly reducing larval penetration were 
B. thuringiensis and neem seed kernel (16.71% 
and 17.64%, respectively). The highest mortality 
rates were generated by B. thuringiensis (83.29%) 
and neem seed kernel (82.36%), with rice husk 
exhibiting notable mortality (80.80%). Conversely, 
the untreated control showed the highest rates of 
pupation (88.95%) and adult emergence (87.03%), 
suggesting that the larvae developed into adults 
more successfully. Therefore, considering the all 
parameters, the bio-pesticides decrease pupation and 
emergence rates, especially in Bacillus thuringiensis, 
Neem seed kernel and rice husk, which greatly 
inhibit development.

M.M Khatun, M. M. H. Molla and M. M. Rahman
Eleven (11) varieties and advanced materials of 
potato were evaluated against cutworm infestation 
during 2024-25, TCRC, BARI, Gazipur. Among

observed in the remaining germplasm. Out of all

were best performed in terms of productivity and 
performance against potato cutworm and can be 
used as breeding programs, respectively.

Socio-Economics 
Adoption and impact of BARI Potato varieties 
and zero tillage potato cultivation practice in 
saline coastal area
M. E. A. Begum, S.M.A. Shiblee, M. M. H. Molla, 
M. K. Alam, A. T. M. T. Islam and M. M. Rahman
This study aims to identify the adoption and 
impact of potato varieties and zero tillage potato 
cultivation (ZTPC) practice and determinants of 
the adoption of ZTPC practices and their impacts 
on potato farming in saline coastal area. To achieve 
the study objectives, the researchers employed 
Poisson regression, Propensity Score Matching 
techniques and the Adoption and Diffusion 
Outcome Prediction Tool (ADOPT). A total of 
120 potato farmers were surveyed in 2025. The 
results show that the average yields of BARI Alu-
72, BARI Alu-73, BARI Alu-78, and BARI Alu-79 
under zero tillage with rice straw mulch were 21.59 
t/ha, 19.41 t/ha, 26.76 t/ha and 24.13 t/ha which 
provided 218 %, 229%, 301% and 203% higher 
yields than that of conventional tillage (9.88 t/ha, 
8.46 t/ha, 8.89 t/ha and 11.85 t/ha respectively. 
The results indicated their decision regarding 
whether to adopt ZTPC practice was significantly 
influenced by training and visit to demonstration 
field. The impact on productivity with the adoption 
of the ZTPC practices investigated in this study 
was from 5995.72 kg to 6017.33 kg greater for 
adopters than non-adopters. Socioeconomic 
studies into adoption and scaling approaches are 
necessary for a proper technological transfer. For 
that, investment in training facilities is warranted 
to adopt and sustain ZTPC and increase potato 
farmers' income.

BARI Annual Report 2024-25
Adoption and profitability of BARI developed 
Potato varieties in Bangladesh
M. S. Akter, M. A. Rashid, M. M. H. Molla and M. 
M. Rahman
This study aimed to assess the adoption, input use, 
profitability, and marketing challenges associated 
with BARI developed potato varieties in Bangladesh. 
The study was conducted across three major potato 
growing districts namely Bogura and Joypurhat (in 
2024), and Cumilla (in 2025). Data were collected 
from 150 households through random sampling 
between February and June of 2024 and 2025. Field 
survey data from 2024 and 2025 reveal that BARI 
Alu-7 (Diamont) dominates in Cumilla (82%), while 
BARI Alu-25 (Asterix) is most preferred in Bogura 
(44%) and Joypurhat (62%). The overall adoption 
of BARI varieties has increased from 86% in 
2022-23 to 88.42% in 2024-25. BARI Alu-90 and 
BARI Alu-72 had low adoption, mainly due to seed 
unavailability and limited awareness. Region-wise 
Rangpur, Dinajpur, and Bogura contributed over 
60% of total potato production. Input use analysis 
highlights excessive use of urea, TSP, and gypsum 
beyond recommended levels, while labour demand 
remains high (151 man-days/ha). In 2024, BARI 
Alu-90 in Bogura-Joypurhat achieved the highest 
BCR (2.08) and yield (34.48 mt/ha). BARI Alu-54, 
Alu-29, and Alu-25 also performed well. However, 
in Cumilla (2025), BARI Alu-90's BCR dropped to 
1.15 indicating a decline in profitability compared 
to the previous year, due to higher input costs and 
lower farmgate prices. Local varieties like Pakri 
and Sakila, though grown on small scales, achieved 
higher market prices but had lower yields. Farmers 
faced multiple challenges including high seed costs 
(96%), low-quality seeds (94%), and poor market 
access, especially in terms of unstable prices and 
limited storage. The declining BCR trend highlights 
the need for better input management, stable 
pricing and enhanced extension services to sustain 
profitability.

Screening of lentil germplasm for resistance to 
stemphylium blight disease
M. S. U. Zaman, D. Sarker and M. A. Y . Akhond
Stemphylium blight (SB) is a major constraint to 
lentil production in Bangladesh. A total of 400 
lentil germplasm were evaluated during 2023-24, 
followed by 133 germplasm in 2024-25, for their 
response to SB under field conditions at the PRC, 
Ishwardi, Pabna, and the RARS, Jashore. The 
analysis of variance revealed significant effects of 
genotype on disease severity and other yield-related 
traits. The mean disease severity varied across the 
geographical origin of germplasm (Bangladesh 
versus Canada), which was reflected in the frequency 
distributions of disease reactions. The frequency 
distribution of mean disease severity scores of 
228 germplasm revealed a continuous distribution, 
suggesting the interplay of several genes with minor 
effects in SB resistance. Six accessions- 9507-4-1, 
LR26-138, LR59-121, LR26-78 and Crimson AGL 
in 2024 and seven accessions- 9527-22-1, LRIL 
21-67, FLIP-95-1L, M-2, 9522-10-1, FLIP-87-70L 
and 87512 in 2025were found resistant to SB. The 
percent disease index was negatively correlated with 
yield and its related traits.
Screening of lentil germplasm for tolerance to 
terminal heat stress
M. S. U. Zaman and M. A. Y . Akhond
Late-sown lentils face terminal heat stress during 
the reproductive stage, causing major yield losses. 
One hundred ninety-two germplasm were evaluated 
under field conditions, showing significant 
genotypic variation in stress response. Heat stress 
shortened phenology (DF, DM) by ~13-15%, 
reduced plant height by 5-14%, and decreased 
branching by 23-31%. The most severe effect was 
on filled pods (47-59% reduction), leading to yield 
losses of 58% at Rajshahi (Raj) and 68% at Ishwardi 
(ISD). Heritability was moderate to very high, while 
genotype × treatment interactions were limited. 
AMMI and GGE biplots revealed contrasting 
responses: genotype 188 had the highest yield but 
poor stability, while genotypes 22, 26, 85, and 
167 performed moderately with high stability. The 
"which-won-where" analysis identified genotype 
188 (along with 56 and 185) as superior in ISD in 
2024, whereas genotypes 27, 136, and 134 were 
best adapted to Raj. Multi-trait selection (MTSI) 
highlighted several stable, high-yielding lines, 
including 188, 56, 34, 52, 116, 106, 153, 158, 59, 
85, and 185.
Evaluation of lentil genotypes under controlled 
heat stress conditions
M. S. U. Zaman, M. Ashraful Alam and M. A. Y . 
Akhond
Heat stress significantly affected physiological and 
yield traits in lentil genotypes compared with the 
control. Total chlorophyll content declined across all 
genotypes, with M-2 retaining the highest relative 
level (78% of control), while BLX-13004-12 showed

28 I Pulse Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
the sharpest reduction (48%). Electrolyte leakage 
increased significantly under stress, indicating 
membrane injury, with BLX-13004-12 recording 
the greatest increase (126% of control) and ILL-
5068 the least (87%). Leaf relative water content 
was generally reduced, although L-4147 maintained 
near-full levels (99% of control), contrasting with 
the marked decline in BLX-13004-12 (79%). Pod 
production was drastically reduced under heat stress, 
with BLX-13004-12 retaining only 3% of its control 
level, whereas M-2 and L-4147 showed better 
tolerance, maintaining about 30%. These findings 
highlight contrasting physiological responses among 
genotypes, with M-2 and L-4147 exhibiting superior 
heat tolerance compared to BLX-13004-12.

Evaluation of grass pea genotypes as a herbage 
(leafy vegetable) compare to yield in southern 
region of Bangladesh 
M. M. Rahman, M. A. Zaman, S. Ahmaed, R. Uddin, 
M. M. R. Talikder and M. S. I. Khan
Grasspea (Lathyrussativus L.) locally known as 
"Khesari" was extensively cultivated in all over 
Bangladesh. Five advanced grass pea genotypes were 
grown along with check variety BARI Khesari-3 
during winter season of 2024-25 at Regional 
Agricultural Research Station, BARI, Rahmatpur, 
Barishal following three rows with three meter and the 
preference of grasspea consumption in the descending 
order: highly soft & succulent > medium soft & 
succulent > hardy & rough . This study focuse on the 
exploration, collection, and survey of grasspea as a 
leafy vegetable with the aim of revitalizing traditional 
knowledge for practical applications. Significant 
differences were observed in five genotypes along 
with check BARI Kheseri-3 on the basis of herbage 
yield and organoleptic test. Among the tested entries 
these genotypes BGP-13010, IGYT-122 and BARI 
kheseri-3 were highly soft &succulent; two genotypes 
BGP-13009 and IGYT-125 were medium soft & 
succulent and one genotype IGYT-123 was hardy and 
rough. The highest yield (9397.22 kg/ha) was found 
in our check variety BARI Kheseri-3 and BGP-13010 
(8238.89 kg/ha) followed by IGYT-122 (7811.11 kg/
ha). Based on organoleptic test of leaves of selected 
genotypes of grasspea was assessed for proximate 
parameters. This comprehensive study provides 
valuable insights into use and preferences associated 
with grasspea consumption in Bangladesh, paving 
the way for practical applications and the revival of 
traditional knowledge.

Field screening of grasspea genotypes against 
heat
M. A. Zaman, S. Mahmud, M. M. Rahman, A. K. M. 
Alam, and M. M. Anwar.
High temperature at the terminal stage is a major 
abiotic constraint for the reduction of grasspea 
yield and seed quality. Thus, the selection of heat-
tolerance genotypes is essential to identify either 
high yield potential or stable performance. Owning 
to select the genotypes of grasspea an experiment 
was conducted with 50 genotypes including local 
landraces, advanced breeding lines, commercial 
varieties and exotic germplasm under stress and non-
stress conditions during 2024-25 at Pulses Research 
Centre (PRC), Ishurdi, Pabna and Regional Pulses 
Research Station (RPRS), Madaripur. Experiment 
were sown under two conditions: (1) set one was 
sown at optimum sowing time on 28-29 November 
(OS) at RPRS, Madaripur, and PRC, Ishurdi, Pabna 
respectively when day/night temperatures were 
below 32/8°C at their reproductive phase and (2) 
another set was sown on 29 December (LS), (one 
month delay compare to optimum sowing time) at 
both locations. All genotypes were arranged in an 
Alpha-lattice designand repeated two times with 
unit plot was 2.5 m long× three rows, the row to row 
distance was 50. Comparison the field performance 
and yield potentiality under stress and non-stress 
condition at both locations the genotypes BD 5651, 
BD 5667, BD 5659, BD 5515,BD 5654, BD 5556, 
Patuakhali local, BGP-13009, 114509, IGYT-122, 
BD 5648, and BD 5665 were selected for further 
evaluation in the next season with more stress 
condition.
Screening of grasspea germplasm for tolerance to 
waterlogging at seedling stage
M. S. U. Zaman and M. A. Zaman
Waterlogging is a major constraint to grasspea 
(Lathyrus sativus L.) productivity. Twenty-five 
genotypes were evaluated for yield-related traits 
under control and waterlogged conditions. ANOV A 
showed significant genotypic variation for all traits 
except total chlorophyll (Tchl), with waterlogging 
causing highly significant reductions across traits. 
Genotype × treatment interactions were significant 
for grain yield, branch, pods, shoot and root biomass, 
and root length, indicating differential stress 
responses. PCA of stress tolerance indices explained 
56.7% of the variation, with shoot biomass and plant 
height strongly influencing genotype separation. 
Four contrasting genotypes were further assessed for 
physiological traits. BARI Khesari-2 and BK-2021-
002 maintained comparatively higher biomass, 
yield (2.4-3.3 g/plant), and harvest index (33-47%) 
under stress, indicating strong tolerance, whereas

32 I Pulse Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
SEL-1327 exhibited pronounced reductions in these 
traits and was identified as highly susceptible. These 
results highlight key trait associations and identify 
tolerant genotypes for breeding waterlogging-
tolerant grasspea.

of seed yield. Among the genotypes, BFPX 17002-
7 flowered and matured earlier than the other 
genotypes. The highest plant height was recorded 
in BFPX 17001-3 followed by BFPX 17005-4 and 
BFPX 17001-11 in all locations. The genotypes 
BFPX 17001-3 exhibited the highest number of pods 
per plant among the tested genotypes. The highest 
hundred seed was found in BFPX 17001-11 and 
lowest showed in the genotype BFPX 17002-7. In 
the current study, as depicted by the mean seed yield 
of 13 genotypes ranged 1277 kg/ha (BFPX 17005-
4) to 1583 kg/ha (BFPX 17002-7). The maximum 
yield was demonstrated in BFPX 17002-7 (1583 
kg/ha) followed by BFPX 17005-1 (1578 kg/ha), 
BARI Motor-4 (1575 kg/ha) and BFPX 17001-3 
(1567 kg/ha). The results reveal significant genotype 
× environment interaction. Jashore and Ishurdi 
emerged as high-potential sites for evaluating and 
selecting superior genotypes. Gazipur was the most 
challenging site, where no genotype performed 
satisfactorily, suggesting stress-prone conditions. 
Barishal offered moderate productivity, making it 
suitable for testing stability rather than maximum 
yield. As revealed by GGE biplots and average seed 
yield across locations, the genotype the genotypes 
BFPX 17003-8 (E11), BFPX 17001-3 (E12), BFPX 
17005-7 (E9), 17002-7 (E13) and BFPX 17005-
1 (E3) identified as most adapted line and stable 
performer with negligible G × E interaction and high 
yield could be used directly as variety.

Preliminary yield trial of mungbean (Set-I)
M. G. Azam, A. K. M. M. Alam, M. M. Rashid, S. 
Kobir, M. M. Rahman and M. M. Anwar
A preliminary yield trial (PYT) of twelve mungbean 
genotypes, including the checks BARI Mung-6 and

36 I Pulse Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
BARI Mung-8, was conducted during Kharif-I, 
2025 at four locations in Bangladesh (Barishal, 
Ishurdi, Jashore, and Madaripur) to find out 
desirable genotypes of mungbean using yield and 
yield-contributing traits. Significant differences 
were observed among genotypes and environments 
for days to flowering, maturity, plant height, pods 
per plant, and seed yield. Days to flowering ranged 
from 36 to 38 days on average, while maturity was 
completed within 63-66 days. Plant height varied 
widely (49-57 cm), with taller plants generally 
recorded at Ishurdi. Pods per plant ranged from 21 
to 26, and 100-seed weight varied between 3.74 g

17008-2-1 outperforming the standard checks.

most favorable environment (1317 kg ha−1), while 
Barishal was the least productive (957 kg ha−1). 
The study identified high-yielding and promising 
genotypes that may be advanced to Regional Yield 
Trials (RYT) for further evaluation and possible 
release as improved mungbean varieties adaptable 
to diverse environments in Bangladesh.
Preliminary yield trial of mungbean for export 
quality (Set-II)
M. G. Azam, A. K. M. M. Alam, M. M. Rashid, S. 
Kobir, M. M. Rahman and M. M. Anwar
The present study was conducted during Kharif-I, 
2025 at four locations in Bangladesh (RARS, 
Barishal; PRC, Ishurdi; RARS, Jashore; and 
RPRS, Madaripur) to identify desirable mungbean 
genotypes for yield and yield-contributing traits. 
Ten genotypes, including the check variety BARI 
Mung-6, were evaluated in RCBD with three 
replications. Significant variability was observed 
among genotypes across environments for 
phenological, morphological, and yield-related 
traits. Days to flowering ranged from 25 to 44, 
while maturity varied between 64 and 66 days. Plant 
height differed considerably, with BMB-2023003 
producing the tallest plants (61.17 cm). Pods per 
plant varied from 21 to 23, while 100-seed weight 
(HSW) ranged from 5.18 g (BMB-2018001) to 
5.98 g (BMB-2023001). Seed yield varied between 
978 kg ha−1 (BMB-2018001) and 1160 kg ha−1 
(VI000470 AG). Overall, VI000470 AG emerged 
as the most promising genotype, combining higher 
seed weight (5.78 g) with the highest yield (1160 
kg ha−1), while BMB-2023003 and BMB-2023001 
also showed potential by combining larger seed 
size with competitive yields. Among the genotypes, 
VI000470 AG, BMB-2023002, BMB-2023001 
and VI001339 AGconsistently outperformed the 
standard check BARI Mung-6, demonstrating 
higher yield with bold seed and broader adaptability. 
The study identified high-yielding and promising 
genotypes that may be advanced to Regional Yield 
Trials (RYT) for further evaluation and possible 
release as improved mungbean varieties adaptable 
to diverse environments in Bangladesh.

globally but its production is declining due to due 
to different biotic and abiotic constraints. Among

Yield Trial (PYT) over mungbean growing areas of 
the country in next cropping season.

Bio-fortification of chickpea through water 
soluble zinc sulfate
M. S. Alam, M. M. Kamal and M. S. Uddin
Zinc fortified chickpea maintains balance nutrition 
of pregnant women and children and contributes 
to the growth and reproduction of plants, animals, 
and humans. Therefore, a field experiment was 
conducted at PRC, BARI, Ishwardi, Pabna during 
two years rabi season of 2023-2024 and 2024-2025, 
respectively to find out the response of chickpea 
to nodulation, zinc bio fortification, seed quality 
and yield. The experiment was laid out in RCBD 
with three replications and assigned 6 different 
treatments. The treatments were T1= Native fertility, 
T2= Soil ZnSO 4 @ 2 kg ha -1, T3= Soil ZnSO 4 @ 5 
kg ha-1, T4= Foliar spray ZnSO 4 @ 0.1% at before 
flowering stage, T5= Foliar spray ZnSO 4 @ 0.2% at 
flowering stage and T6= Soil ZnSO4 @ 2 kg ha-1 and 
foliar spray ZnSO4 @ 0.2%at flowering and poding 
stage. The two years mean results revealed that all 
the treatment showed statistically identical effect on 
plant height, nodule number plant-1, pod plant-1, 
nutrient contents and seed yield of chickpea. The 
higher mean seed yield (2117 kg ha -1) was found in 
(T6) and the lower seed yield (1197 kg ha -1) were 
obtained from the control (T1). Yield increased over 
control was (43-31%). The maximum gross margin 
and BCR were found in soil application 2 kg ZnSO4 
and spray ZnSO 4 @ 0.2% solution at flower & 
poding (T6).

Effect of integrated weed management on growth 
and yield of mungbean
A. A. Begum, M. S. Alam, M. A. Rahman, M. R. 
Karim, M. Z. Ali, S. T. Zannat and M. A. K. Mian
An experiment was conducted at PRC field, 
Ishwardi, Pabna during Kharif-1season 2025 to 
find out suitable and economic weed management 
practice for mungbean. Treatments were:T1 = Two 
hand weeding (HW) at 25 and 45days after sowing 
(DAS), T2 = Bentazone 48 SL @ 1.5 L/ha at spraying 
at 2-3 leaf stage of weed, T 3 = Pendametheline 
33% EC @ 2 L/ha at 3 DAS, T 4 = Pendametheline 
33% EC @ 2 L/ha at 3 DAS + HW at 25 DAS, T 5 
= Pendametheline 33% EC @ 2 L/ha at 3 DAS + 
Quizalofop-p-ethyl 10% EC @ 0.8 L/ha at 30 DAS, 
T6 = Quizalofop-p-ethyl 10% EC @ 0.8 L/ha at 15 
DAS, T7 = Quizalofop-p-ethyl 10% EC @ 0.8 L/ha 
at 15 DAS + HW at 25 DAS, T8 = BARI wider at 25 
and 45 DAS, T 9 = Spading at 25 and 45 DAS, and 
T10 = Control (No weeding) were laid out in a RCB 
design with three replications. Among the treatments, 
Two hand weeding (HW) at 25 and 45 days after 
sowing (DAS), Pendametheline 33% EC @ 2 L/ha 
at 3 DAS + HW at 25 DAS, and Quizalofop-p-ethyl 
10% EC @ 0.8 L/ha at 15 DAS + HW at 30 DAS 
performed better. If two hands weeding at 25 and 45 
DAS gave higher yield, economic performanceand 
effective for weed control but the high production 
cost due to labor availability and wage associated 
with this method increases the overall production 
expenses. So, Pendametheline 33% EC @ 2 L/ha at 
3 DAS + HW at 25 DAS showed also the higher 
seed yield (1645 kg ha -1), weed control efficiency 
(90 %) and intensity of infestation was 1.3. Yield 
increased over control 51% in same treatment and 
also gave better economic performance representing 
higher gross return (Tk. 113200 ha -1) and gross 
margin (Tk. 50853ha -1).Therefore, Pendametheline 
33% EC @ 2 L/ha at 3 DAS + HW at 25 DAS would 
be most remunerative and effective weeding method 
for controlling weeds with higher seed yield of 
mungbean during kharif-1 at Ishwardi, Pabna (AEZ 
11). This technology can be adopted at field level.
Validation of performance of herbicides for 
controlling weeds in field pea
J. Hossain, M. M. Rashid, S. Mahmud, M. S. Alam 
and S. Ahmed
A field experiment was conducted at the Regional 
Pulses Research Station (RPRS), Madaripur during 
2024-25 to find out the performance of herbicides 
for controlling weed in field pea. Six treatments 
were viz. T 1: Panida-33EC (Pendimethaline @ 
5mlL-1 water), T 2: Weednil (Quizalofop-p-ethyle@ 
1.5 ml L -1 water), T 3: Panida-33EC and Weednil, 
T4: Panida + Hand weeding at 30 DAE,T 5: Hand 
weeding at 15 DAEand T 5: Control (No Weeding). 
Herbicides were applied at moist condition of soil 
after seed sowing. Panida + Hand weeding gave the 
maximum weed control efficiency, higher seed yield 
and the maximum gross return. Therefore, Panida + 
Hand weedingwas a better option to control weeds 
in field pea.

Crop Protection 
Identification and characterization of root rot 
pathogens of lentil
D. Sarkar, M. Z. Rahman, M. A. A. Momin, M. 
Akhterruzzaman, M. Hossain, J. Hossan and R. 
Humauan 
Root rot disease is one of the major threats to 
the production of lentil in Bangladesh. It is very 
complex to identify which soil-borne pathogens 
are associated with root rot disease on lentil and to 
determine their prevalence, a survey was conducted 
from November 2024 to March 2025 at different 
pulse-growing regions in Bangladesh. Lentil root 
rot symptoms were obtained from seven Research 
plots in various Agri-ecological Zones. Rotted roots 
were washed, potential pathogens were cultured, 
and isolates were putatively identified into the major 
pathogen groups based on morphology and cultural 
variation. The percentage of Fusarium spp during 
the survey was the most dominant (38%) compared 
to other pathogens, where Rhizoctonia, Sclerotium, 
and Oomycetes & unidentified isolates recovered 
ranged from 18%, 13%, and 31% respectively. 
From the pathogenicity test, Rhizoctonia and 
unidentified isolates were attacked early compared 
to the Fusarium and Sclerotium isolates. This survey 
provided baseline information on the prevalence 
of critical soil-borne pathogens. In the future, 
additional genetic markers will be utilized to further 
identify organisms, a species characterization will 
be conducted to assess pathogenicity and virulence, 
and lentil germplasm will be screened for resistance.
Screening of lentil germplasm for root rot and

D. Sarkar, M. Z. Rahman, M. R. Humauan, and B.

The experiment was conducted at Pulses Research 
Centre (PRC), Ishurdi, Pabna, during 2024-25. 
Forty-seven lentil advanced entries were selected 
from the previous year's trial to search for root rot 
disease resistance. Breeding resistant cultivars is 
the major approach to control the disease. This 
investigation aims to evaluate lentil cultivars against 
root rot Disease. Fifteen germplasm lines were found 
to be Resistant to lentil root rot disease and these 
genotypes could be used in future breeding programs 
to get stable and higher yields of lentil in the country.
Evaluation of biosynthesized agnps against foot 
and root rot pathogens of lentil
M. Z. Rahman, D. Sarkar, A. K. M. Sahfiqul Islam 
and A. K. M. Alam
Foot and root rot disease caused by Sclerotium 
rolfsii, Rhizoctonia solani, and Fusarium sp, 
which inflicts significant yield losses of about 
100 %. To address this, the green synthesis of 
AgNPs using Azadirachta indica (Neem), Moringa 
oleifera (Moringa) leaf extract, and silver nitrate 
(AgNO3), examined their efficacy against foot and 
root rot disease. The biosynthesized AgNPs were 
characterized through various analytical techniques. 
The results of UV-visible spectrophotometers 
revealed an absorption peak ranging from 421 to 
434 nm, validating the synthesis of AgNPs in the 
solution. In vitro assays demonstrated the significant 
inhibitory effects of AgNPs on mycelial growth of 
F . oxysporum, R. solani, and S. rolfsii particularly 
at Ag:N (10:3) and Ag:NM (10:1) concentrations. 
The findings highlight the potential of AgNPs as a 
sustainable and effective alternative for managing 
foot and root rot disease in lentil, offering a safer 
solution amidst environmental concerns associated 
with conventional fungicides.
Effect of biological agents and chemical fungicides 
for controlling foot and root rot of lentil
M. Z. Rahman, D. Sarkar, Raziuddin and A. K. M. 
M. Alam
The experiment was conducted at the Pulses 
Research Sub-center, BARI, Gazipur, and the Pulses 
Research Centre, Ishurdi, Pabna, during 2024-25 to 
identify effective fungicides and biological agents for

42 I Pulse Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
controlling foot and root rot disease of lentil. Eight 
fungicides were tested for their efficacy against the 
disease, with the susceptible variety BARI Masur-1 
used as a control treatment. The lowest foot and 
root rot (5.56 % & 7.06 %) was obtained from seed 
treatment with Provax 200 WP (Carboxin + Thiram) 
and Companion (Mancozeb + Carbendazim) @ 3 g/

was obtained from the untreated control. The highest

g/kg, respectively, and the lowest yield was obtained 
from untreated control plots (1152 & 1263 Kg/ha).
Screening of different groups of fungicides and 
bio-agents against stemphylium blight of lentil
M. Z. Rahman, D. Sarkar, Raziuddin and A. K. M. 
M. Alam 
The experiment was conducted at Pulses Research 
Sub-Center, BARI, Gazipur, and Pulses Research 
Centre, Ishurdi, Pabna during 2024-2025 to find out 
the effective and economic fungicide in controlling 
stemphylium blight of lentil. Eight fungicides were 
tested for their efficacy against the disease. The 
susceptible variety BARI Masur-1 was used, and 
Stemphylium blight disease severity was measured 
using 0 to 5 rating scale. According to the study, 
Fungicides Luna sensation, Cabritop, and Stromin 
gave good results to control disease, as well as grain 
production. Overall, every fungicidal treatment 
decreased the severity of the disease and enhanced 
seed output compared to the control, except for the 
biological control approach.

Effects of tillage and P management under 
conservation agriculture on root rot disease 
management 
D. Sarkar, Z. Rahman, A. Rahman and M. Anwar 
The root rot disease is one of the major threats to the 
production of lentil in Bangladesh. A Conservation 
Agriculture (CA) experiment was conducted 
to identify suitable tillage systems for lentil 
production, as well as for managing root rot disease. 
Soil moisture is essential for the development of 
Root Rot disease (RRD). This season's root rot 
disease was relatively lower than last year's, since 
there was no rainfall following the sowing. Among 
the tillage systems, all tillage were provided good 
results for the management of root rot disease, but 
at the later stage, Stemphylium Blight disease was 
observed, and there is a significant difference among 
the tillage practices. The highest nodules per plant 
(9) at 60 DAS was observed in NT practice whereas 
lowest was found at ST practice STB disease was 
lower at NT with RD P fertilizer (30%) and ST with 
HD P fertilizer showed highest (60%) STB Disease. 
In grain yield, HD of P fertilizer showed higher yield 
(1369 kg/ha) compare to RD and LD. In the future, 
an in-depth study will be needed to further identify 
soil microorganisms under different tillage systems.

Oilseeds 
Rapeseed-Mustard
Crop Improvement 
Rapeseed- mustard is a major oilseed crop in 
Bangladesh. It contributes a lion share to the total 
edible oil production in the country. The Oilseed 
Research Centre of BARI has already developed 21 
rapeseed and mustard varieties, which comprises 10 
Brassica rapa, 7 B. juncea, and 4 B. napus. Most of 
the developed varieties take long duration to mature 
except a few. As a result, they do not fit well in the 
existing T.aman - mustard - Boro rice cropping 
pattern. There is a limited scope of horizontal 
expansion of cultivation of rapeseed-mustard. So, 
for increasing rapeseed-mustard production, seed 
yield must be increased per unit area. Hybrid variety 
can play an important role in this regard. Now 
quality of mustard oil has been considered in variety 
development. Short duration double low varieties 
have to be developed. Therefore, high yielding 
and short duration rapeseed and mustard varieties 
should be developed to fit into the existing cropping 
pattern. The existing varieties are also susceptible 
to Alternaria leaf blight and white mold diseases, 
and aphids. Thus, to develop varieties with high 
yield potential, early maturity, disease and insect 
resistance, and wider adaptability, the following 
experiments were conducted.
Collection of rapeseed mustard germplasm
D. R. Datta and M. S. Uddin
During the 2024-25 season, two germplasm of 
Brassica juncea were collected from Vietnam 
through online. The seeds, characterized by their 
brown color and bold seeded. These collected 
germplasm will be grown for further characterization 
and preliminary evaluation in the upcoming season.
Maintenance of rapeseed mustard germplasm
M.Q.I. Matin, D. R. Datta and M. S. Uddin 
During the rabi 2024-25 season, a total of 149 
accessions were grown to maintain and utilize 
germplasm of Brassica rapa L., B. juncea L., and B. 
napus L. This included 82 accessions of B. rapa L., 
47 of B. juncea L., and 20 of B. napus L., all planted 
in a non-replicated trial at Joydebpur on November 
25, 2024. Each plot measured 3 rows by 3 meters, 
with row spacing of 30 cm and plant spacing of 5 
cm after thinning. Fertilizers were applied at rates 
of 120 kg/ha N, 80 kg/ha P, 60 kg/ha K, 40 kg/ha S, 
4 kg/ha Zn, and 1 kg/ha B using Urea, TSP, MOP, 
Gypsum, Zinc sulfate, and Boric acid, respectively. 
Half of the urea and all other fertilizers were applied 
at final land preparation, with the remaining urea 
applied at flower initiation. Intercultural operations 
were carried out as needed to ensure optimal crop 
growth. Seeds from twenty randomly selected plants 
per accession were collected and stored for future 
breeding programs. These seeds will be grown and 
further evaluated in the next season to continue 
preservation and enhancing the germplasm.

Evaluation of segregating generations of Brassica

M. S. Uddin and D.R. Datta 
During the 2024-25 season at Gazipur, segregating 
generations of Brassica rapa were evaluated to 
develop homogeneous lines. The F1 to F6 seeds were 
sown using the cross-to-row method, with families 
from the F 5 and F 6 generations sown using the 
family-to-row method, alongside BARI Sarisha-14 
as a check. The sowing took place on November 
16, 2024, in 4-row plots each 3 meters long, with a

after germination. Fertilization followed a regimen

and Boric acid, respectively. Half of the urea 
and all other fertilizers were applied at final land 
preparation, with the remainder of the urea applied 
at the flowering stage. Intercultural operations were 
carried out as needed. Selection focused on short-
duration plants (maturing in up to 85 days), erect 
and compact types with desirable agronomic traits, 
and tolerance to disease and insects. From the F 1 to 
F4 generations, desirable plants were selected based 
on earliness, seed yield, and yield attributes, with 27, 
16, 14, and 13 plants selected from the F2, F3, F4, and 
F5 generations, respectively. For the F6 generation, 5 
progenies were chosen for seed yield evaluation in 
the observational trial for the following year. 
Selection in segregating generation (F 2-F6) of 
Brassica SPP.
M. K. Alam, M. I. Riad and M. M. Kadir 
Segregation in genetics, also known as Mendel's 
first law or the Principle of Segregation, describes 
the separation of genes and their alleles during 
meiosis, leading to distinct genetic combinations 
in daughter cells. This principle also applies to 
populations exhibiting phenotypic variation, where 
the objective is to select desirable traits based 
on phenotypic performance, maturity, disease 
resistance, and physical grain quality for advancing 
generations. Seeds from the F 2 to F 6 generations of 
Brassica species were sown between November 16, 
2024, with space planting in 3-meter-long plots and 
a 30 cm row spacing. Recommended fertilizers were 
applied, and uniform crop growth was ensured. The 
number of families planted, families selected, and 
single plants selected for Brassica rapa, Brassica 
napus and Canola germplasm.

Hybridization in Brassica napus (Set-I)
M. K. Alam, M. I. Riad, M. M. Kadir and MS Uddin 
A hybridization program was conducted at RARS, 
BARI, Jamalpur during 2024-25 to develop new 
recombinant Brassica napus L. lines with early 
maturity, disease tolerance, abiotic stress resilience, 
and high yield potential. The 8×8 half diallel mating 
design resulted in 28 successful cross combinations, 
producing a total of 1203 seeds. These seeds were 
harvested for future confirmation trials. The cross 
combinations involved various parental lines, with 
days to maturity ranging from 84 to 88 days. The 
number of pollinated buds and successful buds 
varied across combinations, with the highest seed 
production observed in crosses such as Nap-20009 × 
Nap-18010 (86 seeds), Nap-15029 × Nap-15037 (72 
seeds), and Nap-16036 × Nap-21070 (66 seeds). All 
the harvested seeds have been preserved for further 
evaluation in the next season's trials.

Evaluation of F1 generation of Brassica napus
M. K. Alam, M. I. Riad and M. M. Kadir 
The F1 generation refers to the first filial generation. 
Filial generations are the nomenclature given to 
subsequent sets of offspring from controlled or 
observed reproduction. The initial generation is 
given the letter "P" for parental generation. The first 
set of offspring from these parents is the known as the 
F1 generation. The F 1 generation can be reproduced 
to create the F 2 generation, and so forth. Scientists 
use this designation to track groups of offspring as 
they observe the genetics of various generations. 
Development of homogenous line through 
conventional breeding, it is essential to advance 
the filial generations from F 1 to F 6. The present 
investigation was therefore to know the hybrid 
performance of the crosses involving 8 parents and to 
advance F1 to F2 generation. F 1 seeds were obtained 
from 28 cross combinations from Brassica napus. It 
was made during 2024-25 and included in this trial. 
The seeds were sown on the 14 November, 2024. 
Each entry was grown in a single row of 2 m long 
plot with spacing 40 cm and 10 cm between row and 
plant respectively along with their parents as check. 
Five competitive plants were randomly selected 
from each F 1 plots and parents for data collection. 
Twenty eight hybrids were confirmed and selected 
for growing as F2 in the next generation. F1 progenies 
were harvested, bulked and seeds were preserved to 
grow F 2 population in next generation.
Observation yield trial of Brassica napus
M. K. Alam, M. I. Riad and M. M. Kadir 
An observational yield trial of Brassica napus was 
conducted during rabi 2023-24 at RARS, Jamalpur,

BARI Annual Report 2024-25
Oilseed Crops I 49
involving 30 genotypes, including the check varieties 
BARI Sarisha-8 and BARI Sarisha-13. The trial 
aimed to evaluate yield and yield-contributing 
characteristics. Each plot measured 3.0 m x 2.0 m, and 
seeds were sown on 13th November 2024. Fertilizers 
were applied according to recommended doses, 
and urea was split between land preparation and 
the flowering stage. Data were collected on various 
traits, including days to flowering, days to maturity, 
plant height, inflorescence length, siliqua per plant, 
and seed yield. Significant differences were observed 
for most traits except primary branches per plant and 
siliqua per plant. Genotype Nap-22021 recorded the 
highest yield of 1979 kg/ha, outperforming the check 
varieties by 21%. Nap-22016 produced the second-
highest yield at 1971 kg/ha, with 20% and 21% higher 
yields than BARI Sarisha-8 and BARI Sarisha-13, 
respectively. Nap-22019 followed with a yield of 
1897 kg/ha, which was 16% higher than both check 
varieties. Other notable genotypes were Nap-22037 
and Nap-22026, yielding 1853 kg/ha and 1845 kg/ha, 
respectively. These genotypes matured within 80-82 
days, making them suitable for cultivation between T. 
Aman and Boro rice. The experiment was conducted 
using an RCBD design with two replications. Based 
on the results, Nap-22021, Nap-22016, Nap-22019, 
Nap-22037, and Nap-22026 showed superior 
performance in terms of yield, early maturity, and 
other agronomic traits. These genotypes, which 
matured within 82 days and produced yields close 
to 2000 kg/ha, are promising candidates for further 
evaluation in preliminary yield trials next season. 
The highest standard error and coefficient of variation 
were observed for yield and the number of primary 
siliqua per plant. These findings suggest that these 
genotypes could significantly enhance productivity in 
Brassica napus cultivation.
Preliminary yield trial of Brassica napus 
M. K. Alam, M. I. Riad, M. M. Kadir and D.R. Datta
The experiment was conducted at Regional 
Agricultural Research Station, Jamalpur during 
rabi 2024-2025 with 14 promising genotypes 
of Brassica napus including two checks BARI 
Sarisha-8 and BINA Sarisha-9. The experiment 
was laid out in RCBD design with two replications. 
The plot size was 3.0 m x 2.0 m. Seeds were sown 
on 3 December, 2024 in continuous and row 
was 30 cm apart from each. The seedlings were 
thinned after 11 days of germination 5 cm apart. 
Fertilizer were applied @ 120:80:60:40:4:1 kg/ha 
of N: P: K: S: Zn:B from Urea, TSP, MP, Gypsum, 
Zinc sulphate and Boric acid. Half of the urea 
and all other fertilizers were applied during final 
land preparation. The rest of the urea was applied 
at the initial stage of flowering. All intercultural 
operations were done timely to raise the crop 
uniformly. Data were taken on days to flowering, 
days to maturity, plant height, and primary 
branches per plant, siliqua/plant, seeds/siliqua, 
thousand seed weight and yield per plot. The 
plot yield was converted into per hectare yield. 
The genotype Nap-50021 produced the highest 
yield (1925 kg/ha) and gave 19% and 36% higher 
yield than BARI Sarisha-8 and BINA Sarisha-9, 
respectively. The second highest yield (1839 kg/
ha) was recorded in Nap-33021, which was 13% 
and 30% higher yield than BARI Sarisha-8 and 
BINA Sarisha-9 respectively. The third highest 
yield (1804 kg/ha) obtained in Nap-20021 and 
followed by Nap-19021(1741kg/ha), Nap-
19023(1735kg/ha). They took only 82-84 days for 
maturity. However, early maturity line recorded in 
Nap-19021 and required 80 days. It produced 1741 
kg/ha yield and significantly fifth position among 
the entries. Moreover, these five genotypes Nap-
50021, Nap-33021, Nap-20021, Nap-19021 and 
Nap-19023 are suitable for growing in between 
T.Aman and Boro rice and produced higher seed 
yield than check varieties and they became mature 
below 85 days. Considering yield and yield 
contributing characters, these genotypes may be 
selected for evaluation in preliminary yield trial 
in the next year. The highest standard error and 
coefficient of variation (CV) were recorded in the 
character yield (138.5) and siliqua/plant (15.02%), 
respectively.

Hybridization in Brassica napus (Canola)
M. K. Alam, M. I. Riad and M. M. Kadir 
Hybridization can contribute to the production 
of new species or the introgression of beneficial 
adaptive features between species. It has great 
potential in agricultural systems to boost the process 
of targeted crop improvement. The main aim of 
plant breeding is to produce new crop superior to 
the existing ones. The most frequently employed 
plant breeding technique is hybridization. The aim 
of hybridization is to bring together desired traits 
found in different plant lines into one plant line via 
crossing.

Crop and Soil management 
Validation of oilseed-based mixed cropping with 
boro rice across different regions of Bangladesh
M.M. Karim, M.U. Islam and M. J. Hussain
The present study evaluated the agronomic and 
economic impacts of mixed cropping mustard 
with boro rice within a four-crop rotation system 
to enhance cropping intensity, productivity, and 
resource use efficiency in rice-based farming 
systems of Bangladesh. The experiment was laid 
out in RCBD with two treatments. Treatments were: 
T1: Traditional rice-based cropping pattern (Boro-
Aus-T. Aman); T2: Mixed cropping of Boro rice with 
BARI Sharisha-14, followed by Aus and T. Aman. 
Boro rice variety (local recommended variety). 
Results showed that mixed cropping significantly 
improved land use efficiency and total system 
productivity without reducing rice yield. Mustard 
varieties exhibited satisfactory growth and yield 
performance when mixed cropped, contributing 
to additional income and enhanced soil nutrient 
status. The findings suggest that mixed cropping 
of mustard with Boro rice is an effective strategy 
for diversifying crops, intensifying land use, and 
improving the sustainability of rice-based farming 
systems in Bangladesh.

N. A. Sultana and K. Jahan
