Insect Management
Development of a management approach against 
flea beetle (Phyllotreta striolata) attacking 
mustard
M. A. Islam, A. Samiha and R. Islam
The experiment was conducted at the Oilseed 
Research Centre, BARI, Gazipur, during the rabi 
season of 2024-25 to develop effective management 
packages against flea beetles in mustard. The study 
included six treatments: T1 (White sticky trap + 
Spinetoram), T2 (White sticky trap + Bio-chamak), 
T3 (White sticky trap + Biotrin), T4 (White sticky 
trap + Spinosad), T5 (Nitro 505 EC), and T6 as the 
untreated control. Mustard seeds (BARI Sorisha-14 
and BARI Sorisha-18) were sown on November 
19, 2024, and January 10, 2024, respectively, using 
a RCBD with three replications. The unit plot size 
was 5.0 m x 4.0 m for BARI Sorisha-14 and 1.0 m 
x 1.0 m for BARI Sorisha-18, with a 1.0 m row-to-
row spacing and 30 cm between plants. Pest counts 
for flea beetles were recorded at seven-day intervals 
from five randomly selected plants and five leaves 
from each plant, and the number of beetles captured 
per sticky trap was also counted. Results revealed 
highly significant treatment effects in reducing flea 
beetle populations. T 1 and T 2 achieved the lowest 
pest densities and highest percent reduction in 
infestation (61.65% and 47.65%, respectively), with 
T1 outperforming all other treatments. In contrast, 
the untreated control (T 6) showed the highest level 
of plant infestation (68.89%), confirming high pest 
pressure in absence of intervention. Correlation 
analysis indicated average association between 
flea beetle abundance and meteorological variables 
(temperature and relative humidity), implying that 
climatic factors may be the primary drivers of pest 
dynamics in this context. The findings underscore 
the efficacy of integrated strategies particularly the 
combination of white sticky traps with reduced-risk 
insecticides like Spinetoram and Bio-chamak as 
sustainable alternatives to conventional pesticides.

Morphological variation in sesame (Sesamum 
indicum L.) induced by EMS treatment in M 1 
generation
M. H. Rashid
The application of 0.5% EMS successfully induced 
significant morphological changes in the M1 
generation of sesame. The observed mutant traits 
demonstrate the potential of mutation breeding to 
enhance genetic diversity and improve yield-related 
characteristics. Further screening and selection in 
subsequent generations are essential to identify 
stable and heritable traits for potential incorporation 
into breeding programs
Healthy sesame seeds were soaked and treated 
with 0.5% Ethyl Methane Sulfonate (EMS) for 
a specified duration under controlled laboratory 
conditions. Post-treatment, seeds were thoroughly 
washed and sown to raise the M1 generation. The 
experiment included a control group (untreated) 
for comparative observation. Quadra-fruits per 
node: Some mutants produced up to four fruits 
per node, a trait potentially beneficial for yield 
improvement. Tri-fruits per node: Another set 
of plants displayed three fruits per node, deviating 
from the normal dual-fruit pattern. Multiloculated 
fruits: Enlarged capsules with multiple locules 
were observed, which may impact seed content and 
capsule architecture. Unbranched plants: Certain 
plants lacked lateral branching, which may influence 
plant architecture and light capture. Thick stems 
with long petioles: This robust growth form may 
suggest altered hormonal responses and structural 
reinforcement.

Insect Management
Insect pollinators and their role on yield of 
sesame (Sesamum indicum)
R. Islam, A. Islam and A. Samiha
Pollinators play a vital role in maintaining 
agricultural ecosystems and enhancing crop yields. 
This study investigated the diversity and abundance 
of insect visitors to sesame and their effects on yield 
parameters at BARI, Gazipur, during the 2024-
25 cropping season. Nine plots (4.0 x 5.0 m each) 
were established in three random blocks. Before any 
floret had opened, five plants covered with white 
mosquito net bags (1 mm mesh width) to exclude 
insect visitors, allowing for self-pollination, For 
each one of the other five sesame plants were tagged 
and left open to be accessible to visitors. Another 
five plants applied hand pollination and covered with 
mosquito net bag. At the end of the flowering period, 
the open plants were also bagged, in order to avoid 
seed predators, and all sesame plants (n =15 plants) 
were left that way up to seed maturation and the set 
was assessed. Flower-visiting insects were observed 
weekly intervals. A total of 25 insects, representing 
five species from two orders and three families, were 
recorded on sesame flowers (Table 1). Hymenoptera 
were the most abundant, dominated by Apis dorsata, 
A. mellifera, and A. cerana. Among Diptera, Musca 
domestica (Muscidae) and a Syrphid species were 
common. The results confirm that sunflowers attract 
a variety of insect species, particularly honeybees, 
emphasizing the vital role of insect pollination in 
enhancing sunflower yield and overall agricultural 
productivity. The observed 20-21% increase in yield 
under open pollination emphasizes the contribution 
of natural insect visitors. Honeybees (Apis spp.) were 
particularly effective, highlighting their importance 
in sesame ecosystems.
Relative susceptibility of sesame cultivars against 
green tobacco capsid (Nesidiocoris tenuis Reuter)
M. A. Islam, A. Samiha and R. Islam
The experiment was conducted during the rabi season 
of 2024-25 at the Oilseed Research Centre (ORC), 
BARI, Gazipur, aimed to assess the susceptibility of 
four BARI-released sesame varieties (BARI Till-3, 
BARI Till-4, BARI till-5, and BARI Till-6) to green 
tobacco capsid. Sesame seeds were sown in a well 
prepared seed bed on 03 March 2025. The unit plot 
size was 4.0 m x 3.0 m with 30 cm row to row and 5 
cm plant to plant distance. Pest assessments focused 
on whitefly, leafhopper, hairy caterpillar, and green 
tobacco capsid, with weekly monitoring from March 
25 to May 25, 2025. Among the tested cultivars, 
BARI Till-5 exhibited the highest susceptibility 
to GTC (6.75 ± SE), significantly exceeding that 
of the other varieties, which grouped statistically 
as more resistant (Till-3: 3.12; Till-4: 2.38; Till-
6: 1.95). In contrast, BARI Till-5 demonstrated 
notable resistance to other pests, indicating a 
unique interaction between varietal traits and GTC. 
The Pearson correlation matrix revealed a highly 
significant negative correlation between GTC 
incidence and maximum temperature (r = -0.931, 
p < 0.01), suggesting thermal suppression of GTC 
activity. Relative humidity at 2:00 PM showed 
a moderately positive, though non-significant, 
relationship (r = 0.740), indicating potential 
humidity-facilitated pest proliferation. These 
findings underline GTC as a dominant and distinct 
pest in sesame agroecosystems, capable of inflicting 
damage independent of varietal resistance to other 
insects. BARI Till-5, while promising against general 
pests, may be unsuitable in GTC-prone regions 
unless managed through targeted IPM. The varietal 
differences and climate interactions observed here 
provide critical insights for breeding programs and 
pest forecasting models. This study reinforces the 
urgency of GTC-focused surveillance and cultivar 
screening to ensure sustainable sesame production 
under changing climatic conditions. These findings 
suggest BARI Till-5 is more susceptible, warranting 
further investigation in the next season.
Groundnut
The groundnut or peanut (Arachis hypogaea) is 
a species in the family Fabaceae. The peanut was 
probably first domesticated and cultivated in the

BARI Annual Report 2024-25
Oilseed Crops I 59
valleys of Paraguay. The domesticated peanut is 
an amphidiploid or allotetraploid, meaning that it 
has two sets of chromosomes from two different 
species, thought to be A. duranensis and A. ipaensis. 
These probably combined in the wild to form the 
tetraploid species A. monticola , which gave rise to 
the domesticated peanut. This domestication might 
have taken place in Paraguay or Bolivia, where 
the wildest strains grow today. Groundnut is the 
most important oil legume crop cultivated in the 
world. Among the oil crops grown in Bangladesh, 
groundnut stands third position both in area and 
production. Apart from its rich sources of oil content 
(48-52%), groundnut seed is a good source of 
protein (22-25%), carbohydrate (20%) and vitamin 
B and E. Being highly digestible, the children's food 
made from groundnut can help in meeting part of the 
nutritional needs. The Oilseed Research Centre of 
BARI has developed 12 groundnut varieties, which 
comprises 8 Spanish, 3 Valencia and 1 Virginia type 
of groundnut. The objective of groundnut breeding 
programme is to develop high yielding, early 
maturing, determinate type, widely adapted, disease 
and insect resistant/tolerant, dwarf varieties suitable 
for kharif season as well as suitable for the existing 
cropping pattern.

Disease management 
Evaluation of different group of commercial 
fungicides against tikka (leaf spot) and rust 
disease of groundnut (Arachis hypogaea)
K. Jahan and N. A. Sultana
Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.), is a promising 
leguminous oilseed crop, belonging to the family 
Fabaceae. The crop is susceptible to a variety of plant 
pathogens, among the fungal diseases of groundnut, 
early leaf spot (Cercospora arachidicola ), late leaf 
spot (Cercosporidium personatum, and groundnut 
rust (Puccinia arachidis) are most devastating. 
A field trial was performed to assess the effect of 
various fungicides against Tikka/leaf spot disease 
of groundnut in natural epiphytotic conditions. 
Groundnut variety, "Dhaka-1" was cultivated at 
Research field of ORC, BARI, Gazipur during 2024-
25 growing season. Nine treatments namely, Score 
(Dyfenoconazole), Nativo (Tebuconazole 50% + 
Tryfloxystrobin 25%), Folicure (Tebuconazole), 
Tilt (Propiconazole), Autostin (Carbendazem), 
Rovral (Iprodian), Amister top (Azoxytrobin + 
Difenoconazole), Navara (Azoxystrobin20% + 
Cyporoconazole 8%), Ridomil (Mancozeb 64% + 
Metalaxyl 4%) were sprayed three times according 
to disease prevailing conditions. For Tikka disease, 
Amister top (Azoxytrobin + Difenoconazole) 
showed minimum disease incidence (24.09%) 
which was 63.62% disease reduction over untreated 
control treatment. For Rust disease, Navara 
(Azoxystrobin20% + Cyporoconazole 8%) showed 
minimum disease incidence (23.25%) which was 
60.75% disease reduction over untreated control 
treatment. 
Screening of groundnut varieties/lines against 
tikka rust and other soil borne diseases
K. Jahan and N. A. Sultana
Groundnut (Arachis hypogaea L.) is a promising 
oil legume crop in Bangladesh. More than 40 
fungal diseases have been reported in groundnut. 
Among them, Tikka/leaf spot caused by Cercospora 
arachidicola and Cercosporidium personatum Berk. 
and Curt., and rust caused by Puccinia arachidis Speg. 
are serious foliar fungal diseases. An experiment 
was conducted at Oilseed Research Centre, BARI, 
Gazipur during rabi 2024-25 cropping season under 
natural epiphytotic condition to evaluate groundnut 
entries against Tikka (leaf spot) and Rust diseases. 
Disease data were recorded at 141 days of plant 
age using '0-5' scale for Tikka and "1-9" scale for 
Rust. Among the 35 tested varieties/lines, 27 entries 
showed Moderately Susceptible and 8 entries 
showed Susceptible reaction against Tikka. Percent 
disease severity for Tikka ranges between 32.22 to 
63%. The lowest disease severity 32.22% obtained 
from ICGV-95090 (T 14), followed by ICGV 0207 
(T11), ICGV 91176(T 8), ICGV 35-1 (T 13) and ISD-
94323 (T5). For Rust disease percent disease severity 
ranges between 29.85 to 59.49%. The lowest disease 
severity 29.85% obtained from ISD-502-4-3-1(T18), 
followed by ISD-2914 (T 25), ISD-94062 (T 6), ISD-
94323 (T5), and 14-403 (T24). No entry was observed 
either Resistant or Moderately Resistant against 
Cercospora leaf spot and Rust (Puccinia arachidis) 
disease of groundnut. 
Insect Management
Development of a management approach against 
major insect pests of groundnut
M. A. Islam, A. Samiha and R. Islam
The experiments were conducted during robi season 
2024-25 at ORC research field, BARI, Gazipur and 
to develop effective management approach against 
major insect pests of groundnut. The experiment 
was laid out in RCBD with three replications. 
Groundnut seeds (BARI Chinabadam-9) was sown 
on 06 January 2025 at Gazipur. The unit plot size 
was 5.0 m x 4.0 m with 1.0 m and row to row 30 cm

BARI Annual Report 2024-25
Oilseed Crops I 63
distance. The normal intercultural operations were 
done as and when necessary. The treatments were 
as follows: T 1= White sticky trap + Spinetoram 
(Delegate 11.7 SC) @ 1.0 ml/L of water, T2= White 
sticky trap + Bio-chamak (Celastras angulatas 1% 
EW) @ 2.5 ml/litre of water, T3= White sticky trap+ 
Spraying of (Chlorfenapyr + Emamectin benzoate) 
(Benapore 12 SC) @ 1ml/L of water, T 4= White 
sticky trap+ Spraying of Spinosad (Success2.5 SC) 
@ 1.2 ml/ L of water, T5= Spraying of (Chlorpyrifos 
+ Cypermethrin) Nitro 505 EC @ 1ml/L of water, 
T6= Untreated control. Results demonstrated 
that T 1, comprising white sticky traps combined 
with Spinetoram (Delegate 11.7 SC) at 1.0 ml/L, 
significantly suppressed all major pest populations. 
T1 recorded the lowest infestations of whitefly (0.92 
± 0.10/leaf), jassid (1.28 ± 0.12/leaf), and thrips 
(1.15 ± 0.18/twig), as well as the lowest counts 
of leaf roller (1.33 ± 0.16/10 plants) and hairy 
caterpillar (0.88 ± 0.09/10 plants). Correspondingly, 
T1 also yielded the highest productivity (2.18 ± 0.15 
t/ha), surpassing the control (1.46 t/ha). Economic 
analysis confirmed the cost-effectiveness of T 1, 
which yielded the highest net return (Tk 118,000/ha) 
and the most favorable marginal benefit-cost ratio 
(MBCR = 2.40), outperforming all other treatments. 
The study concludes that integrating physical 
trapping with a selective insecticide like Spinetoram 
offers a robust and economically viable solution for 
managing key insect pests in groundnut cultivation.
Screening of groundnut entries against major 
insect pests under natural field condition
A. Samiha, R. Islam and M. A. Islam
Seventeen groundnut entries were evaluated for 
resistance to major insect pests during the 2024-
25 season at the Oilseed Research Centre (ORC), 
BARI, Gazipur. The study included 18 entries, with 
BARI Chinabadam-8 as the check variety. Seeds 
were sown on December 29, 2024, in a RCBD 
with three replications, and no insecticides were 
applied. Visual assessments of foliage damage from 
jassids, thrips, leaf roller and hairy caterpillar were 
conducted on five randomly selected plants from 
each entry every seven days across various growth 
stages. The lowest no. of jassid population was 
recorded in ICGV-0207 (1.7%), similar to ISD 3814 
(2.3%) and ICGV-0704 (2.7%). Additionally, the 
lowest no. of thrips population was in ICGV-0704 
(1.7%). The lowest infestation by leaf roller was 
found in ISD 3814 (7.67%), similar to ICGV-0207 
(9.67%). ICGV-0704 (8.33%) exhibited the lowest 
hairy caterpillar infestation (12.7%), comparable 
to ICGV-0207 (9.67%). Overall, the entries ICGV-
0207, ICGV-0704 and ISD-3814 exhibited lower 
pest infestations and better performance, making 
them suitable candidates for further breeding 
programs aimed at developing insect-resistant 
groundnut varieties.
Soybean
Soybean (Glycine max), native to East Asia, is a 
legume primarily cultivated for its edible beans, 
classified as an oilseed by the UN Food and 
Agricultural Organization (FAO). It belongs to the 
genus Glycine, which includes the subgenus Soja 
(containing both the cultivated soybean and its wild 
ancestor, Glycine soja) and the subgenus Glycine, 
which comprises wild perennials. Soybean is a key 
global crop, ranking fourth in production volume and 
leading among oilseeds. Its seeds are rich in protein 
(42-45%) and edible oil (20-22%). In Bangladesh, 
soybean is gaining popularity, particularly for its 
oil, which is increasingly used for cooking, though 
traditional methods of oil extraction are still being 
developed. The crop's seeds are also utilized in 
the feed industry and for producing various food 
items such as soy milk, soy cakes, and soy biscuits. 
The introduction of soybean to Bangladesh's sub-
tropical climate presents challenges like seed 
longevity issues, altered growth rates due to changes 
in photoperiod, and various biotic and abiotic 
stresses. To address these, experiments are being 
conducted to develop high-yielding varieties that are 
resistant or tolerant to yellow mosaic virus (YMV) 
and possess other desirable traits.

Hybrid development, F1 confirmation, and 
evaluation of F1 performance in soybean
U. Kulsum and Hosna Kohinoor
Eleven parental lines, namely Bangladesh 
Soybean-4, BARI Soybean-6, BARI Soybean-7, 
Richmond, Australia-1, MTD-453, BR-33, BS-
33, BINA Soybean-2, BU Soybean-2, and BU 
Soybean-4, were used as parents for hybridization. 
Hybridization was conducted at the ORC net house 
during kharif 2024. Data were recorded on the 
number of soybean buds pollinated, pod set, seeds 
produced, and pod set percentage. Immature flowers 
were emasculated in the afternoon before anther 
dehiscence, and pollination was done the following 
morning to improve seed set.
F1 seeds from each cross were sown on 24 January 
2025 in single 4-meter rows alongside parents. Data 
collected included final plant stand, pods per plant, 
and seed yield per plant. Five plants from each 
parent line were also selected for data comparison.
A total of 557 buds from 35 crosses were crossed, 
resulting in 121 pods and 224 seeds. Approximately 
22.3% of single crosses succeeded in producing 
pods. 
All F1 seeds were planted in rows with their parents 
and evaluated for pods per plant and yield (Table 3). 
Hybridity was confirmed using flower and seed coat 
color, where purple flowers and cream seed coats 
indicated dominant hybrid traits. Seventy-eight

harvested separately. Selected plants exhibited pod 
numbers ranging from 7 to 105 and seed yield per 
plant up to 23.8 g. Seeds from these plants were

season.

Evaluation of waterlogging tolerance in soybean 
germplasm at vegetative stage
U. Kulsum, H. Kohinoor and S. H. Habib
Thirty-two soybean genotypes, including BARI-
released varieties, were evaluated under two 
treatments: waterlogged (WL) and control (C), 
in a pot experiment conducted during the rabi 
season of 2024-2025 at Gazipur. Waterlogging 
stress was imposed at 20 days after sowing (DAS) 
and maintained for 21 days by keeping the water 
level consistently 2.0 inches above the soil surface. 
Following the stress period, the pots were drained, 
and the plants were kept for a 7-day recovery period 
under normal conditions. Data were recorded on 
the number of plants before and after stress, post-
recovery survival, number of leaves, shoot and

66 I Oilseed Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
root length, and fresh weight of shoots and roots. 
Mortality percentage was calculated as the proportion 
of plants that died during the waterlogging period, 
while recovery percentage reflected the proportion 
of plants that survived and resumed growth during 
the recovery phase.
Based on mortality and recovery percentages, 
genotypes were classified into three tolerance 
categories: Tolerant (mortality ≤ 20% and recovery 
≥ 70%), Sensitive (mortality ≥ 70% and recovery 
≤ 20%), and Moderately Tolerant (those falling 
between these thresholds). To analyze clustering 
patterns based on these predefined tolerance levels, 
supervised classification was performed using 
Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA). Prior to 
analysis, all quantitative traits (mortality, recovery, 
shoot and root traits) were standardized. LDA was 
used to reduce dimensionality and maximize group 
separation, allowing clear visualization of genotype 
clustering according to waterlogging tolerance. All 
data analysis and visualization were performed 
using R software.
Waterlogging stress at the vegetative stage resulted 
in considerable variation among the 32 soybean 
genotypes in terms of mortality and recovery 
percentages. Genotypes such as GMOT-95, BD-
2341, and BD-2348 exhibited low mortality (≤ 
20%) and high recovery (≥ 70%), which indicates 
high waterlogging tolerance. These genotypes were 
also clustered together under the Tolerant group 
in the LDA classification (Figure 2). In contrast, 
genotypes like USDA-92, USDA-40, BD-2332, and 
LG-92P-1176-1 showed high mortality rates (above 
70%) with poor recovery, aligning with the Sensitive 
cluster in the LDA. Rest of the genotypes like Shohag, 
BARI Soybean-5, and MTD-453, demonstrated 
moderate stress effects and post-flood recovery, and 
were categorized as Moderately Tolerant.
Waterlogging stress caused a significant reduction 
in morphological traits across genotypes, including 
leaf number, shoot length and shoot fresh weight. All 
the untreated plants had more number of leaves than 
the treated plants. The average shoot length under 
control was 30.1 cm, which decreased significantly 
under waterlogged conditions to 20.7 cm. Similarly, 
shoot fresh weight dropped from 2.3 g in the control 
to 1.2 g under waterlogging that indicates substantial 
growth inhibition. The reduction is likely due to 
hypoxia in the root zone that reduces nutrient uptake 
and impairs physiological processes. These findings 
are consistent with previous studies that reported 
similar effects of waterlogging on soybean growth.
Root traits also displayed significant genotypic 
variation under waterlogging. Interestingly, a slight 
increase was observed in average root length (from 
10.8 cm to 10.9 cm) and root fresh weight (from 1.4 
g to 1.6 g) under stress. Genotypes in the tolerant 
and moderately tolerant groups exhibited better root 
development. This may be due to the formation of 
adventitious roots, which are commonly induced 
under waterlogged conditions and typically emerge 
from the basal stem region in the upper soil layers. 
These roots improve access to atmospheric oxygen, 
aiding plant survival in anaerobic conditions. 
Nguyen et al. (2015) also reported similar increases 
in root traits under flooding stress. 
Study of genetic diversity of soybean (Glycine 
max (L.) MERR.) genotypes using SSR markers 
U. Kulsum, P. Roy, A. Samiha and S. H. Habib
Total forty-five genotypes collected from different 
countries and currently maintained in BARI were 
used as study materials. Total genomic DNA from 
fresh and young leaves was isolated and purified 
following ORC Molecular Biology Lab standardized 
CTAB protocol. The concentration and quality of 
the DNA samples was estimated using NanoDrop 
2000TM spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher 
Scientific, USA) by determination of A260/A280 
absorbance ratio. Finally, a portion of DNA was 
diluted in molecular grade water to a concentration 
of 50 ng/μl and stored at −20 °C. 
Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplification was 
conducted using the standardized protocol. The 
amplified PCR products were then separated by 
electrophoresis on 2% (w/v) agarose gel, stained 
with SYBR safe (1 mg/mL) and photographed 
under UV light using BioRade software. The size 
of the amplified products was determined using 
50 and 100 bp DNA ladder as size standard. SSR 
markers developed by Cregan et al.1999 were used 
in the present study. A total of 35 SSR markers 
representing all the 20 linkage groups of soybean 
were chosen for genotyping from SSR database 
(http://www.soybase.org).

BARI Annual Report 2024-25
Oilseed Crops I 67
Data from the SSR primers were analyzed to obtain 
the information on genetic diversity of the soybean 
entries. The summary statistics including the number 
of alleles per locus, major allele frequency, gene 
diversity, Polymorphism Information Content (PIC), 
genetic distance-based clustering were calculated 
with the unweighted pair group method arithmetic 
average (UPGMA) using Power Marker v 3.25 (Liu 
and Muse, 2005) and a UPMA dendrogram was 
constructed based on the dissimilarity matrix from 
MEGA 11.0 software.
Molecular characterization of germplasm reveals 
underlying allelic diversity and genetic base within 
soybean germplasm collection in BARI. The 45 
promising soybean genotypes were profiled with 
35 crop specific SSR markers. Among the 35 SSR 
primer pairs, 22 primer pairs produced scorable 
bands and were found to be polymorphic. A total 
of 87 alleles were detected from these 22 primer 
pairs of which, 81 alleles were polymorphic with an 
average of 3.68 alleles per primer pair. 
The number of alleles generated from each primer 
pair ranged from 2 (seven primer pairs) to 10 
(Satt460). The highest major allelic frequency 
of 0.96 was observed using marker Satt336 and 
lowest frequency of 0.27 was detected using 
Satt600. Genetic diversity ranged from 0.08 for 
marker Satt336 to 0.83 for marker Satt600 and 
Satt460 with a mean value of 0.52. The highest PIC 
value (0.81) was observed in Satt600 and Satt460 
and lowest value (0.08) was recorded for the primer 
Satt336 with average of 0.47. The H values for the 
markers ranged from 0.0 to 1.0 with an average of 
0.16. 
The UPGMA based dendrogram grouped the 49 
genotypes of soybean into two major clusters 
viz., I and II comprising of 26 and 19 genotypes 
respectively. Cluster I is further divided into two 
sub-groups Ia and Ib with 14 and 12 genotypes, 
respectively. The cluster II with 19 genotypes is 
also divided into another two sub-groups IIa and IIb 
comprising of 4 and 15 genotypes, respectively. This 
indicated that dissimilar accessions are grouped into 
distantly related clusters. This dissimilar grouping or 
distant clusters is so important because it helps the 
breeders to select the accession(s) with important 
dissimilar traits from the studied accessions for 
hybridization to get the higher heterotic responses.

Effect of two different plant growth regulators on 
grain filling of sunflower
M.U. Islam, S. H. Habib, and M. M. KARIM and 
M. J. Hussain
A field experiment was carried out at the research 
field of the Oilseed Research Centre, Bangladesh 
Agricultural Research Institute, Gazipur during the 
Rabi season of 2024-2025 to investigate the effect 
of foliar application of plant growth regulators 
(PGRs) on grain filling and yield of sunflower. The 
experiment was conducted followed by factorial 
in Randomized Complete Block Design with three 
replications. Factor A included three crop growth 
stages: vegetative (S1), anthesis (S2), and vegetative 
plus anthesis (S 3), while Factor B comprised four 
hormone treatments: H 0 (control), H 1 (BA 150 
mg/L), H 2 (GA 150 mg/L), and H 3 (BA+GA 150 
mg/L). Seeds of BARI Surjomukhi-3 were sown 
on 25 November 2024. Results showed that foliar 
application of BA at anthesis stage (S2H1) produced 
the highest matured seed (91.22%) and maximum 
seed yield (2.12 t/ha), followed by GA at vegetative 
and anthesis stage (S 3H2). All PGR treatments 
enhanced the percentage of mature seeds compared 
to the control. The findings suggest that appropriate 
timing and concentration of PGRs, especially BA 
at anthesis, can significantly improve grain filling 
and yield in sunflower. Further multi-year trials are 
needed for final recommendation.

Intercropping red amaranth and spinach with 
sunflower at different row arrangement 
M. M. Karim, M.U. Islam, P. Roy and M. J. Hussain
A field experiment was conducted at the Oilseed 
Research Centre, BARI, Gazipur during the 
rabi season of 2024-25 to evaluate the optimal 
row arrangement of red amaranth and spinach 
intercropped with sunflower for enhanced 
productivity and economic return. The study 
comprised nine treatments: sole sunflower (T 1), 
various combinations of red amaranth (T 2-T4) and 
spinach (T5-T7) intercropped with sunflower, and sole 
red amaranth (T8) and spinach (T9). The experiment 
was laid out in RCBD with three replications. 
Although intercropping slightly reduced sunflower 
yield, overall productivity increased due to the 
additional yield of companion crops. The highest 
sunflower equivalent yield (SEY) was recorded in T9 
(sole spinach, 2.36 t/ha), followed by T5 (one row of 
spinach with sunflower, 2.30 t/ha), while the lowest 
SEY was observed in sole sunflower (T1, 1.64 t/ha). 
The highest benefit-cost ratio (BCR) of 1.28 was 
obtained in T 5, attributed to its higher SEY , gross 
return, and gross margin (Tk. 23,000/ha). These 
results suggest that intercropping one row of spinach 
with sunflower is a productive and economically 
viable practice.
Effect of foliar application of boron on seed 
setting and yield of sunflower 
M.U. Islam, M. M. KARIM and M. J. Hussain
A field experiment was conducted during the 
rabi season of 2024-2025 at the research field of 
the Oilseed Research Centre, BARI, Gazipur to 
evaluate the effect of foliar application of boron 
(B) on seed setting and yield of sunflower. The 
experiment followed a factorial arrangement in 
RCBD with three replications. Treatments included 
three crop growth stages: S 1 - vegetative stage, S 2 
- anthesis stage, and S 3 - flowering and anthesis 
stage, combined with five boron concentrations: B0 
- control (distilled water), B 1 - 50 mg/L, B 2 - 100 
mg/L, B3 - 150 mg/L, and B 4 - 200 mg/L. Seeds 
of BARI Sunflower-3 were sown on 25 November 
2024. The results showed that foliar application 
of 150 mg/L boron, particularly when applied 
during both the vegetative and anthesis stages, 
significantly increased the number of mature seeds 
per head, 1000-seed weight, and seed yield of 
sunflower. A consistent trend of increased mature 
seed percentage and decreased immature seeds 
was observed with increasing boron concentration. 
These findings suggest that proper timing and 
dosage of boron application play a critical role 
in improving reproductive success and yield in 
sunflower. Based on the consistent outcomes over 
two seasons, foliar application of boron at 150 
mg L−1 during both the vegetative and anthesis 
stages is recommended as an effective agronomic 
practice to enhance sunflower yield under similar 
environmental conditions.

Disease Management 
Effect of sowing date on the Alternaria blight 
diseases severity and yield contributing 
characters of sunflower
K. Jahan and N. A. Sultana
A field experiment was carried out during winter 
season, 2024-25 at Oilseed Research Centre, BARI, 
Gazipur to find out Alternaria leaf blight incidence 
and severity in sunflower varieties sown at early, 
mid and late sowing dates in November, December 
and January. Alternaria leaf blight caused by 
Alternaria helianthi is considered as most dangerous 
that reduce productivity. A survey has revealed that 
losses due to this in seed yield ranging from 27-
80%, oil yield from 17-33%. The experiment was 
conducted in randomized block design with three 
replications. Two varieties BARI Sunflower-3 and 
Hysun-33 and nine sowing dates were used in this 
field trial. Disease severity, under natural conditions 
in the field, was evaluated at four growth stages 
of the crop, with reference to "0-5" scale of this 
disease. Marked plants were harvested individually 
according to their maturity for evaluation of 
yield and yield contributing characters. The 
results showed significant effects of sowing dates 
and varieties on yield and yield components of 
sunflower. BARI Sunflower-3 always showed higher 
disease severity e.g. 41.8% at vegetative stage at 30 
January compared to Hysun-33 where severity was 
21.8%. Lowest percent diseased leaf area (10%) 
was observed in December sowings, whereas higher 
percent diseased leaf area (40-45%) in late January 
sowings. November sowings also show moderately 
high percentage of leaf area covered by the disease 
(30-35%). Hysun-33 gave the highest seed yield at 
10 November followed by 20 November with 272 
gm and 230.33gm/5plants seed weight, respectively. 
Whereas, BARI Sunflower-3 showed higher seed 
yield (151.33 gm/5plants seed) at 20 November. The 
higher plant height, stem diameter, head diameter, 
500-seed weight and no. of mature seed/head were 
also observed in mid-November to early-December 
sowings. Delayed sowing also shortened the 
crop duration of sunflower in the field. For BARI 
Sunflower-3 and Hysun-33, crop duration reduces 
by about 34 and 26 days when sowing is delayed 
from early November to late January, respectively. 
The study recommended mid-November to early-
December as optimal sunflower planting dates For 
BARI Sunflower-3 and Hysun-33.
Evaluation of some fungicides against leaf blight 
of sunflower
N. A. Sultana and K. Jahan 
A field experiment was conducted at the Oilseed 
Research Centre (ORC), Gazipur, during the 2024-
2025 cropping season to evaluate the efficacy of 
seven fungicides namely, T 1 = Rural (2g/L), T 2 = 
Amistar Top (1 ml/L), T 3 =Folicure (1ml/L), T 4 
=Mancer(2g/L), T5 =Tilt(1ml/L), T6 = Mancozeb (2 
g/L), T7=Score(1ml/L and T8 = Control In managing 
Alternaria leaf blight of sunflower (Helianthus annuus 
L.) and their impact on yield and yield-contributing 
traits. The study followed a Randomized Complete 
Block Design with eight treatments, including 
a control. Fungicides were applied at disease 
onset and repeated at 10-day intervals. Results 
revealed that Rovral (0.2%) was the most effective, 
significantly reducing disease incidence by 65.49% 
over the control and achieving the highest seed yield 
(1722.3 kg/ha), representing a 34% yield increase. 
Amistar Top (0.1%), was the second highest, 
significantly reducing disease incidence by 58.89% 
over the control and achieving the seed yield (1673 
kg/ha), representing a 32% yield increase. Score 
(0.1%), and Folicure (0.1%) also provided moderate 
disease control and yield enhancement. In contrast, 
Mancer, Tilt, and Mancozeb were less effective. 
The untreated control exhibited the highest disease 
severity and the lowest yield. These findings suggest 
that Rovral, followed by Amistar Top and score, can 
be effectively integrated into disease management 
strategies to control Alternaria blight and improve 
sunflower productivity. Considering the benefit cost

72 I Oilseed Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
ratio, the fungicide Amistar Top (0.1%), was found 
to be highly economic (BCR 3.8).
Insect Management
Development of IPM package against the major 
insect pests of sunflower
M. A. Islam, A. Samiha and R. Islam
The experiment was conducted during Robi season 
2025 at ORC research field, BARI, Gazipur to 
develop an effective management approach against 
major insect pests of sunflower. The experiment was 
laid out in RCBD with three dispersed replications. 
Sunflower seeds (BARI Surjamukhi-3) were sown 
on 29 December 2024 at Gazipur. The unit plot size 
was 4.5 m x 4.0 m, with 30 cm row-to-row distance 
and 1 m plot-to-plot distance. Normal intercultural 
operations were performed as needed. The treatments 
were as follows: T1 (IPM Package-1) = Hand 
picking of larvae + Sex pheromone mass trapping of 
Spodoptera litura + Application of Spinosad (Success 
2.5 SC) @ 1.2 ml/litre of water; T2 (IPM Package-2) 
= Hand picking of larvae + Sex pheromone mass 
trapping of Spodoptera litura + Application of 
Bioclean (D-limonene 5% SL) @ 1 ml/litre of water; 
T3 (IPM Package-3) = Hand picking of larvae + Sex 
pheromone mass trapping of Spodoptera litura + 
Application of SNPV @ 2 g/10 litre of water; T4 
(IPM Package-4) = Hand picking of larvae + Sex 
pheromone mass trapping of Spodoptera litura + 
Bio-chamak (Celastras angulatus 1% EW) @ 2.5 ml/
litre of water; T5 = Farmers' practice (Application 
of Nitro 505 EC [Chlorpyriphos + Cypermethrin]) 
@ 1 ml/litre of water; T6 = Untreated control.The 
study monitored the population dynamics of major 
pests, including whitefly (Bemisia tabaci), aphid 
(Aphis gossypii), jassid (Amrasca biguttula), thrips, 
hairy caterpillars, and Spodoptera litura, along with 
their effects on yield. Statistical analysis showed 
that IPM Package T4 (hand-picking + pheromone 
trapping + Bio-chamak) significantly lowered 
pest populations across all species, leading to the 
highest yield (1.78 t/ha), followed by T1 and T5. 
T4 also exhibited the highest net return (Tk 86,400) 
and marginal benefit-cost ratio (MBCR) of 2.89, 
indicating strong economic feasibility. Conversely, 
T2 and T3 displayed lower pest control and returns, 
falling below the profitability threshold. The 
findings demonstrate that a comprehensive IPM 
approach, especially the combination used in T4, can 
effectively reduce pest incidence while increasing 
yield and farm profitability.

Screening of diverse genotypes of oilseed crops 
using SSR primers: molecular characterization 
of Brassica genotype(s) for low erucic acid and

S. H. Habib, P. Roy and U. Kulsum
Rapeseed (Brassica spp.) is the most important 
source of edible oil in Bangladesh, contributing a

BARI Annual Report 2024-25
Oilseed Crops I 73
significant percentage to the country's domestic 
oil production. However, the varieties developed 
by the Oilseed Research Centre (ORC), BARI,

Study of genetic diversity of soybean (Glycine 
max (L.) Merr.) genotypes using SSR markers
U. Kulsum, P. Roy, A. Samiha and S. H. Habib
Soybean is a vital oilseed crop. Evaluation of 
genetic diversity and associations among breeding 
materials using molecular markers holds significant 
implications for improving crop plants. A total 
of 35 SSR markers were developed to study the 
genetic divergence among 45 soybean genotypes. 
Among them, 22 primer pairs were found to be 
polymorphic producing a total of 81 polymorphic 
alleles; and the allele number for each locus ranged 
from two to ten with an average of 3.68 alleles per 
primer pair. Polymorphic information content (PIC) 
values of SSRs ranged from 0.08 to 0.81 with an 
average of 0.47. The dendrogram constructed based 
on dissimilarity indices clustered the 45 genotypes 
into two major groups and four sub-groups. These 
22 polymorphic markers could be used for further 
diversity analysis of soybean.
Biochemical and molecular variability analysis 
for high oleic acid contents in sunflower mutants
S. H. Habib, P. Roy, R. Islam and U. Kulsum
High-oleic sunflower, is valued for the oxidative 
stability and health benefits. In this study, a number 
of EMS induced sunflower mutants were evaluated 
using both biochemical and molecular approaches 
to identify lines with elevated oleic acid expression 
and increased seed oil percentage. A set of insertion-
deletion (InDel) primers targeting F AD2-1, SAD, and 
high-oleic-associated genes were used to identify 
gene expression in the sunflower mutants. Most 
mutants showed higher oil content than the control 
(40.09%), except MFA9 (27.63%) and highest was in 
MFA2 (51.55%). Mutants with elevated oil content 
and higher expression of key genes (F AD2-1, SAD, 
high oleic ) are promising candidates for breeding 
sunflower varieties with improved oil content and 
fatty acid composition.
Genetic analysis of honeybee, apis mellifera 
populations using rapd markers
R. Islam, A. Samiha, S.H. Habib and M. A. Islam
Honey bees (Apis mellifera) are essential pollinators 
that contribute significantly to global food 
production, with over one-third of crops depending 
on insect-mediated pollination. This study aimed 
to investigate the genetic diversity of western 
honeybee (Apis mellifera ) populations using the 
Randomly Amplified Polymorphic DNA (RAPD) 
marker technique. Specimens of Apis mellifera were 
collected from four geographically distinct districts 
in Bangladesh: Gazipur, Munshiganj, Satkhira, and 
Brahmanbaria and preserved in plastic containers 
filled with 70% ethanol, appropriately labeled with 
sample number, collection site, and date at 4 °C. 
After DNA extraction from the thorasic tissue of 
thec specimens, Random Amplified Polymorphic 
DNA (RAPD) analysis was performed using 
12 oligonucleotide primers. PCR products were 
analyzed using agarose gel electrophoresis in a 1.6% 
gel prepared with 1x TAE buffer and gel images were 
captured and archived using a gel documentation 
system. RAPD primers amplified 100 bands. The 
percentage of polymorphic loci ranged between 
0 and 37.5%. Total 15 polymorphic segments of 
DNA were recorded from all honeybee. Genomic 
differences were found in the similar species from 
various areas in terms of polymorphic band with 
varying molecular weight and size with same primer.
Cropping Pattern 
Development of Mustard - Sesame - T. Aman 
cropping pattern against farmers pattern for 
increasing cropping intensity and productivity 
M.M. Karim, M.U. islam, P. Roy and M. J. Hussain
A field experiments were conducted at the Oilseed 
Research Centre, BARI, Joydebpur during 2023-
2024 season to evaluate an improved cropping 
pattern aimed at increasing cropping intensity and

74 I Oilseed Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
productivity in rice-based cropping systems. The 
experiment followed RCBD with four replications. 
The tested cropping pattern was Mustard (BARI 
Sarisha-18) - Sesame (BARI Til-5) - T. aman rice 
(BRRI dhan75). The seed yields of mustard, sesame, 
and T. aman rice were 1.33 t/ha, 0.9 t/ha, and 3.48 
t/ha, respectively. The rice equivalent yield (REY) 
of the cropping pattern was 9.51 t/ha with a gross 
return of Tk. 285,300 per hectare. The benefit-cost 
ratio (BCR) of the improved cropping pattern was 
1.73, indicating higher profitability than the existing 
farmers' cropping pattern. With a benefit-cost ratio 
of 1.73, this pattern offers a profitable alternative 
to traditional rice-based systems, maintaining soil 
health and increasing overall cropping intensity.
Development of four crop based cropping pattern 
for increasing cropping intensity and productivity
M.M. Karim, M.U. Islam and M. J. Hussain
Field experiments were conducted at the Oilseed 
Research Centre of BARI during 2023-24 to evaluate 
the agronomic performance and economic returns of 
four crop-based cropping patterns compared to the 
existing rice-based system. The study was laid out in 
RCBD with four replications. The cropping patterns 
included: CP1 = Mustard-Indian Spinach + Onion-T. 
Aman; CP2 = Groundnut + Onion-T. Aus-T. Aman; 
CP3 = Groundnut + Lentil-T. Aus-T. Aman; CP 4 = 
Sunflower + Garden Pea-T. Aus-T. Aman; and CP5 
(control) = Fallow-Boro-Fallow-T. Aman. Among 
the patterns, CP1 recorded the highest rice equivalent 
yield (REY) of 29.94 t/ha, while CP 3 achieved the 
highest benefit-cost ratio (BCR) of 4.07. All four 
cropping patterns outperformed the control (CP5) in 
terms of productivity and profitability, indicating the 
potential of diverse, short-duration crop integrations 
to enhance system intensification, farm income, 
and food and nutritional security. These intensified 
systems not only improve farm profitability but 
also generate increased employment opportunities 
for both male and female laborers. Additionally, 
the diversified production contributes to improved 
household food and nutritional security, supporting 
the broader goals of sustainable and resilient 
agricultural development.

S. Brahma, M. N. Yousuf, M. M. Akand, M. M.

A field study was conducted to characterize 
morphologically and evaluate perennial chilli 
genotypes for potential use in breeding programs. 
Fourteen chilli genotypes collected from different 
regions of Bangladesh were evaluated using 
qualitative descriptors under a randomized complete 
block design at the Regional Spices Research 
Center, BARI, Gazipur during 2024-2025. The 
study revealed considerable morphological 
variation. Certain traits such as perennial life cycle, 
intermediate growth habit, flattened stem shape, 
entire leaf margin, and green anthers with white 
filaments were consistent across all genotypes. High 
frequencies were observed for dense branching, ovate 
leaf shape, white corolla color, and intermediate 
flower position, green fruit color at intermediate 
stage, elongate fruit shape, and pointed blossom-
end fruit shape. The findings suggest significant

Spices Crops I 79
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
genetic diversity among the genotypes, which may 
be utilized in developing improved chilli varieties.
Development of inbred lines of chilli (advancing 
of generation S5 to S6)
M. A. Alam, M. M. Haque, M. M. Hasan, A. H. F. 
Fahim and M. Z. H. Prodhan
The present study was conducted to advance S 5 
generation progenies to S6 with the aim of developing 
superior homozygous inbred lines of chilli (Capsicum 
annuum L.). The experiment was carried out at 
Spices Research Centre, BARI, Shibganj, Bogura 
during 2024-2025, using segregating progenies 
derived from hybridizations between OC-20 and 
BARI Morich-2, and OC-20 and BARI Morich-3, 
along with their parents. A total of thirteen progenies 
were evaluated for yield and yield-contributing 
traits. Several progenies exhibited superior 
performance compared to both parental checks. 
Notably, lines such as (ON-20XBM-3)1-2-1-9-10-7, 
(ON-20XBM-3)1-1-2-8-3-8, and (ON-
20XBM-2)3-1-2-6-2-7 produced significantly 
higher fruit yield per plant (13.23 g, 11.38 g, and 
10.75 g respectively) compared to the parental 
checks BM-2 (2.91 g) and BM-3 (5.07 g). These 
promising lines will be further advanced for S6 
generation and considered for future inbred line 
development programs.
Development of inbred lines of chilli through 
hybridization (set-1: advancing of generation S 2 
to S3)
M. A. Alam, M. M. Haque, A. H. F. Fahim and M. 
Z. H. Prodhan
The present study was undertaken to advance S 2 
progenies to the S 3 generation with the goal of 
developing superior homozygous inbred lines of 
chilli (Capsicum annuum L.). The experiment was 
conducted during the winter season of 2024-2025 
at the Spices Research Centre, BARI, Shibganj, 
Bogura. A total of 36 S 2 progenies derived from 
diverse hybridizations among elite breeding lines 
and released varieties (including TOZP-11, OC-
22, BARI Morich-2, BMCMA, BGCMA, and 
BGCOMA) were evaluated for yield and yield-
contributing traits. Substantial variation was 
observed for key traits including plant height, fruit 
length, fruit diameter, and fruit yield per plant. 
Fruit yield ranged from 0.40 t/ha to 13.23 t/ha 
per plant, indicating wide genetic variability and 
scope for selection. Notably, progenies such as 
(BARI Morich-2 × BGCMA-17)-4 (13.23 t/ha), 
(BARI Morich-2 × BGCMA-17)-1 (11.93 t/ha), 
and (BARI Morich-2 × BGCMA-17)-6 (12.00 t/ha) 
demonstrated superior yield performance compared 
to the parental checks. These elite lines will be 
advanced to the S3 generation and further evaluated 
for stability and performance in subsequent breeding 
programs. The results highlight the effectiveness of 
early-generation selection for genetic improvement 
in chilli.
Preliminary evaluation and germplasm 
maintenance of chilli genotypes (Set-I and II)
M. A. Alam, A. H. F. Fahim, M. A. Rahman, M. A. 
Mottalib, M. M. Haque and M. Z. H. Prodhan
This study presents the preliminary evaluation of 
50 (Set I) and 36 (Set-II) chilli genotypes grown 
in a single plot (3 m2) setup. The objective was to 
evaluate basic phenological and yield-related traits, 
including plant height (PH), number of branches 
(NB), flowering length (FL), pedicel length (PL), 
fruit diameter (FD), individual fruit weight (IFW), 
and fruit yield per plant (FY). Descriptive statistics 
in Set-I revealed moderate to high variability across 
genotypes. Notably, FY ranged from 0.8 to 22.9 
g, indicating significant potential for selection in 
future replicated trials. In case of Set-II descriptive 
statistics indicated wide phenotypic diversity, 
with FY ranging from 1.83 to 15.00 g per plant. 
Genotypes CO-634 and CO -611-2 performed best 
in terms of FY and associated traits. The findings 
provide a baseline reference for selecting elite lines 
for further multi-location evaluations and genetic 
improvement.

Evaluation of test cross hybrids of chilli 
M. A. Alam, A. H. F. Fahim, M. A. Rahman, M. A. 
Mottalib, M. M. Haque and M. Z. H. Prodhan
A field experiment was conducted at the Spices 
Research Centre (SRC), BARI, Bogura during 
the winter season to evaluate the performance 
of ten chilli test cross hybrids involving diverse 
parental lines. The trial followed RCBD with two 
replications. Significant genetic variability was 
observed among the hybrids for all studied traits. 
High heritability coupled with moderate to high 
genetic advance was recorded for fruit yield per plant 
(97.39%), individual fruit weight (96.24%), and

× AF-001 exhibited superior yield potential. These 
results offer valuable insights for developing high-
yielding chilli hybrids suitable for the winter season 
in Bangladesh.

Regional yield trial of chilli
M. A. Alam, M. A. Hossain, R Sarkar, A. H. F. 
Fahim and M. Z. H. Prodhan
The performance of nine chilli genotypes was 
evaluated across three locations during the 2024-
2025 growing season. The trial was conducted at the 
Spices Research Centre (SRC), Shibganj, Bogura; 
Spices Research Centre (RSRC), Faridpur; and 
Spices Research Sub-Centre (SRSC), Lalmonirhat, 
using a randomizeSubd complete block design 
(RCBD) with three replications. Measured traits 
included plant height, number of branches, fruit 
length, fruit diameter, single fruit weight, and fruit 
yield. Significant genetic variation was observed 
for most traits, with high heritability estimates for 
single fruit weight (0.69) and fruit yield (0.85), 
indicating strong genetic control and potential for 
selection. VTNMCH-1 (13.18 t/ha) and BARI 
Morich-2 (13.62 t/ha) were the highest-yielding 
entries, while BGCOMA-4 recorded the lowest 
yield (4.11 t/ha). Across environments, Bogura and 
Faridpur provided more favorable yield outcomes 
than Lalmonirhat. Genotypes such as VTNMCH-1, 
BARI Morich-2, and INDCH-23 displayed 
consistent performance across sites, indicating 
potential for broader adaptation. These findings 
reinforce the importance of genotype-environment 
interaction studies for optimizing chilli yield under 
diverse growing conditions.

Advanced yield trial of turmeric 
M. A. Alam, A. H. F. Fahim, M. A. Rahman, M. A. 
Mottalib and M. Z. H. Prodhan
An advanced yield trial (AYT) on turmeric (Curcuma 
longa L.) was conducted at the Spices Research Centre, 
BARI, Bogura, during the 2024-2025 growing season 
to evaluate nine turmeric genotypes including two 
check varieties (BARI Holud-4 and BARI Holud-5). 
The objective was to evaluate genetic variability 
and identify high-performing lines under Bogura 
conditions. The experiment was laid out in RCBD 
with three replications. Fourteen agro-morphological 
and yield-related traits were measured. High genotypic 
variability was found for traits such as number of 
primary fingers (NPF), weight of primary fingers 
(WPF), and weight of secondary fingers (WSF). The 
highest yield was recorded in genotype T0107 (39.53 
t/ha), followed by Patnai (38.20 t/ha) and T0095 
(37.33 t/ha). Heritability estimates were high (>0.90) 
for traits like plant height (PH), number of tillers 
(NT), number of leaves (NL), and number of mother 
rhizomes (NMR), indicating strong genetic control. 
The findings suggest T0107, T0095, and Patnai as 
promising candidates for future breeding and possible 
release.

Germplasm maintenance and evaluation under-
utilized spice crops
M. A. Alam, A. H. F. Fahim, M. A. Rahman, M. A. 
Mottalib, S. Naher and M. Z. H. Prodhan
This report summarized the evaluation and 
maintenance strategy for germplasm lines of five 
spice crops: Firingi, Ajowan, Mouri, and Sholuk, 
based on one-season field data collected from field 
trials at Spices Research Center, BARI. Seven key 
traits-plant height (PH), number of branches (NB), 
number of umbels (NU), fruits per umbel (FPU/
UPU), seeds per fruit (SPF/SPU), thousand grain 
weight (TGW), and weight per plant (WPP)-were 
measured. Firingi line FR-02, Ajowan line TA-07, 
Mouri line FN-17, and Sholuk line Dill-02 were 
identified as the best performers. The results suggest 
strong genetic control over key traits, facilitating 
targeted selection in future breeding. The report 
recommends priority lines for seed maintenance 
and outlines a strategy for germplasm conservation 
based on genetic variability, trait performance, and 
breeding value.

A germplasm maintenance study was conducted

Regional yield trail of naga chili lines
F. Ahmed, J. C. Sarker and M. H. M. B. Bhuyan 
Regional yield trial was conducted with selected 
two advance Naga chili lines at five different 
locations of BARI research stations during winter 
season of 2024-25 to observe their yield and yield 
potentiality as well as quality of chili produced. 
Maximum plant height was recorded in CC Jai-
010 (170 cm) at Jaintapur, whereas the shortest 
plant was recorded in CC Jai-018 (82.03 cm) in 
Cumilla. CC Jai-010 produced the highest number 
of fruits per plant (180) at Jaintapur while CC Jai-
018 produced the lowest number of fruits per plant 
(89.23) at Akbarpur. Fruit length found maximum in 
CC Jai-018 (6.08 cm) at Jaintapur but the shortest 
fruit was found in CC Jai-010 (3.53 cm) in Cumilla. 
Fruit diameter was found maximum in CC Jai-010 
(3.17 cm) at Jaintapur, whereas the lowest fruit 
diameter (1.52 cm) was found in CC Jai-018 at 
Akbarpur. Maximum individual fruit weight 6.73 
g) was obtained from Akbarpur but the minimum 
fruit weight (3.57 g) was obtained in Cumilla. The 
line CC Jai-010 recorded the maximum fruit yield 
(1211.5 g plant-1) at Jaintapur while the line CC 
Jai-018 recorded the lowest fruit yield (323.01 g 
plant-1) at Akbarpur. The line CC Jai-010 produced 
maximum yield (20.19 t ha−1) at Jaintapur whereas, 
the line CC Jai-018 produced the lowest yield (5.38 
t ha−1) at Akbarpur. Considering growth, yield and 
yield contributing characteristics the line CC Jai-010 
can be proposed to release a variety.

Screening of chilli genotypes for waterlogging 
stress tolerance
S. Brahma, M. N. Yousuf, M. M. Kamal, N. Nath 
and M. M. Haque
To mitigate the adverse effects of climate-induced 
waterlogging stress on chilli, a pot experiment was 
conducted with 15 genotypes during 2024-2025 at 
the Regional Spices Research Center. Waterlogging 
was imposed at 30 days after transplanting (DAT) 
by submerging pots in water 5 cm above the soil 
surface for 48 hours (Set I) and 72 hours (Set II). 
The experiment aimed to identify genotypes that 
demonstrate tolerance to waterlogging stress. 
Fifteen genotypes survived 48-hour waterlogging, 
while only one genotype (G16) survived the 72-
hour treatment. Based on survival percentage, 
SPAD values, dry matter accumulation, and Stress 
Tolerance Index (STI), genotypes G7, G12, G16, 
G21, G22, G24, G13, G17, G23, G20, G3, G2, G11, 
G15, and G10 were identified as relatively tolerant 
to waterlogging.

A field experiment was conducted to evaluate the

to mites, while 26 and 25 lines, respectively, were 
classified as susceptible.

Study of pollination approach on the true seed 
production of onion
 Mst. Sadia Naznin, M. A. Alam and M. Z. H. 
Prodhan
The experiment was conducted at the Spices Research 
Centre, BARI, Shibganj, Bogura, during the 2024-25 
Rabi season to study the effect of different pollination 
approaches on true seed production of onion (Allium 
cepa L.), variety BARI Piaz-6. The experiment 
was laid ot in RCBD with five treatments and three 
replications. The unit plot was 3.0 m x 1.2 m having 
plant spacing of 15 cm x 10 cm. The bulb of BARI 
Piaz-6 was sowing on 17 November 2024. Five 
treatments were implemented: T 1 involved natural 
pollination combined with regular hand pollination; 
T2, T3, and T 4 incorporated natural pollination with 
hand pollination at intervals of 1, 2, and 3 days, 
respectively; and T5 served as the control with only 
natural pollination. Results revealed that T1 (natural 
+ daily hand pollination) and T2 (natural + 1-day 
interval hand pollination) significantly enhanced 
key parameters such as 1000-seed weight (3.12 g 
and 2.88 g), seed yield (301.50 kg/ha and 284.21 kg/
ha), seeds per umbel (325.50 and 299.40) and active 
florets per umbel (115.93 and 110.30), compared 
to the control (T5) which recorded the lowest 
performance in all traits. The findings suggest that 
combining natural pollination with frequent hand 
pollination greatly improves true seed production of 
onion in Bangladesh. 
Effects of seed priming on germination and 
seedling growth summer onion
Mst. Sadia Naznin, M. N. A. Chowdhury and M. Z. 
H. Prodhan
The experiment was conducted at Spices Research 
Centre, BARI, Shibganj, Bogura during 25 
February 2025 to evaluate the effects of different 
seed priming methods on germination and early 
growth of summer onion cultivar BARI Piaz-5. 
The experiment followed a Randomized Complete 
Block Design (RCBD) with three replications. Five 
treatments were consisted: T 1: Hydro-priming, 
T2: Osmopriming, T 3: Hormonal priming, T 4: 
Biopriming, T 5: control, each replicated thrice. 
The highest germination (84.67 and 81.33%) were 
recorded in T 2 and T 3 respectively. The maximum 
seedling density (471.67 and 438.00 Seedlings/
m2) were observed in T 3 and T 4, respectively. The 
maximum seedling vigor index (1028.68 and 
1018.27) were noted in T2 and T3 respectively. The 
highest dry matter content (3.07%) and survival rate 
(88.67) were exhibited in T3 treatment. Biopriming 
(T4) produced the tallest plants (13.31cm) while 
the control treatment (T5) consistently exhibited the 
lowest performance including germination (59.67%), 
vigor index (737.91) and survival rate (61.33%). The 
study concludes that seed priming particularly with 
GA3 and KNO3 significantly improves germination, 
seedling vigor and early growth of summer onion 
and can be recommended for enhancing productivity 
under field conditions.

Application of micronutrients (Fe and Zn) for

M. A. Rahman, M. N. A. Chaudury, M. S. Naher, M. 
A. Alam, A. H. F. Fahim and Z. H. Prodhan 
Onion (Allium cepa L.) is a vital crop but often 
lacks essential micronutrients like iron (Fe) and 
zinc (Zn), which are crucial for human health.

economic viability. Six treatments were tested: T 1

An evaluation of yield limiting nutrients in onion 
using compositional nutrient diagnosis (cnd) 
norms on bangladesh soils
M. N. Yousuf, S. Brahma, M. M. Akand, A. J. M. 
Sirajul Karim, M. E. Ali, M. H. Rashid and M. M. 
Haque
Generic models can assist Compositional Nutrient 
Diagnosis (CND) in providing a yield cutoff value 
between high-and low-yielding subpopulations 
for small databases. The present study aimed 
to determine minimum bulb yield target of high 
yielding subpopulations in farmers' field and 
nutritional difference between high and low 
yielding subpopulations. Popular high yielding 
onion cv. BARI piaz-4 was extensively grown all 
over Bangladesh. Data were collected at random 
using a survey database of 42 observations from 
42 districts of Bangladesh including bulb yield 
and green portion or leaf nutrient concentrations. 
Nutrient composition was determined form leaf 
at 45-50 days after transplanting. Mean, median,

90 I Spices Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
minimum, maximum, standard deviations, skewness 
of yield as well as nutrient concentration for N, 
P, S, K, Ca, Mg, Na, Zn, Cu, B, Fe and Mn were 
determined and a R, which comprises all nutrients 
not chemically analyzed and quantified in onion. 
Row centered log ratio and cumulative variance 
ratio function of each nutrient was calculated. The 
CND generic model gave 27.49 tha -1 as minimum 
cutoff yield of the high-yield subpopulation. Zinc 
was identified as the core yield limiting nutrient 
for onion in piedmont plain, floodplain and basin 
soils of Bangladesh. However, Ca, S, B, Cu, N, Fe 
and Mn also play a significant role for increasing 
bulb yield of onion. Onion in farmers' fields of 
Bangladesh may require higher Zn fertilizer dose for 
better bulb yield. From the studied piedmont plain, 
floodplain and basin soils of Bangladesh, the yield 
limiting nutrients were established the following 
series: Zn>Ca>S>B>Cu>N>Fe>Mn>Mg>K>P.

Effect of chemical fertilizers on growth and yield 
of ginger (Zingiber officinale) rhizome in sack 
cultivation
M. S. Naher, M. A. Islam, M. A. Rahman and M. Z. 
H. Prodhan
From April 2024 to February 2025, six fertilizer 
treatments (0%, 100%, 125%, 150%, 175%, and 
200% of recommended fertilizer doses) were 
tested on sack-grown ginger at SRC Bogura. Each 
sack received a base soil mix, compost, coco dust, 
ash, cow dung, and varying amounts of chemical 
nutrients (urea, TSP, MoP, gypsum, ZnSO4, and 
borax), with split applications of nitrogen and 
potassium at 50, 80, and 110 days after planting. The 
150% RDF treatment consistently outperformed 
others producing the highest yield (998 g per sack), 
delivering a top marginal benefit-cost ratio (14.23), 
and maintaining low disease levels. Treatments 
above 150% RDF showed reduced effectiveness 
and higher disease incidence. Applying 150% of the 
recommended fertilizer dose is the best agronomic 
and economic strategy for sack-cultivated ginger, 
especially for urban and space-limited growers.

Effect of organic fertilizers on leaf yield of mint 
cultivation
M. S. Naher, M. A. Rahman, M. N. A. Choudhury 
and M. Z. H. Prodhan
A field experiment was conducted from December 
2024 to May 2025 at the Spices Research Centre, 
BARI, Bogura, to evaluate the effects of organic 
fertilizers on the leaf yield of mint (BARI 
Pudina-2). Treatments included cowdung (5 t/ha), 
vermicompost (3 t/ha), poultry manure (2.5 t/ha), 
trichocompost (2 t/ha), and an untreated control, 
arranged in RCBD with three replications. Organic 
fertilizers significantly improved plant height,

ha) came from the control. The results highlight 
that using organic fertilizers enhances yield and 
supports sustainable soil health and environmental 
safety, promoting organic nutrient management as 
an effective alternative or supplement to chemical 
fertilizers in mint cultivation.
Development of fertilizer recommendation for 
mint
M. S. Naher, M. A. Rahman, M. N. A. Choudhury 
and M. Z. H. Prodhan
A field experiment was conducted at the Spices 
Research Centre, BARI, Bogura during the 2024-
2025. Fourteen fertilizer treatments combining 
different levels of N, P, K, and S were tested on the 
mint variety BARI Pudina-2 using RCBD design.

identify optimal nutrient doses. Response of N was 
more pronounced in comparison to P and K. The

dose of 2 kg B, 4 kg Zn and 2-ton cowdung/ha appear 
to be the best treatment for maximizing the seed yield 
of dill. The results aim to support region-specific 
fertilizer recommendations, boosting sustainable and 
profitable mint cultivation in Bangladesh.

Incidence of fall armyworm, Spodoptera 
frugiperda on ginger in ginger growing areas of 
bangladesh
M. Z. H. Prodhan 
Fall Armyworm (FAW), Spodoptera frugiperda, 
(J.E. Smith) has been recorded in Bangladesh on 
maize during November 2018. It is a destructive 
and invasive pest, about 79% maize plants and 
26% cob were damaged by the pest in Bangladesh 
during 2019-20. Subsequently the pest was reported 
to attack on cabbage and tobacco from Rangpur, 
Bangladesh. Recently, the pest was found to attack 
on ginger (Zingiber officinale ) fields, about 12% 
infestation observed during 2024-25. It is suspected 
that the infestation spread gradually to the ginger 
growing areas in Bangladesh.

Survey and identification of summer onion 
diseases
N. Nath, M. A. Wadud, M. M. Kamal, M. N. Yousuf 
and S. N. Mozumder
Survey was conducted at different summer onion 
growing areas namely Gazipur, Faridpur, Rajbari 
and Bogura during 2024-25 to identify the diseases 
of summer onion with their causal organisms. Basal 
rot (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cepae) and purple 
blotch (Alternaria porri) were found predominantly 
in the surveyed area. Black mold (Aspergillus 
niger) was seen in post-harvest storage condition. 
Basal rot was observed at growth stage (30 to 45 
days old seedlings). Purple Blotch was observed 
in small, water-soaked spots on leaves that enlarge 
into purplish-brown lesions with yellow halos at 
the mid growth stage of the bulb. In storage, black 
mold was also found as a black, sooty discoloration 
on the neck and outer scales of the bulb. These 
fungi were identified as Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. 
cepae, Alternaria porri and Aspergillus niger were 
isolated from diseased plant parts on PDA medium 
for identification.
Detection of viruses and their vectors of chilli in 
Bangladesh
N. Nath, M. S. Rahman, M. A. Wadud, M. M. Kamal
The study was undertaken with a view to determining 
the reduction of growth and yield contributing 
parameters due to the viruses in Chilli (Capsicum 
annum L.). Based on symptomatological study, 
virus infected samples were collected from naturally 
infected chilli field from Regional Spices Research 
Centre, BARI, Gazipur. The infected samples 
were tested in the laboratory of Plant Pathology 
by Double Antibody Sandwich Enzyme-Linked 
Immuno-Sorbent Assay (DAS-ELISA). In order to 
draw up the management practices for the control of 
virus diseases of chilli, reliable tests are required for 
its detection. DAS-ELISA was found as the suitable 
tests for the detection of viruses. In this experiment, 
eight infected chilli germplasm were used against the 
antiserum i.e. Chilli veinal mottle virus (ChVMV) 
to detect the virus separately. The most common 
sucking pests such as aphids, whitefly, thrips and 
tiny mites were observed in the infected plants. 
However, only one infected chilli sample (A VPP-
1236-2) gave the positive result against the virus. 
The results suggested that Chilli veinal mottle virus 
(ChVMV) as the causal organism of that infected 
chilli germplasm.

Potential use of remote sensing platforms for 
garlic yield prediction
M. A. Mottalib, M. A. Alam, A. H. F. Fahim, M. A. 
Rahman, M. A. Islam, M. M. Hasan, M. M. Alam, 
M. Z. Hasan, M. A. Hoque, M. A. Rahman, K. 
Hassan, and Z. H. Prodhan
This study evaluated the suitability of various 
vegetation indices from Sentinel-2 imagery 
for predicting garlic yield across different 
growth stages. The indices analyzed included 
NDVI, SA VI, GESA VI, GCVI, EVI2, NDRE, 
and MCARI. NDRE consistently showed the 
strongest correlation with yield, achieving the 
highest R2 value (0.6798) on 09 March 2024 
coinciding with garlic's bulb development 
and maturity stage. GCVI (R2 = 0.5573) and 
GESA VI (R2 = 0.5281) also performed well, 
while MCARI showed poor results throughout. 
NDRE's sensitivity to chlorophyll and canopy 
structure under high biomass makes it highly 
effective in dense garlic fields. GCVI provided 
the best model fit (R2 = 0.6063), while NDRE 
had the lowest prediction error (RMSE = 194.80 
kg/ha; MBE = 160.62 kg/ha). GESA VI, despite 
weaker statistical performance, aligned most 
closely with BBS yield estimates, highlighting the 
importance of ground validation. Yield mapping 
revealed that 68% of the area produced 9.3-10.1 
t/ha, confirming NDRE as the most reliable index 
during late growth stages.
Land suitability assessment for spices crop 
production through remote sensing and GIS in 
southern saline region of Bangladesh
M. A. Mottalib, M. A. Alam, A. H. F. Fahim, M. A. 
Rahman, M. A. Islam, M. M. Hasan, M. M. Alam, 
M. Z. Hasan, M. A. Hoque, M. A. Rahman, K. 
Hassan, and Z. H. Prodhan
This study aimd to identify suitable land for spices 
crop production in the southern saline region of 
Bangladesh, considering topography, climate, and 
soil properties. The Analytical Hierarchy Process 
(AHP), a Multicriteria Decision-Making approach, 
was applied using GIS. Key criteria included 
soil texture, depth, salinity, land type, surface 
temperature, rainfall, slope, elevation, and drainage. 
Weights were assigned through expert judgment and 
pairwise comparison, while sub-parameter scores 
were based on field data and standards. Results 
showed 26.31% (8804.52 ha) as highly suitable, 
45.32% moderately suitable, 13.56% marginally 
suitable, and 14.81% permanently unsuitable. 
Shallow soil, steep slope, and high salinity limited 
suitability. Further study will be conducted next year 
for improved validation and interpretation.

Studies on quality of developed ginger-garlic mix 
paste during storage
M. M. Alam, M. G. F. Chowdhury and M. Z. H. 
Prodhan
This experiment was carried out to investigate the 
effect of preservatives, storage conditions and time 
on the keeping quality of ginger-garlic (G-G) mix 
paste. The fresh peel ginger sliced and garlic cloves 
were crushed in blender. The mix paste was prepared 
using 50:50 of ginger sliced and garlic cloves. 
Among three treatments, samples of mix pastes were 
treated with T1 - salt + sodium benjoate + citric acid, 
T2- salt + KMS + citric acid, T3-citric acid only. All 
the prepared samples (G-G mix paste) were stored 
in glass bottle (GB) and food grade plastic pot (PP) 
kept in room temperature (RT) and refrigerated 
temperature (RFT). The moisture, ash, pH and TSS 
of G-G paste of all the samples were observed at 
30 days interval up to 270 days of storage. It was 
found that ash, pH and TSS of G-G paste in GB and 
PP were increased while moisture was decreased 
with the increase in storing time at all treatments. 
The colour, flavor, texture and overall acceptability 
of all the samples were observed at 15 days interval 
up to 270 days storage. It was observed that in room 
temperature the highest shelf life 270 days and 180 
days were found of ginger-garlic mix paste in GB 
and PP by T2(treated with NaCl + CA+ KMS) which 
was closely followed by T 1 (treated with NaCl + 
CA + sodium benjoate) with 150 and 120 days 
and T3 (treated with CA) with 75 and 60 days for 
same storage condition. It is also observed that in 
refrigerated storage the highest shelf life of ginger-
garlic mix paste 270 days was found in T 1 and T 2 
for both glass bottle and plastic pot, but T 3 showed 
150 and 120 days shelf life when it was packed in 
glass bottle and plastic pot.In order to determine 
the suitability of two samples of ginger-garlic paste 
(which were found better in RT and RFT) in a curry, 
it was decided to conduct organoleptic taste test 
of chicken and beef curry using above 2 samples 
(T1and T3) with fresh ginger-garlic paste. The results 
showed that all the samples were statistically almost 
identical in respect of colour, flavour, pungency, 
taste and overall acceptability though there was little 
bit difference in scoring among each attributes.

Hybridization of eggplant
S. Yesmin, M. Ratna, E. Mahmud, M. Islam, N. 
Akter and M. A. Rahman
An experiment was carried out at Regional 
Horticulture Research Station, Lebukhali, 
Patuakhali during October, 2024 to March, 2025 
to develop hybrid variety of eggplant for round 
the year production. Six parental lines were used 
in this experiment. The parents were crossed by 
following 6×6 full diallel cross design. The parents 
were crossed in all possible combinations including 
reciprocals and a total of 30 cross combinations 
were made. A total of 221 crosses were done and 
140 fruits were harvested. The seeds obtained from 
the harvested fruits will be used to raise F 1 plant.

Heterosis study of eggplant hybrids
A. K. M. Quamruzzaman, S. Akter and L. Akter
A field experiment was conducted at BARI, Gazipur,

Maintenance and quality seed production of 
eggplant (OP varieties, Hybrids varieties and 
parental lines of concern hybrids)
L. Akter, A. K. M. Quamruzzaman and S. Akter
The study evaluated genetic purity maintenance and 
seed production parameters in eggplant varieties at 
BARI. Isolation techniques effectively preserved 
genetic purity, with all varieties maintaining 98-99% 
purity (off-types <2%), well below the 5% national 
standard, confirming the efficacy of 200-meter 
isolation distances. Seed yield varied significantly 
among varieties, with BARI Begun-12 producing 
exceptional yields (45 kg/20 decimals) due to superior 
fruit size and seed-setting capacity, outperforming 
hybrids (4-8 kg). Despite lower quantities, hybrid 
seeds met premium quality standards, exhibiting 
97.6-99.2% germination rates with optimal physical 
purity and moisture content. Disease incidence 
remained minimal (0.5%) through stringent sanitation 
and controlled fermentation practices. The inverse 
yield-area relationship in BARI Begun-12 highlights 
genotype-specific efficiency differences. These findings 
establish BARI Begun-12 as ideal for commercial seed 
production while underscoring the need for optimized 
hybrid seed protocols to balance yield and quality. The 
study provides critical insights for enhancing eggplant 
seed production systems in Bangladesh.

Heterosis and combining ability analysis in 
tomato (Solanum lycopersicum L.)
M. R. Islam, M. M. R. Salim and A K M 
Quamruzzaman
The experiment was conducted at the research farm 
of Olericulture Division, Horticulture Research 
Centre, BARI, Gazipur to estimate heterosis and 
combining ability in tomato. A randomized complete 
block design (RCBD) with two replications was 
used to evaluate nine tomato parents, their hybrids, 
and standard checks for yield, earliness, and quality 
traits. Significant genotypic variation (p < 0.05) was 
observed for yield/plant, fruit traits, flowering time 
and TSS. Hybrid P3 × P7 showed the highest heterosis 
for yield and strongest SCA, while P4 × P6 combined 
yield heterosis with improved TSS. P 1 × P2 was the 
best for earliness, showing negative heterosis and 
favorable SCA. GCA analysis identified P 3 and P 4 
as top yield donors, P 2 and P 4 for TSS, and P 1 and 
P6 for earliness. These results highlight key parental 
combinations for targeted hybrid development, with 
P3 × P7 and P4 × P6 recommended for multi-location 
testing.

This study was conducted to produce breeder seed

varietal purity through the application of genetic 
and agronomic principles. The experiment included

M. A. Islam, M. H. Islam and A. K. M. 
Quamruzzaman
A field trial was conducted at the experimental field 
of Olericulture Division, HRC, BARI, Gazipur 
during the winter season of 2024-25 to evaluate the 
growth, yield, and curd quality traits of four broccoli 
genotypes. Significant differences were observed 
among the genotypes for all studied parameters. 
BARI Broccoli-1 was the earliest maturing 
genotype, initiating curd at 39 days and harvesting 
at 54.67 days, but exhibited the lowest yield (12.13 
t/ha). In contrast, BOI-04 showed the highest yield 
potential (20.00 t/ha) with superior marketable curd 
weight and plant biomass, although it matured later. 
The genotypes BOI-03 and BOI-01offered a balance 
between earliness (43 days to curd initiation) and 
higher yield (17.37 t/ha and 15.27 t/ha, respectively). 
In addition, BOI-01 demonstrated satisfactory 
seed production capability under the prevailing 
climatic conditions. Based on the findings, BOI-
04 is recommended for high-yield cultivation and 
BOI-01 may serve as suitable genotypes combining 
earliness with reasonable yield potential with seed 
production capacity. These results support varietal 
improvement and commercial broccoli production 
in Bangladesh.
Maintenance and quality seed production of 
broccoli (BARI Broccoli-1)
M. A. Islam and A K M Quamruzzaman 
A maintenance breeding program for BARI 
Broccoli-1 was conducted during the rabi season of 
2024-25 at the Olericulture Division, Horticulture 
Research Center, BARI, Gazipur, to preserve genetic 
purity and varietal identity. Seedlings were raised in 
seedbeds using the double transplanting method and 
transplanted at the 4-leaf stage with a spacing of 50 
× 50 cm. Out of 425 total plants, 320 were selected 
as true-to-type, achieving 75% varietal uniformity. 
The selected plants produced 4.13 kg of seed, with 
an average seed yield of 12.90 g per plant. The seed 
yield was 516 kg/ha without rouging and 387 kg/
ha with rouging. Although rouging reduced total 
yield, it was essential to maintain genetic purity and 
uniformity. The study demonstrates that systematic 
selection, rouging, and controlled pollination are

BARI Annual Report 2024-25
critical for producing high-quality breeder seed of 
BARI Broccoli-1.
Radish 
Evaluation of radish genotypes
M. A. Islam, S. Akter and A. K. M. Quamruzzaman
The study was conducted at the experimental field 
of Olericulture Division, Horticulture Research 
Center, Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute, 
Gazipur during 2024-25 to evaluate the performance 
of eleven radish genotypes, including three released 
varieties (BARI Mula-1, BARI Mula-2, and BARI 
Mula-3), based on vegetative and yield-contributing 
traits. Significant genotypic variation (p < 0.001) 
was observed across all parameters. RS 03 showed 
the highest number of leaves (30) and leaf breadth 
(46.0 cm), while RS 06 produced the longest roots 
(35.8 cm) and the highest marketable root weight 
(631.7 g). Yield per hectare ranged from 17.8 t/ha 
(RS 02) to 43.0 t/ha (RS 06), with RS 06, RS 07, 
RS 04, and RS 05 outperforming the check varieties. 
BARI Mula-1 yielded best among the released 
varieties (38.6 t/ha). Overall, RS 06, RS 07, RS 04 
and RS 05 were identified as promising genotypes 
for future variety development.
Maintenance and quality seed production of 
radish (BARI Mula-1 and BARI Mula-2)
M. A. Islam and A K M Quamruzzaman 
A maintenance breeding program was conducted 
during the rabi season of 2024-25 at the 
Olericulture Division, Horticulture Research 
Center, BARI, Gazipur to preserve the genetic 
purity of two released radish varieties, BARI 
Mula-1 and BARI Mula-2. Seeds were sown in 
November, and true-to-type plants were selected 
and replanted for seed production. In BARI Mula-
1, 405 plants were selected from 580, maintaining 
70% varietal uniformity, and producing 13 kg 
of seed, equivalent to 830 kg/ha with rouging 
compared to 1188 kg/ha without rouging. In 
BARI Mula-2, 60 plants were selected from 90, 
ensuring 66% uniformity, and producing 0.8 kg 
of seed, corresponding to 325 kg/ha with rouging 
compared to 495 kg/ha without rouging. Although 
rouging reduced seed yield, it was essential for 
maintaining varietal identity, genetic purity, and 
quality breeder seed production.
Carrot 
Evaluation of carrot genotypes
M. A. Islam, S. Akter and A. K. M. Quamruzzaman
A field trial was conducted at the experimental field 
of Olericulture Division, HRC, BARI, Gazipur 
during the winter season of 2024-25 to evaluate the 
growth, yield, and root quality traits of four carrot 
genotypes. Significant variability was observed, 
indicating potential for genetic improvement. 
Genotype DC-03 exhibited the highest total plant 
weight (235.93 g) and marketable yield (20.22 t/ha) 
but its fibrous roots made it unsuitable for visual and 
textural selection. In contrast, DC-1 showed the best 
root quality, with the lowest core: flesh ratio (0.51), 
smooth texture, and acceptable yield (18.22 t/ha). 
DC-06 (18.53 t/ha) and DC-7 (18.96 t/ha) also 
demonstrated moderate yield and better root texture 
than DC-03, making them suitable alternatives. 
DC-7 had the thickest roots after DC-3 (4.57 cm), 
while DC-06 maintained favorable uniformity. High 
heritability and genetic gain in root traits suggest that 
DC-01, DC-06, and DC-07 are promising candidates 
for selection based on root quality for future trial, 
with DC-3 useful as a yield donor in breeding.
