Advanced yield trial of snake gourd lines
M. R. Islam and A. K. M. Qumruzzaman
This study evaluated five snake gourd genotypes at 
Olericulture Division, HRC, BARI, Gazipur, during 
the 2024-2025 Kharif season to identify high-yielding 
lines. The experiment followed a randomized 
complete block design with three replications, 
standard agronomic practices, and comprehensive 
trait assessments. The line TC 46 emerged as the 
superior genotype, exhibiting the earliest flowering 
(65.67 days), first harvest (76.67 days), highest fruit 
yield (8.86 kg/plant; 26.60 t/ha), maximum fruits per 
plant (32.33), and widest fruit diameter (4.47 cm). 
The line TC 01 produced the longest (50.00 cm) and 
heaviest fruits (315.33 g) but had moderate yield 
(22.38 t/ha) and the shortest harvest duration (58.67 
days). The line BARI CHICHINGA-1 showed the 
earliest flowering initiation (64.33 days) and longest 
harvest duration (72.67 days) but low yielded 
(15.96 t/ha) with the narrowest fruits (3.90 cm). The 
line TC 58 recorded the lowest yield (3.95 kg/plant; 
11.86 t/ha) and fewest fruits (20.33). The results 
demonstrate TC 46 has optimal balance of early 
maturity, high productivity and robust fruit traits, 
recommend it for breeding programs and further 
evaluation.

Maintenance of BARI released OP and hybrid 
varieties of bitter gourd
M. R. Islam, M. M. R. Salim and A. K. M. 
Qumruzzaman
Breeder seed production was done in Olericulture 
Division, HRC, RARI, Gazipur in the 2024-25 
season evaluated seed yield and genetic purity of 
two hybrids (BARI Hybrid Karola-2 and 3) and one 
open-pollinated variety (BARI Karola-2) of bitter 
gourd in Bangladesh. Seedlings were transplanted 
into 18 m × 1.2 m beds (18 plants per bed) under 
designated layouts: BARI Hybrid Karola-2 
contains (12 female + 6 male beds), Karola-3 
hybrid (8 female + 6 male beds), and Karola-2 OP 
(20 beds). Balanced fertilization and split nutrient 
applications were applied. Rigorous rouging at 
vegetative, flowering, and fruiting stages, together 
with field isolation and hand pollination at anthesis, 
maintained varietal integrity. The Karola-2 hybrid 
female line (20 beds, 360 plants) yielded 1.3 kg 
seed (65 g/bed; 3.6 g/plant), Karola-3 (14 beds, 
252 plants) yielded 1.3 kg (93 g/bed; 5.2 g/plant), 
and open-pollinated Karola-2 (20 beds) produced 
2.3 kg (115 g/bed; 6.4 g/plant). Yield differences 
reflect genetic background and pollination mode. 
These protocols support sustainable production of 
high-quality breeder seed in this cross-pollinated 
crop.

Maintenance and quality seed production of 
watermelon
L. Akter, A. K. M. Quamruzzaman and S. Akter
This study successfully demonstrated the 
effectiveness of rigorous maintenance breeding 
protocols for watermelon breeder seed production at 
HRC, BARI Gazipur and RHRS, Patuakhali during 
the 2024-25 season. Through strict isolation (1000m), 
controlled pollination, and systematic roguing, 
genetic purity exceeding 98% was maintained 
for both BARI Tarmuj-1 and Tarmuj-2 varieties. 
The produced seeds consistently met superior 
quality standards, with germination rates of 95-
97%, physical purity >99%, and minimal pathogen 
contamination (<0.5%). Location-specific yield 
analysis revealed Patuakhali's superior performance 
for Tarmuj-1 (40% higher than Gazipur), indicating 
its better agro-climatic suitability. The combined 
seed production of 6.0kg (3.6kg Tarmuj-1 and 
2.4kg Tarmuj-2) from both locations, coupled with 
the initiation of a second production cycle with 
30% expanded acreage, establishes a sustainable 
framework for quality seed multiplication. These 
findings provide valuable insights for optimizing 
watermelon seed production systems in Bangladesh 
while maintaining genetic integrity and quality 
standards.
Advanced yield trial of netted melon
M. R. Islam and A. K. M. Qumruzzaman
This study evaluated nine advanced netted melon 
(Cucumis melo var. reticulatus) lines in Gazipur, 
Bangladesh, during the 2024-2025 rabi season 
using a randomized complete block design. CM-
07 achieved the highest yield (12.44 t/ha and 1.87 
kg/plant) due to maximal fruit count (4.67/plant), 
though with moderate fruit weight (400 g) and 
sweetness (7% TSS). CM-04 ranked second (11.01

matching CM-01, which also exhibited superior fruit 
diameter 10.33 cm and flesh thickness 2.75 cm. CM-
06 showed peak sweetness (12.33% TSS) but 
moderate yield (9.78 t/ha). Significant trade-offs 
were observed: high-yield/large-fruit lines (CM-07, 
CM-04 and CM-01) had reduced TSS (5.33-8%), 
while the sweetest genotype (CM-06) moderate 
yield. These results identify CM-07 and CM-04 for 
yield focused cultivation and CM-01 and CM-06 
for trait-specific breeding, addressing Bangladesh's

Regional yield trial of hyacinth bean 
M. R. Islam and A. K. M. Qumruzzaman
Regional yield trial of twelve hyacinth bean lines 
was conducted at the Olericulture Division, HRC, 
BARI, Gazipur during winter season of 2024-25 to 
find out superior lines. The experiment followed a 
Randomized Complete Block Design with three 
replications, using standard agronomic practices. 
Data on phenology, yield, pod characteristics, and 
pest/disease incidence were recorded and analyzed. 
Significant differences were observed among 
genotypes. DL Gaz-024 emerged as the highest 
yielder (7.83 kg/plant; 32.65 t/ha), exhibiting early 
flowering (47 days) and high pod count (706/plant), 
no mosaic virus and had moderate borer infestation 
(8.00%). LP Jam 008 combined high yield (6.88 kg/
plant; 28.69 t/ha), very early maturity (flowering: 
41 days; first harvest: 52 days), long pods (13.43 
cm), and absence of mosaic virus, despite moderate 
borer infestation (6.33%). DL Gaz-032 produced 
the longest (13.67 cm) and widest (3.70 cm) pods 
with low borer infestation (4.66%) and no mosaic 
virus, but yielded moderately (5.26 kg/plant). 
Conversely, LP Pah-005 and LP Pah-006 were 
the lowest yielders and some lines (LP Pah-025, 
LP Pah-006) suffered high borer infestation and 
mosaic virus. DL Gaz-024 was the highest yielder 
and LP Jam 008 demonstrated the most promising 
combination of desirable traits for potential varietal 
release.

Evaluation of F 4 progeny rows of okra for yield 
and resistance to yellow vein mosaic virus
S. Sultana and M. S. Ali
An experiment was conducted to evaluate F 4 
progeny rows of okra along with the check variety 
BD Dherosh-2 for yield and resistance to yellow vein 
mosaic virus (YVMV). Considerable variability was 
observed among progeny families for plant height, 
fruit number per plant, individual fruit weight, and 
yield. Plant height ranged from 80.6 to 183.8 cm, 
fruit number from 11to 17, and individual fruit 
weight from 11.33 to 14.69 g. Yield per hectare

outperformed the check, yielding 10.7-11.4 t/ha 
with no YVMV incidence. Within these families, 
elite plants with complete resistance were identified 
and selfed for advancement to the F 5 generation. 
The results highlight promising progeny families as 
sources of high yield and YVMV resistance for okra 
breeding programs.

Soilless Culture 
Development of coco-coir based soilless culture 
systems (SCS) for growing fruit vegetables
M. H. Islam, B. Ahmed, M. M. R. Salim and S. Akter
Soilless culture systems (SCS) are a promising 
approach for producing high-value vegetables where 
soil-related constraints limit productivity. This study 
aimed to develop a simplified coco-coir-based 
hydroponic system for winter-season production 
of sweet pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) var. BARI 
Mistimorich-2 and tomato (Solanum lycopersicum 
L.) var. BARI Tomato-21. Two nutrient treatments 
were compared: T1 (standard Enshi-shoo solution) 
and T2 (50% strength of a newly formulated 
commercial-grade hydroponic nutrient solution). 
Plants were grown in coco dust substrates under 
drip irrigation, arranged in a completely randomized 
design with six replications. Sweet pepper grown 
with T1 produced higher fruit number (8.83/plant), 
fruit weight (148.08 g), and yield (1.31 kg/plant) 
compared to T2 (7.83 fruits/plant, 139.58 g, 1.09 kg/
plant). In tomato, T1 yielded slightly more (1.62 kg/
plant) than T2 (1.54 kg/plant). The results suggest 
that a coco-coir-based SCS with a balanced nutrient 
solution is effective for winter-season production of 
fruit vegetables in resource-limited regions.
Development and standardization of hydroponic 
nutrient solution based on commercial grade 
chemical fertilizers available in Bangladesh
M. H. Islam, B. Ahmed, M. M. R. Salim and S. Akter
Hydroponic vegetable production offers an efficient 
and sustainable method for cultivating high-value 
crops, especially in land-scarce countries like 
Bangladesh. However, widespread adoption is often 
hindered by the high cost and limited availability of 
imported, analytical-grade nutrient solutions. This 
study was conducted to develop and standardize a 
hydroponic nutrient solution using locally available 
commercial-grade fertilizers and evaluate its 
effectiveness in growing high value vegetables 
such as sweet pepper (BARI Mistimorich-1) and 
tomato (BARI Tomato-19). Four treatments were 
tested: T1 (Enshi shoo standard solution), T 2 (40% 
strength), T3 (50% strength) and T 4 (60% strength) 
of a commercial-grade formulation. Key growth and 
yield parameters were measured. Results indicated 
that the 50% strength solution (T 3) performed

112 I Vegetable Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
comparably to the standard solution in both crops, 
producing optimal yield and plant vigor. These 
findings suggest that the T 3 formulation is a cost-
effective and locally applicable alternative to 
imported hydroponic nutrient solutions, promoting 
accessible and sustainable vegetable production.
Development of a nutrient film technique (NFT) 
system for growing leafy vegetables using 
simplified hydroponic approaches
M. H. Islam, B. Ahmed, M. M. R. Salim and S. Akter
Hydroponic systems offer sustainable alternatives 
to conventional soil-based agriculture, particularly 
in areas facing space and resource limitations. This 
study was conducted to develop a simplified nutrient 
film technique (NFT) hydroponic system using 
locally available materials for winter cultivation 
of leafy vegetables. BARI Lettuce-1 was selected 
as the test crop and evaluated under four nutrient 
regimes: T 1 (standard Enshi Shoo solution), T2 
(60% formulation), T 3 (50%), and T 4 (40%), all 
prepared using locally sourced commercial-grade 
fertilizers. The experiment followed RCBD with 
four replications. Morphological parameters 
including plant height, leaf number, leaf dimensions, 
root length, and fresh weight were recorded after 
4-8 weeks of growth. Results revealed that the full-
strength nutrient solution (T1) significantly improved 
plant vigor and yield (10.67 kg/3m2), followed by 
the 50% solution (T 3) which also demonstrated 
substantial growth potential. Treatments T 2 and 
T4 exhibited stunted growth and lower biomass 
accumulation, indicating the critical role of adequate 
nutrient availability. This research highlights the 
feasibility of adopting low-cost NFT systems for 
efficient leafy vegetable production in peri-urban 
and resource-constrained environments.
Validation of hydroponic system models at 
Jashore and Rangpur
M. H. Islam, B. Ahmed, M. M. R. Salim and S. Akter
The validation of simplified hydroponic system 
models was carried out at the Regional Agricultural 
Research Station (RARS), Jashore and at Rangpur 
during 2024-25 in semi-controlled net house 
conditions. Three hydroponic culture techniques, 
namely soilless culture system (SCS), nutrient 
film technique (NFT), and deep water culture 
system (DWC) were evaluated for their suitability 
in producing both fruiting and leafy vegetables. 
At Jashore, tomato, cherry tomato and capsicum 
were cultivated under SCS, while lettuce and water 
spinach were grown under DWC, and spinach 
and lettuce were tested in NFT. At Rangpur, 
cucumber and tomato were tested in SCS, while 
leafy vegetables including BARI Palongshak-2 and 
BARI Lalshak-1 were evaluated in DWC and NFT 
systems. The systems were developed with locally 
available materials and supplied with standard 
hydroponic nutrient solutions. Results showed 
that SCS performed well for fruit-bearing crops, 
producing higher yields in tomato, cherry tomato, 
capsicum, and cucumber across locations. Leafy 
vegetables exhibited good adaptability in both NFT 
and DWC systems, with lettuce, spinach, palong 
shak and lal shak producing marketable yields within 
short crop cycles. The study highlights the potential 
of simplified hydroponic models in different agro-
ecological zones of Bangladesh, demonstrating 
their effectiveness for safe and high-value vegetable 
production under protected cultivation.

Plant Physiology Section
Enhancing seed yield and quality of sweet pepper 
by application of plant growth regulators
R. Khatoon, L. Akter, M. Moniruzzaman A. Q. M. 
Quamruzzaman and M. F. Ahmed 
An experiment was conducted at the Plant 
Physiology Section research field of the Horticulture 
Research Centre, BARI, Joydebpur, Gazipur during 
2024-25 to enhance seed yield of sweet pepper 
by application of growth regulators. Two growth 
regulators viz. NAA and GA3 were applied as foliar 
spray in two sweet pepper (Capsicum annuum L.) 
varieties to enhance seed yield and quality. The 
experiment was laid out in RCBD (factorial) with 
three replications. Ten treatment combinations 
comprising five growth regulators viz. GA 3 25 
ppm, GA 3 50 ppm, NAA 25 ppm, NAA 50 ppm 
and untreated control and two mistimorich varieties 
viz. BARI Mistimorich-1, CA0043A which was 
proposed as BARI Mistimorich-3 were used for 
this experiment. Foliar sprays were done at 30, 
60 and 90 days after transplanting, among plant 
growth regulators, maximum growth and maximum 
germination after harvest was found from 50 ppm 
GA3. But spraying of 50 ppm NAA resulted in 
higher number of fruits per plant, fruit yield per 
plant and seed yield per plant. While the control 
recorded lowest values for the same parameters. 
The seed yield obtained from 50 ppm NAA was 
17.49% and 29.87% higher over the control in 
BARI Mistimorich-1 and CA0043A, respectively. 
There was gradual decline in seed germination 
after 3 months of storage. The highest germination 
percentage (97.78%) was recorded in 50 ppm NAA 
whereas the lowest was observed in case of control 
treatment (71.11%) after 3 months of storage. 
Similar trend was observed for seed vigour indices. 
Thus, it may be concluded that foliar spray of 50 
ppm NAA played an important role in improving 
the fruit yield, seed yield attributing parameters. 
Foliar spray of 50 ppm GA 3 and 50 ppm NAA at 
30, 60 and 90 DAT can be considered as a suitable 
technique for improving seed yield and quality of 
sweet pepper, as well as reducing loss in qualitative 
seed character during seed storage.
Effect of humic acid on flower retention, pod 
setting and yield of summer country bean
R. Khatoon, M. Moniruzzaman and M. F. Ahmed
A field experiment was carried out at the research 
field of Plant Physiology Section, Horticulture 
Research Centre, BARI during summer season 
of 2024 to reduce flower drop for maximizing 
the yield of summer country bean (var. BARI 
Sheem-7). Two methods of humic acid (HA) 
application: foliar spray and soil application were 
included in the experiment to flower retention and 
find out optimum dose of humic acid for maximum 
pod yield. The treatment consisted of three levels 
of humic acid soil application viz. 5 kg/ha, 10 kg/ha 
and 15 kg/ha and two levels of foliar spray viz.1000 
ppm and 1500 ppm humic acid. The experiment 
was conducted using randomized complete block 
design with 3 replications. Humic acid application 
significantly affected pod setting percentage, pods/
plant and pod yield. Foliar application humic 
acid @ 1500 ppm resulted in higher pod setting 
(26.88%), number of pods/plant (4.83), pod yield/
plant (1582.83g), however it was statistically 
similar to the treatments where HA was soil 
applied @ 10 and 15 kg/ha. It may be concluded 
that humic acid @ 1500 ppm and soil application 
@ 10 kg 15 kg/ha significantly enhanced pod set 
percentages, pod yield and yield components of 
summer country bean.
Effect of boron on flower retention and pod yield 
of summer country bean
R. Khatoon, M. Moniruzzaman and M. F. Ahmed
A field experiment was carried out at the research 
field of Plant Physiology Section, Horticulture 
Research Centre, BARI during summer season 
of 2024 to reduce flower drop for maximizing the 
pod yield of summer country bean (var. BARI 
Sheem-7). The soil test values (boron) showed that

boron (0.15 mg/kg). The treatment consisted of five 
levels of boron (0.1%, 0.2%, 0.3%, 0.4% and soil 
application @ 2 kg/ha) and untreated control. The 
experiment was laid out in randomized complete 
block design with 4 replications. The micronutrient 
boron in the form of boric acid was applied as 
foliar spray and as soil application to determine the 
optimum rate of boron for maximizing the yield of

Vegetable Crops I 115
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
BARI Sheem-7. Foliar application was done before 
flowering stage, at flowering stage and at fruit 
setting stage. The results indicated that application 
of boron had significant influence on the number 
of pods/plant, individual pod weight and pod yield 
per plant. The highest number of pods (302.00) was 
produced by 0.2% foliar spray of boron and the

Effect of salicylic acid on growth, yield and 
physiological attributes of tomato under salinity 
stress 
R. Khatoon, M. Moniruzzaman and M. F. Ahmed
Salicylic acid (SA) usage is a relatively inexpensive 
and quick method for promoting growth and yield 
of crops under saline conditions. A pot experiment 
was conducted in open air at the research field of 
Plant Physiology Section, Horticulture Research 
Centre, BARI during rabi season of 2024-25. The 
experiment was carried out RCBD (factorial) design 
with three replications to evaluate the effect of 
salicylic acid (SA) on tomato (BARI Tomato- 21) 
growth under salt stress condition. The first factor 
was three levels of irrigation water salinity (0, 8 
dS/m and 12 dS/m) and the second factor was 
salicylic acid (SA) concentration (0, 50 ppm and 
100 ppm) which was foliar sprayed. There was 
highly significant reduction in plant height, SPAD 
value, plant dry weights, RWC% and yield per plant 
with increasing salinity. However, yield of plants 
treated with 50 ppm SA was significantly higher 
than the other concentrations. The results revealed 
that growth characters and yield attributes were 
decreased due to the harmful effect of salt stress. 
Spray of salicylic acid (SA) @ 50 ppm improved 
growth characters, RWC%, SPAD value, yield 
attributes and fruit yield under salt stress. The study 
revealed that 50 ppm SA spray could be successfully 
used to obtain better growth and yield in tomato 
under moderate salt stress.
Study of physiological disorder of BARI released 
tomato varieties
R. Khatoon, M. Moniruzzaman and M. F. Ahmed
Tomato is one of the most popular protective 
foodstuffs because of its high lycopene content 
and widely grown vegetables in the world. A 
field experiment was carried out at the research 
field of Plant Physiology Section, Horticulture 
Research Centre, BARI during winter season of 
2025 to study the physiological disorder of BARI 
released tomato varieties. Eleven BARI released 
tomato varieties, namely BARI Tomato-2, BARI 
Tomato-3, BARI Tomato-11, BARI Tomato-14, 
BARI Tomato-15, BARI Tomato-16, BARI 
Tomato-17, BARI Tomato-18, BARI Tomato-19, 
BARI Tomato-20, BARI Tomato-21 were used for 
the study. Tomato plants are susceptible to various 
kinds of physiological problems, which can reduce 
fruit quality and productivity. The purpose of this 
study was to know about the non-parasitic disorders 
which affect the tomato crop and the remedies 
which should be followed to control them. The 
major physiological disorders which are affecting 
the crop are blotchy ripening, fruit cracking (radial 
and concentric cracking), sunscald, and cat facing 
etc. Maximum disorder (13.77%) was found from 
BARI Tomato- 17. In BARI Tomato-16 and BARI 
Tomato-20, no physiological disorder was found. 
Choosing tomato cultivars that are less susceptible to 
physiological problems can improve crop resilience. 
By addressing these issues, growers can improve 
overall crop health, resulting in higher-quality yields 
and lower economic losses.

M. Afroz, L. Yasmin, M. M. Rahman and M. S. Ali
Fourteen tomato varieties/accessions were

Efficacy of chemicals, botanicals and plant 
defense activators in managing okra yellow vein 
mosaic virus
M. M. Rahman, L. Yasmin, M. Afroz and M. S. Ali
This study was conducted to evaluate the efficacy of 
chemicals, botanicals and plant defense activators in 
managing Okra Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus (OYVMV) 
and Okra enation leaf curl disease (OELCuV), as 
well as their impact on crop yield. The experiment 
was conducted at Horticulture research field during 
2024-25 growing season in summer. The experiment 
consisted of eight treatments such as: i) Basil leaves 
5m/L, ii). Neem oil 5ml/L iii). Salicylic acid 0.1 mM, 
iv). Zinger 5ml/L, v) Turmeric 5ml/L vi). Aloe vera 
5ml/L, vii) Imidacloprid 0.5ml/L viii) Untreated 
control. Through, no statistically significant 
differences were found in disease incidence or yield 
across treatments, certain botanicals demonstrated 
promising effects. Aloe vera treatment showed 
OYVMV disease incidence to 39.34% at 60 days 
after transplanting, compared to 44.21% in the 
control. Similarly, turmeric treatment was showed 
OELCuV incidence to 23.52% at 60 days after 
transplanting, relative to 48.38% in the control. The 
highest yield was obtained from ginger treatment 
(2.42 tons/ha) compare to control (1.86 tons/ha). 
These findings suggest that botanical extracts may 
offer potential for integrated disease management 
and yield enhancement in okra cultivation.

Fertilizer management of cauliflower 
intercropping with garden pea system 
productivity, quality and nutrient uptake
M. A. Quddus, R. Ahmed, M. Ataur Rahman and 
Z.H. Fahad 
Intercropping cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. 
botrytis L.) with garden pea (Pisum sativum L.) 
is maximized system crop productivity, enhanced 
crop quality, and improved sustainable soil health. 
Consequently, a field experiment was executed 
during the 2024-2025 period at the research 
field of the Soil & Water Management Section, 
Horticulture Research Centre, BARI, Gazipur. The 
experiment utilized a Randomized Complete Block 
Design (RCBD) with three replications to evaluate 
eight distinct fertilizer and organic amendment 
treatments. The treatments were T 1: Control (No 
use of fertilizer), T 2: N 150P40K100S10Mg12Zn3B2 kg 
ha-1 for cauliflower, T 3: 3 t ha -1 vermicompost 
(VC)+100% of NPKSMgZnB, T 4: 5 t ha -1 
CD +100% of NPKSMgZnB, T 5: 3 t ha -1 VC 
+125% of NPKSMgZnB, T 6: 5 t ha -1 CD +125% 
of NPKSMgZnB, T 7: 3 t ha -1 VC+150% of 
NPKSMgZnB and T 8: 5 t ha -1 CD +150% of 
NPKSMgZnB. Results indicated that treatment T 5 
gave the highest cauliflower curd yield of 39.8 t ha-
1. The highest cauliflower equivalent yield (44.1 t 
ha-1) was also achieved in T 5, which was attributed 
to better growth characteristics and heavier curds.

Vegetable Crops I 119
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
Furthermore, T 5 produced the highest vitamin C 
content (41.0 mg/100 g for Cauliflower and 40.5 
mg/100g for garden pea). These findings suggest that 
a combination of 3 t ha -1 vermicompost and 125% 
of the recommended NPKSMgZnB fertilizer is an 
appropriate approach for successfully cultivating 
cauliflower intercropped with garden peas.
Foliar application of boron and boron 
nanoparticles on growth, yield, quality and 
nutrient use efficiency of cauliflower
M. A. Quddus, M. Ataur Rahman, R. Ahmed and M. 
S. Arfin
Cauliflower (Brassica oleracea var. botrytis L.) is 
responsive to boron fertilization. An experiment 
was conducted in winter season of 2023-24 
and 2024-25 to evaluate the effect of boron and 
boron nanoparticles on growth, yield traits, yield 
and quality of cauliflower. The experiment was 
planned with 5 treatments involving four levels 
of boron nanoparticles (0, 100, 200 and 300 ppm) 
and conventional boric acid @ 1 gL -1 following 
randomized complete block design with three 
replications. The result indicated that foliar 
application of 200 ppm boron nanoparticles 
produced the highest fresh curd yield (50.2 t ha -1) 
which was 88.7% higher than control. The treatment 
was responsible for higher individual curd weight 
(1761 g) and higher content of vitamin C (46.9 
mg/100g). The same treatment achieved higher total 
B uptake (0.578 kg ha-1) by cauliflower. The benefit 
cost ratio was maximum (6.69) in foliar application 
of 200 ppm boron nanoparticles. In contrast, the 
boron use efficiency was higher in foliar application 
of 100 ppm boron nanoparticles. Result suggests 
that foliar application of 200 ppm of B nanoparticles 
can be recommended for cauliflower cultivation.
Evaluation of yield potential of tomato genotypes 
under elevated fertilizer level
M. Ataur Rahman, M. A. Quddus and R. Ahmed
Tomatoes (Solanum lycopersium L.) are highly 
responsive to increased fertilizer application, 
leading to improved crop yield and quality. Hence, 
an experiment was conducted at the research 
field of Horticulture Research Centre (HRC), 
BARI during 2023-24 and 2024-25. Four levels 
of fertilizers viz. control, recommended dose of 
fertilizers (N 120P30K50S20), 150% of recommended

tomato genotypes, namely BARI Tomato -14, BARI 
Hybrid Tomato -8, BARI Hybrid Tomato -10, and 
AvTo-1314 were planted in the subplots following a 
split plot design with three replications. The results 
indicated that yield response to applied fertilizer was 
varied among the genotypes. The genotype BARI 
Hybrid Tomato -8 was more responsive to fertilizer 
that gave maximum yield (78.5 t/ha) under 150% 
recommended fertilizer with 10 t/ha cow-dung. 
The advanced line AvTo-1314 gave significantly 
higher yield compare to control. Infestation of blight 
disease was more severe in AvTo - 1314 causing 
fewer yields compare to other genotypes. Based 
on the higher fruit yield and having maximum fruit 
number per cluster, the tomato variety BARI Hybrid 
Tomato-8 can be recommended as a promising 
variety under elevated fertilizer level.

Post Harvest Technology Section
Determination of maturity indices and shelf life 
of sweet pepper var. BARI Mistimorich-2 
Z. H. Fahad, M. A. Rahman and M. S. Arfin
Sweet pepper (Capsicum annum L.) has emerged 
as a high-value crop in Bangladesh due to rising 
culinary demand. BARI released two varieties, 
BARI Mistimorich-1 and BARI Mistimorich-2, 
which turn red and yellow during ripening, 
respectively. Optimizing postharvest storage and 
determining appropriate harvesting time are essential 
for maximizing shelf life and returns. This study 
was aimed to determine the optimal harvesting 
time for sweet pepper var. BARI Mistimorich-2 
to maximize shelf life maintaining nutritional and 
marketable qualities. Six harvesting time based on 
days after anthesis (DAA) was employed, ranging 
from 45 to 60 DAA at three-day intervals. The 
experiment was laid out in a randomized complete 
block design (RCBD) with six treatments replicated 
thrice. Quality parameters including fruit weight, 
length, firmness, titratable acidity, ascorbic acid 
content, total soluble solids, and colour change were 
analyzed following standard methods. The average 
fruit weight and length increased with delayed 
harvest, while firmness decreased. Total soluble 
solids increased with ripening, and titratable acidity 
decreased as acid-to-sugar conversion approached 
maturity. Ascorbic acid content declined with 
delayed harvesting. Considering both pricing and 
storage life, fruits harvested at 51-54 DAA, when 
turned to yellow stage showed the shelf life about 13 
days were deemed appropriate for the market. 
Effect of harvesting time on the nutritional 
quality and shelf-life of sponge gourd
Z. H. Fahad, M. A. Rahman and M. S. Arfin
Sponge gourd (Luffa cylindrica) is a prevalent 
summer vegetable in Bangladesh, recognized 
for its nutritional value and numerous beneficial 
components. Although sponge gourds mature 
rapidly, optimizing maturity indices is essential to 
ensure both quality, postharvest management, storage 
and favourable market pricing. This experiment was 
conducted to investigate the effect of harvesting time 
on the nutritional quality and shelf-life of sponge 
gourd variety BARI Dhundol-1. A randomized 
complete block design was employed with six 
treatments based on days after anthesis (DAA), 
ranging from 07 to 12 DAA at one-day intervals. 
Physio-chemical properties including weight, 
length, firmness, titratable acidity, total soluble 
solids (TSS), and color change were determined 
following the standard methods weight and length 
increased steadily until 12 DAA, while TSS peaked 
at 11 DAA before declining. Firmness exhibited a 
two-phase pattern, and titratable acidity gradually 
decreased. Seed maturation and fiber formation were

Vegetable Crops I 121
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
closely linked, beginning at 11 DAA. The optimal 
harvest time for fresh vegetable consumption was 
identified as 8-10 DAA, when fruits reached their 
maximum size, high TSS, moderate firmness, and 
lacked fiber development. These findings provide 
a practical guide for determining harvest timing to 
balance market quality in sponge gourd cultivation.
Uniform and safe ripening of tomato using novel 
ethylene gas generator
M. A. Rahman and Z. H. Fahad
Tomato is a very important high-value commercial 
crop rich in different nutrients, which grown round 
the year in Bangladesh. Uneven ripening of tomato 
is a common problem in commercial marketing 
of this fruit. To address this problem, farmers and 
traders usually spray ethyphon solution on pre-
matured tomatoes with unknown concentration 
for force ripening of fruits, which is not permitted 
due health hazard. This experiment was undertaken 
to find out a suitable doze of ethyphon to generate 
ethylene gas, and its effect on the ripening process of 
mature-green tomato var. BARI Tomato-18. To get 
ethylene gas, a novel ethylene gas generator (EG) 
was prepared with a small plastic jar containing 2 
ml ethephon (48% SL ai) and 0.5g NaOH pellet. 
Matured-green tomatoes were harvested from the 
experimental field, brought to the laboratory and 
exposed to three different concentrations of ethyphon 
(2,4 and 6 mLm -3) in ripening chambers for 24h at 
18-20 °C and 70-75% RH. The experiment was laid 
out in a complete randomized design (CRD) with 
four treatments including controls replicated four. 
The EG was found highly effective in triggering the 
ripening process of tomato by day 4 of storage at 
20±1°C and 65-70% RH. More than 90% of treated 
fruits were uniformly ripened on day 6, increased the 
number rapidly reaching 100% on day 7 of storage. 
In contrast, 60% tomato under control treatment 
found ripened on day 6, which increased up to 100% 
on day 8 of storage. All quality parameters including 
external colour, TSS, vitamin C contents of ripe 
tomato found better, and marketable to the local as 
well distant markets.

Evaluation of pineapple germplasm
M. A. Haque and A. Alam
A study was conducted to evaluate the vegetative 
growth and yield performance of four pineapple 
germplasm accessions (Ac Joy-001, Ac Joy-002, 
Ac Joy-003, and Ac Joy-004). Vegetative growth 
parameters were recorded at 12 months after planting, 
while yield and yield-contributing characters were 
assessed at harvest. Highly significant differences 
were observed among the accessions for most 
vegetative and yield traits. Accession Ac Joy-004 
consistently exhibited superior vegetative growth, 
demonstrating the greatest plant height (85.20 cm), 
number of leaves (52.26), and length (68.80 cm) 
and width (5.18 cm) of the D leaf. This accession 
also produced the highest fruit weight (1950 kg 
with crown), fruit length (17.95 cm), and fruit 
width (12.73 cm), making it the most vigorous and 
highest-yielding accession in terms of total fruit 
mass. However, a trade-off was observed in other 
yield components. Ac Joy-002 was found to be the 
most efficient accession in terms of edible fruit, 
with a significantly higher edible portion percentage 
(70.61%) compared to all others. It also had the 
heaviest crown (276.66 g). No significant difference 
was found in TSS content among the accessions, 
with values ranging from 14.90% to 17.90%. The 
findings indicate that Ac Joy-004 is a promising 
accession for high fruit yield and vigorous growth, 
while Ac Joy-002 is highly suitable for uses where a 
high edible portion is desired. The results highlight 
the potential for selecting specific pineapple 
germplasm for different commercial and processing 
applications. 
Evaluation of exotic pineapple germplasm
M. A. Haque and A. Alam
This study presents the growth and yield parameters 
of an exotic pineapple germplasm. At 12 months 
after planting, the plants had an average height of 
60.45 cm and 40 leaves. The D leaf measured 49.50 
cm in length and 4.69 cm in width. Fruit weight 
averaged 1650 g with the crown and 1368 g without. 
The fruit exhibited a high total soluble solids (TSS) 
content of 17.90% and a 73% edible portion. The 
taste was characterized as very sweet, with golden 
yellow, crispy flesh. Notably, the germplasm 
exhibited resistance to pests and diseases, with 
no recorded infections or infestations in the field. 
These findings suggest that this exotic pineapple 
germplasm possesses favorable agronomic and fruit 
quality traits, making it a promising candidate for 
further research and cultivation.

m × 2.97 m) accordingly. Number of fruits per plant 
was higher in CS Hat 001 (142) than that of BARI 
Malta-1 (127). CS Hat 001 produced significantly 
heavier fruits (214 g) compared to BARI Malta-1 
(146 g). Fruit length and diameter were also larger 
in CS Hat 001 (6.96 cm and 7.10 cm) than in BARI 
Malta-1 (5.51 cm and 5.52 cm). Juice content was 
greater in CS Hat 001 (74 ml) compared to BARI 
Malta-1 (56 ml). Total soluble solids (TSS) was also 
higher in CS Hat 001 (9.5%) compared to BARI 
Malta-1 (9.0%).
Collection and eveluation of pomegranate (Punica 
granatum) genotypes in Chattogram region
M. N. Uddin, T. A. Mujahidi, M. S. Jeny, A. S. M. 
H. Rashid, S. M. Faisal and M. S. I. Khan
Pomegranate (Punica granatum L.) is a minor yet 
promising fruit crop in Bangladesh, known for 
its high-value juice and potential nutraceutical 
applications. In view of its growing market demand 
and medicinal significance, an exploratory study was 
undertaken at the Regional Agricultural Research 
Station (RARS), Hathazari, Chattogram during 
2024-2025. The objective was to enrich existing 
germplasm resources and establish grafted plants 
for future evaluation. A total of 12 genotypes were 
collected from 15 upazilas of Chattogram district 
and from commercial nurseries. The genotypes 
were screened, isolated for disease inspection, and 
subsequently established in the RARS orchard. All 
plants are currently in the early vegetative stage, and 
the experiment will continue to assess their growth, 
adaptability, and fruiting potential. This study 
lays the groundwork for future improvement and 
selection of superior pomegranate cultivars suited 
to the agro-climatic conditions of southeastern 
Bangladesh.
Hybridization for developing scion cultivars in 
citrus
F. Ahmed, J. C. Sarker and M. H. M. B. Bhuyan
A hybridization program was carried out among the 
available citrus genotypes during the flowering season 
of 2024-25 at the Citrus Research Station (CRS), 
BARI, Jaintapur, Sylhet for developing new hybrid 
citrus scion cultivars. Six selected genotypes of 
citrus variety were used for hybridization. Maximum 
numbers of successful crosses (14) were obtained 
from BARI Batabilebu-3(♂)×BARI Batabilebu-5(♀). 
The highest percentage of fruit setting (36%) 
was recorded from the cross combination BARI 
Komla-1(♂)× BARI Komla-3(♀), while the lowest 
(10%) was recorded for BARI Komla-3(♂)×BARI 
Malta-1(♀). Maximum number of fruit retention 
(7) was recorded from the crosses between BARI 
Batabilebu-3(♂)×BARI Batabilebu-5(♀) followed 
by BARI Komla-3(♂)×BARI Malta-1(♀) and BARI 
Batabilebu-5(♂)×BARI Batabilebu-3(♀), whereas, no 
fruit was retained in the rest of the cross combinations.

Evaluation of bullock's heart germplasm
M. A. Haque and A. Alam
A study was conducted to assess the genetic 
diversity of five bullock's heart germplasm 
accessions collected from local markets. The 
accessions, designated AR Joy-001 to AR Joy-005, 
were evaluated for a range of morphological and 
biochemical characteristics, including fruit weight, 
fruit dimensions, Total Soluble Solids (TSS), seed 
count, seed dimensions, total seed weight, skin 
weight, and edible portion percentage. The results 
showed variability across most traits. The mean 
fruit weight was 334.44 g, with a high coefficient of 
variation (CV) of 27.73%, while the edible portion 
had a mean of 80.01% with a low CV of 6.66%. 
Accession AR Joy-002 recorded the highest fruit 
weight (498.70 g) and edible portion (88.79%). In 
contrast, AR Joy-001 and AR Joy-003 exhibited 
the highest TSS content (26% Brix), a key indicator 
of sweetness. However, AR Joy-003 also had the 
highest number of seeds (85). The findings suggest 
a valuable genetic diversity within the local market 
germplasm, highlighting promising accessions like 
AR Joy-002 for breeding programs focused on 
increasing fruit size and yield, and AR Joy-001 and 
AR Joy-003 for improving fruit sweetness. These 
results provide a foundation for further selection and 
breeding efforts to develop superior bullock's heart 
varieties.

Collection and eveluation of custard apple 
(Annona squamosa) genotypes in Chattogram 
region
T. A. Mujahidi, M. N. Uddin, M. S. Jeny, A. S. M. 
H. Rashid, S. M. Faisal and M. S. I. Khan
Custard apple (Annona squamosa), a minor yet highly 
valued fruit crop in Bangladesh, is renowned for its 
rich, creamy taste and nutritional benefits. Despite 
its popularity, there has been limited systematic 
collection and evaluation of its genetic resources in 
the country. With an aim to identifying and conserve 
superior genotypes for future cultivation and 
commercial exploitation, a preliminary investigation 
was initiated during 2024-2025 at the Regional 
Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Hathazari, 
Chattogram. A total of 22 custard apple genotypes 
were collected from 15 upazilas within Chattogram 
district. These genotypes were initially characterized 
for fruit traits, and seedlings were established in the 
RARS fruit orchard for further evaluation. As of 
now, all plants are in the early vegetative stage, and 
the trial will be continued for growth, phenological, 
and yield assessments in the upcoming seasons.

Project II: Propagation Technique
Propgation of BARI Komola-1 and BARI Malta-1 
by shoot tip grafting
M. H. M. B. Bhuyan, J. C. Sarker, and F. Ahmed
The experiment was conducted at Citrus Research 
Station, BARI, Jaintapur, Sylhet from September 
2024 to May 2025. Shoot tip grafting of BARI 
Komola-1 and BARI Malta-1 was done on local 
pummelo rootstocks. Seedlings of local pummelo 
were raised in soil less culture fortified with basal 
MS medium in standard conditions of temperature, 
light duration and plant age. Scions collected from 
BARI Komola-1 and BARI Malta-1 mother plants 
were in vitro grown in solidified MS media in 
standard conditions of temperature, light duration 
and microbud age. Results suggested that rootstock 
seedlings showed optimum growth at 30°C with 
complete darkness, whereas optimum growth of the 
microbud was found in 25°C with 16/8h light/dark 
cycle. Shoot tips (0.2 mm long), were aseptically 
excised from the microbuds and were grafted onto 
the decapitated rootstock seedlings. The micrografts 
were grown in culture medium under standard 
condition. Only 6.66% of BARI Malta-1 grafts 
were successful. The grafts will be indexed for 
graft transmissible diseases further. The experiment 
will be continued in the following year to get more 
disease free saplings. 
Effect of method of propagation on survivability 
and growth of Coffee Robusta 
J. C. Sarker, M. H. M. B. Bhuyan, F. Ahmed, and S. 
M. L. Rahman
The experiment was conducted during 2023-24 
at the Citrus Research Station, BARI, Jaintapur,

136 I Fruit Crops
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
Sylhet, to identify an effective vegetative 
propagation technique for Coffee Robusta. Three 
grafting methods including softwood grafting, semi-
hardwood grafting, and side grafting were evaluated. 
The study followed a Completely Randomized 
Design (CRD) with three replications, using 10 
seedlings per treatment. Data were collected on 
plant survival percentage, growth of rootstock and 
scion, number of branches, and number of leaves 
per graft. The results revealed significant differences 
among the treatments. Softwood grafting exhibited 
superior performance, with the highest survival rate 
(68.23%), longest rootstock length (2.80 cm at 120 
days after grafting), greatest number of branches per 
graft (2.16), and maximum number of leaves per 
graft (21.91). In contrast, side grafting consistently 
produced the lowest values across all parameters. 
The study concluded that softwood grafting offers 
better compatibility with the rootstock and is the 
most effective propagation method for Coffee 
robusta under the conditions of the northeastern 
hilly region of Bangladesh.
Standardization of grafting time and techniques 
in cashew nut under Bangladesh condition
J. C. Sarker, M. H. M. B. Bhuyan, F. Ahmed, and S. 
M. L. Rahman
An experiment was conducted during 2023-24 
at the Citrus Research Station, BARI, Jaintapur, 
Sylhet, to determine the most effective vegetative 
propagation technique and optimal grafting time 
for cashew nut. Two grafting methods including 
cleft and veneer grafting were evaluated across 12 
grafting dates at mid-month intervals throughout 
the year. The study followed a factorial arrangement 
in a Completely Randomized Design (CRD) with 
three replications, using 10 seedlings per treatment. 
Data were collected on days to bud break, graft 
success rate, graft survivability, number of leaves 
per graft, and number of shoots per graft. Results 
showed that the interaction between grafting time 
and technique significantly influenced bud break 
and shoot production. The shortest time to bud 
break (17.99 days) and highest shoot number (6.14) 
were recorded with cleft grafting on June 15, while 
the longest bud break (29.78 days) and lowest 
shoot count (2.44) occurred with veneer grafting on 
January 15. Although graft success, survivability, 
and leaf number were not significantly affected by 
the interaction, cleft grafting in June consistently 
yielded the best overall results. In contrast, veneer 
grafting in December and January performed poorly 
across most parameters. The study concluded that 
cleft grafting on June 15 was the most effective 
method for cashew propagation in the northeastern 
hilly region of Bangladesh, while veneer grafting in 
December and January showed poor results.

Pest status and population dynamics of mango 
thrips
G. M. M. Bari and M. M. Rahman
Thrips are persistent pests of mango and 
understanding the dynamics in relation to weather 
factors could be useful for effective IPM. These 
studies done for five years old trees (2024-25) on 
mango revealed that peak incidence of thrips was 
open flowering stage of plant (32.1 thrips/panicle), 
and preference found at new flushing stage (5.9 
thrips/leaf bunch) also. Population density of thrips 
was significantly more abundant in the upper parts 
(9.6 number/leaf bunch) of tree. Mango thrips 
incidence had significant positive correlation with 
maximum average temperature (p<0.01), and 
negatively influenced with relative humidity (RH) 
and rainfall (p<0.01).This validated regression 
model might help IPM decision.

Post Harvest Technology Section
Uniform ripening of mango (Var. BARI Aam-
3) managing quality and food safety using novel 
ethylene gas generator
M. A. Rahman and Z. H. Fahad
Uneven ripening commonly occurs during the 
natural ripening process, posing a significant 
problem, especially for commercial marketing of 
fresh fruits and vegetables. Artificial ripening is the 
process by which ripening is controlled to achieve 
desired characteristics intended for better consumer 
acceptance and improving sales. BARI Aam-3 is one 
of the important commercial varieties in Bangladesh. 
However, like other mangoes, fruits of BARI Aam-
3 do not ripe uniformly, which makes problem in 
marketing the fruit properly. Fruit growers and 
traders on the other hand, usually spray ethyphon 
or calcium carbide for force ripening of fruits, 
which is not permitted because of health hazard. 
This experiment was undertaken to standardize the 
dozes of ethyphon along with standard protocol for 
uniform and safe ripening of mango var. BARI Aam-
3 using low-cost novel ethylene gas generator (EG). 
To prepare the ripening chamber, one cubic meter 
(1m x 1m x 1m) bamboo structure was made along 
with a piece of high-density polyethylene film. Each 
EG was prepared with a small piece of cotton, 02 
ml of ethephon (48% SL) and 0.5g NaOH. Matured-
green mangoes were harvested from the HRC fruit 
orchard, brought to the laboratory and exposed to 
three different concentrations of ethyphon (2,4 and 
6 mLm-3) in ripening chambers for 24h at 18-20 °C 
and 70-75% RH. The experiment was laid out in a 
CRD with five treatments including two controls 
replicated four. All EGs containing 2, 4 or 6 mL 
ethyphon found highly effective in initiating the 
ripening process of fruits within 24h. About 100% 
of fruits treated even with the lowest concentration 
of ethyphon (2 mL) were uniformly ripened after 
48h of treatment application at 20±1°C and 65-70% 
RH. Control fruits, on the other hand started to ripe 
after 48h, increased thereafter reaching 100% after 
72h. All quality parameters including flesh colour, 
TSS, vitamin C contents of ripe mangoes found 
better and acceptable for marketing to the local as 
well distant markets. It is an environmentally safe, 
low-cost and affordable technology that can be 
used by all categories of farmers and fruit traders in 
Bangladesh.
Uniform ripening of mango (Var. BARI Aam-
4) managing quality and food safety using novel 
ethylene gas generator
M. A. Rahman and Z. H. Fahad
Different fruits like mango, banana, jackfruit, 
papaya etc. should be ripened properly both for 
fresh consumption and minimal processing to get 
optimum aroma, sweetness, taste and eating quality. 
BARI Aam-4 is one of the mega commercial 
varieties in Bangladesh grown widely across the 
country. However, fruits of this variety took longer 
for ripening, especially when produced with pre-
harvest fruit-bagging technique. Therefore, this

and safe ripening of matured-green mango using

a piece of high-density polyethylene film. Novel EG

ethephon (48% SL) and 0.5g NaOH. Matured-green 
mangoes were harvested from the fruit orchard of 
HRC at maturity stage-2, brought to the laboratory 
and exposed them to three different concentrations 
of ethyphon (2,4 and 6 mLm-3) in ripening chambers 
for 24h at 18-20 °C and 70-75% RH. The experiment 
was laid out in a CRD with five treatments including 
two controls. The ethylene gas (C 2H4) generated 
from the ethephon-based EG inside the ripening 
chamber found highly effective in onset the ripening 
process of mango within 48h. Almost 100% of 
ethyphon-treated fruits were uniformly ripened after 
60h of treatment application at 20±1°C and 65-70% 
RH. In contrast, the ripeness of absolute control 
and control fruits was initiated after 60h of storage

exhibiting 20.9 and 33.3% ripe fruits, respectively 
after 72h, increased thereafter reaching 100% after 
96h after storage. All quality parameters including 
flesh colour, TSS, vitamin C contents of ripe 
mangoes found better and acceptable for marketing 
to the local as well distant markets.
Extending the green life of plantain banana by 
1-methylcyclopropene
M. A. Rahman and Z. H. Fahad
Plantain (Musa paradisiaca L.) is an important 
commercial crop that grown across the world 
including Bangladesh. In Bangladesh, this banana 
is known as "cooking banana", which is generally 
used as curry at its green stage. But being perishable 
nature, the green life of this banana loss quickly 
after harvest, which is a barrier to marketing the 
crop in distant markets. To address this problem, an 
experiment was undertaken to evaluate the efficacy 
of aqueous 1-methylcyclopropene (1-MCP) on 
retaining the green life of plantain banana. Mature 
green fruits were harvested at stage-2, brought to the 
laboratory and immersed in 1-MCP solutions at 100, 
200, or 300 μg L−1 for 10 min, air-dried, packed in 
0.5% perforated low-density polyethylene film, and 
stored at 18-20 °C and 70-75% RH for 30 days. The 
experiment was laid out in a complete randomized 
design (CRD) with four treatments including 
control. All concentrations of 1-MCP showed 
greater effect in suppressing ethylene evolution 
compared to control treatment during the stipulated 
storage period. 1-MCP treatments even at lowest 
concentration (100 μgL -1) retained the maximum 
tissue firmness of 13.5 N and green skin colour at 
the end of 30 days storage, and extended storage life 
by at least five days compared to control without 
compromising peel appearance, pulp texture and 
other quality parameters.

M. T. Rashid, F. N. Khan, N. Pervin, K. Ambia,

A field experiment was conducted from October

Horticulture Research Centre, BARI, Gazipur, to 
evaluate the agronomic and floral performance of ten 
gladiolus genotypes, including BARI Gladiolus-1 
as a check. The genotypes were evaluated under a 
randomized complete block design (RCBD) with 
three replications. Significant variation was observed 
among genotypes in terms of spike length, floret 
number, rachis length, spike weight, and shelf life. 
Genotypes GL-025 and GL-002 recorded the highest 
floret number per spike (15), while GL-025 also 
produced the longest spike (95.0 cm), highest spike 
weight (60.0 g), and longest shelf life (9 days). GL-
037 showed similar performance in terms of spike 
length (90.0 cm), floret number (14.5), and yield 
(230,000 spikes/ha). Early flowering was observed 
in GL-003 (47 days to 50% spike initiation). All 
genotypes exhibited moderate tolerance to leaf blight, 
with no significant insect infestation reported. Based 
on overall floral traits, earliness, and post-harvest 
shelf life, GL-002, GL-012, GL-025, and GL-037 
were identified as promising lines for commercial 
cut flower production and potential variety release 
under Bangladesh agro-climatic conditions.

N. Pervin, F. N. Khan, M. R. R. Bhuyin, K. Ambia,

identifying TR-020 and TR-021 as superior for

Collection, evaluation and maintenance of water 
lily
N. T. Hasan, F.N. Khan, N. Pervin, K. Ambia, M. M. 
R. Bhuyin and M.T. Rashid
A study was conducted during August 2025 to June 
2026 at the Floriculture Research Field, HRC, BARI, 
Gazipur, to evaluate the morphological diversity and 
flowering performance of twenty native and hybrid 
Nymphaea (water lily) germplasms. The experiment 
revealed significant variations in flower diameter, 
durability, and number of flowers per plant. Larger 
flowers (>10 cm) were recorded in native accessions 
N-001 and N-002 and in hybrid lines N-010, N-014, 
N-019, N-022, and N-023. The highest flower count 
per plant was observed in N-021 (15.0), while

genotypes maintained floral durability for 3 days,

diversity within the evaluated germplasm. The 
findings highlight promising candidates such as 
N-005, N-012, N-014, and N-021 for breeding, 
ornamental cultivation, and future conservation 
programs. Continued collection and evaluation of

Hybridization in gladiolus flower
F.N. Khan, N. T. Hasan, K. Ambia, N. Pervin, 
M.M.R. Bhyyin and Mt. Rashid
A long-term hybridization program was carried out 
at the Floriculture Research Field, HRC, BARI, 
Gazipur from November 2016 to June 2025 to 
develop new hybrid gladiolus lines with improved 
ornamental traits. A total of twenty controlled crosses 
were performed among visually attractive gladiolus 
genotypes. All crosses successfully produced pods, 
which matured within 30-45 days. Seeds from each 
cross generated a large number of cormels, which 
were planted and maintained annually to develop 
flowering-sized corms. Successive evaluations 
revealed significant variation among the F1 hybrids 
in vegetative and floral characteristics. Among 
the twenty hybrids, GL hybrid 5 recorded the 
highest spike length (105.5 cm), while GL hybrid 
13 produced the maximum number of florets per 
spike (15.5). Notably, GL hybrid 35 exhibited the 
heaviest flower stick weight (130 g), and GL hybrid 
3 produced the largest single corm weight (85.8 g). 
Considerable genetic variation was confirmed by 
high coefficients of variation in traits such as flower 
stick weight (34.60%), corm weight (27.79%), and 
floret diameter (8.78%). Based on floral morphology, 
spike characteristics, and corm production, several 
hybrids including GL hybrid 5, GL hybrid 13, and 
GL hybrid 35 were identified as promising lines for 
future varietal development and commercialization.

Cultural management
Standardization of potting media for better 
growth and yield of dendrobium orchid
N. T. Hasan , F.N. Khan, N. Pervin, K. Ambia, M. 
M. R. Bhuyin and M.T. Rashid 
The study was conducted at the Floriculture Field 
of the Horticulture Research Centre, Bangladesh 
Agricultural Research Institute during 2025-2026 
to evaluate the effect of different potting media on 
the growth and flowering of Dendrobium orchid. The 
experiment was laid out in a Completely Randomized 
Design with six treatments replicated three times using 
two-month-old seedlings. Treatments comprised 
T1: Charcoal + Coconut Husk (50:50), T2: Coconut 
Husk + Brick (50:50), T3: Charcoal + Brick (50:50), 
T4: Charcoal (100%), T5: Coconut Husk (100%), and 
T6: Brick (100%). Data on vegetative (plant height, 
number of leaves, leaf area) and reproductive (spike 
length, number of flowers, number of inflorescences) 
traits were recorded and analyzed statistically. 
Significant differences were observed among potting 
media for all measured parameters. The mixture of 
Charcoal and Coconut Husk (50:50) (T1) produced 
the highest plant height (16.0 cm), number of leaves 
(9.6), leaf area (40.0 cm2), spike length (20.0 cm), 
number of flowers per plant (12.7), and number 
of inflorescences (2.0), whereas Coconut Husk 
alone (T5) recorded the lowest values for most 
parameters. The findings indicate that a potting 
medium comprising Charcoal and Coconut Husk in 
equal proportion provides optimal conditions for the 
growth and flowering of Dendrobium orchid under 
shade-net house conditions.
Foliar application of flora on growth and 
flowering of chrysanthemum
N. T. Hasan , F.N. Khan, N. Pervin, K. Ambia, M. 
M. R. Bhuyin and M.T. Rashid
A field experiment was conducted at the Floriculture 
Research Field of Horticulture Research Centre 
(HRC), BARI, Gazipur during 2025 to evaluate 
the effects of foliar application of Flora Hormone 
on the growth and flowering performance of 
Chrysanthemum morifolium (CM-011). The 
study followed a factorial Randomized Complete 
Block Design (RCBD) with three replications, 
incorporating four hormone concentrations (0, 1, 
2, and 3 mL/L) and two application intervals (15 
and 25 days). Significant variation was observed in 
both vegetative and floral traits across treatments. 
The application of 2 mL/L Flora Hormone (A3), 
particularly at 15-day intervals (B1), resulted in the 
best vegetative growth, producing the tallest plants 
(31.0 cm), largest leaf area (6.0 cm2), and highest 
number of branches (4.9). This treatment also led to 
the earliest bud initiation (60 days), earliest flowering 
(75 days), largest flower diameter (4.9 cm), and 
highest flower count per plant (9.5). Statistical 
analysis confirmed significant effects of both 
hormone concentration and spray interval, as well as 
their interaction, on all parameters. These findings 
suggest that foliar application of Flora Hormone at 
2 mL/L every 15 days optimizes vegetative growth

(S1V2-S1V5), Light Pink and Magenta cultivars

under protected environments in Bangladesh.

Sustainable practices and adoption challenges in 
rose and gladiolus flower farming in Bangladesh
R. Islam
This study examined the sustainability and adoption 
challenges of rose and gladiolus cultivation in 
major flower-producing districts of Bangladesh-
Rangpur, Jashore, and Cox's Bazar. Findings 
showed that floriculture, especially rose farming, 
was a profitable enterprise with favorable benefit-
cost ratios (BCRs exceeding 1.00 across districts). 
However, profitability is largely achieved through 
heavy reliance on chemical fertilizers, pesticides, 
and costly planting materials, which threatens long-
term soil health and environmental sustainability. 
Adoption of sustainable practices such as integrated 
pest management (IPM), organic fertilizers, efficient 
irrigation, and improved post-harvest handling 
remains moderate to low. Farmers generally 
recognized the benefits of soil health and profitability 
from sustainability but are less convinced of IPM's 
effectiveness and cost-reducing potential. Barriers 
to adoption included high input costs, lack of 
quality seedlings and bulbs, limited access to 
credit, weak extension and training services, and 
climate-induced risks, particularly in coastal areas. 
Regional differences are evident: Jashore shows 
higher productivity and profitability due to better 
market linkages and training, while Cox's Bazar 
faces major constraints in institutional support and 
climate-related vulnerabilities.

Efficacy of fungicides on botrytis blight of lilium
L. Yasmin, M. Afroz and M. M. Rahman, M. S. Ali 
and F. N. Khan 
The experiment was conducted at Floriculture 
research field of Horticulture Research Centre, 
BARI, Gazipur during December 2024 to March 
2025 to find out effective fungicides to manage 
the botrytis blight disease of lilium. Among the 
treatments, the lowest plant mortality (14.47%), 
incidence (60.0%) and PDI (18.0%) was found in T2 
treatment (Rovral 2gm/l) followed by T 1 treatment 
(Amistar top 1 ml/l), T 3 treatment(Autostin 2 
gm/1) and T 4 (Luna sensation 2 ml/1) where plant 
mortality, disease incidence and PDI were18.41%, 
21.0%, 23.27%; 65.0%d, 70.0%c, 75.0% and18.0%, 
20.0%, 25.0%, respectively. The highest rachis 
length 42.27cm obtained from T 2 followed by T 3 
(37.27cm), T4 (37.0cm) and T1 (36.0cm). The lowest 
rachis length 35.0cm and highest plant mortality 
(25.0%), incidence (90.0%) and PDI (50.0%) 
recorded in control treatment.

Introgression of recessive nud gene by 
combination of marker assisted breeding for 
hulless barley
Z. A. Talukder, A. Tabassum, M. M. Billah and R. 
Sultana
The hulless trait of barley was reported to be 
controlled by a17-kb deletion harboring the entire 
ethylene response factor (ERF) gene on the nud 
locus that resides on the barley chromosome 7HL.
In the present study, two hulled barley genotypes 
(BARI Barley-5 and IBON19) were targeted for 
the marker-assisted introgression of nud allele and 
convert to hulless. Two hulled barley viz., BARI 
Barley-5 and IBON19 were used as recurrent 
parents and two hulless barley viz., BARI Barley-7 
and BARI Barley-9 were used as donor parents. 
Two recurrent parents were crossed with two donor 
parents in rabi season 2023-24 at BARI, Gazipur and 
produced 490 F1 seed. In 2024-25, total 464 true F 1 
plant was identified with nud gene specific marker. 
True F1 plant crossed with two recurrent parents and 
produced 790 BC1F1 seed.

Advanced yield trial of barley (Set-I)
Z. A. Talukder, S. Mondal, H. M. K. Bashar, K. 
Isalm and R. Sultana
Seven barley lines including two checks were 
evaluated at saline area (Satkhira, Khulna and 
Patuakhali) and non-saline area (Gazipur). The 
superior and stable genotypes were identified with 
GGE biplot and AMMI (Additive main effects 
and multiplicative interaction) models. Significant 
variation was observed among the lines and 
locations for all the traits. Based on results, grain 
yield was significantly dependent on environments 
(E), genotypes (G), and GEI. Significant yield 
reduction was recorded in almost all genotypes 
in saline environment compared to non-saline 
condition; however, some salttolerant genotypes 
showed minimal reduction in yield. BHL-33 
produced highest yield in saline (2.6 t/ha) and non-
saline condition (3.0t/ha) followed by BARI Barley 
-10 (Non-saline:2.7 t/ha; Saline:2.4 t/ha.) AMMI 
and GGE biplot analysis revealed that the BHL-
33 and BB-10 genotype were selected under saline 
and non-saline condition. Among the lines, BHL-
33 exhibited high K+/Na+ ratio and antioxidant 
enzymatic activity. Considering yield, K+/Na+ ratio 
and antioxidant enzymatic activity, BHL-33 were 
selected r as candidate variety.

Preliminary yield trial of sorghum genotypes for

Z. A. Talukder, M. M. Billah, A. Tabassum, M. S.

Waterlogging is one of the most important constraints 
for sorghum production and productivity in kharif-2 
season in Bangladesh. A total 10 sorghum genotypes 
were evaluated at Gazipur during May 2025 with the 
aim to select excess soil moisture tolerant sorghum 
genotypes. Water was imposed at pre-flowering

waterlogged condition. The experiment is still in the 
field. Data recording of yield and yield contributing 
characters are going on.

Screening of barley genotypes (Hordeum vulgare 
L.) for drought tolerance at seedling stage on the 
basis of morphology using peg
S. Begum, M. M. Billah, Z. A. Talukder, A. H. Akhi, 
A. Tabassum, R. Sultana
Drought stress plays a pivotal role in plant 
growth. In order to evaluate PEG 6000-mediated 
water stress in barley (Hordeum vulgare) lines, a 
germination experiment was conducted. The seeds 
of 28 barley F 5 generation lines were subjected to 
PEG 6000 osmoticum and created five levels of 
osmotic stresses: T 1: Control (distilled water), T 2: 
5% PEG 6000 (-0.05 MPa), T 3: 10% PEG 6000 
(-0.15 MPa), T4: 15% PEG 6000 (-0.30 MPa), and 
T5: 20% PEG 6000 (-0.49 MPa). On the 7th day of 
treatment, data was taken on various germination 
parameters. The PEG stress treatments significantly 
changed the germination percent, root number, root 
length, plumule length, relative germination ratio 
(RGR), relative water content (RWC), and seedling 
vigor index (SVI). Of all the studied lines, based 
on their performance, it is concluded that barley 
lines such as P32, P42, P46, and P50 are found 
to be potential against drought stress over PEG 
treatments.

BRAC and Hajari) grown in Bangladesh. The result 
revealed that the SCAR-W11-F and SCAR-W11-R 
markers were very useful for detecting male and 
hermaphrodite of eight studied papaya cultivars, 
by giving the accurate PCR product approximately 
830bp length in male and hermaphrodite but not 
in female. Furthermore, the new designed markers 
(PH2-F and PH1-R), were successfully useful to 
determine only in hermaphrodite of all validated 
papaya cultivars, by generating the PCR product 
(approximately 101bp length). These indicated that 
both molecular markers were greatly beneficial and 
valuable to identify the sex types of papaya plants at 
an early seedling stage.

Effect of boron fertilization on yield and quality 
of BARI sarisha-18
J.A. Chowdhury, S. S. Kakon, M. R. Karim and M. 
A. K. Mian
A field experiment was conducted at Agronomy 
research field of Bangladesh Agricultural Research 
Institute, Joydebpur, Gazipur, during Rabi season 
of 2024-2025 to find out the appropriate amount 
of boron fertilizer for optimum yield of BARI 
Sarisha-18. The experiment was comprised of 6 
treatments viz. T 1= Control (no boron applied); 
T2=1.5 kg/ha boron; T 3=1.75 kg/ha boron; T 4=2.0 
kg/ha boron; T 5=2.25 kg/ha boron and T 6=. 2.5 
kg/ha boron. The soil of the research area belongs 
to the Chhihata series under AEZ-28. Soils of the 
experimental plots were collected and analyzed. The 
soil was clay loam with pH 5.90 (slightly acidic), 
OC 1.44% (very low), total N 0.124% (very low), 
exchangeable K 0.0121 meq/100g soil (very low), 
available P 59.27 μg/mg (optimum), available S 
31.16 μg/g (optimum), available Zn 0.474 μg/g 
(low) and available B 0.249 μg/g (very low). Organic 
carbon and Zn were under critical level in the soil. 
The experiment was laid out in a Randomized 
Complete Block Design (RCBD) with three 
replications. The unit plot size was 4.2 m × 3 m. The 
soil of experimental plots were fertilized at the rate 
of 120-36-90-27-3 kg/ha N P K S Zn (FRG,2018) as 
urea, triple super phosphate (TSP), muriate of potash 
(MoP), gypsum and zinc sulphate. Boron fertilizer 
was applied as boric acid according to experimental 
treatment set up. Half of N and all other fertilizer 
was applied as basal during final land preparation 
and rest N was applied as top dress at the time of 
flower initiation stage (25 days after sowing). Seeds 
were sown on 14 November, 2024 at the rate of 7 kg/
ha seed and crop was harvested at 23 February 2024. 
Intercultural operations such as weeding, thinning, 
irrigation, spraying of insecticides and weedicides 
were done uniformly. For recording dry matter five 
plants from each replication were sampled at 30, 
45, 60, 75, 90 DAS and at harvest. Different plant 
parts of the collected samples were separated and 
then oven dried at 80 0C for 72 hours. At harvesting 
stage, randomly 10 sample plants were uprooted 
from each unit plot to collect data on different yield 
contributing characters. Yield data was recorded by 
harvesting whole plot area excluding border line. 
Collected data were analyzed and the means were 
adjudged by using LSD at 5% level of significance. 
Cost and return analysis was also done considering 
local market price of harvested crop. Results 
indicated that yield and yield attributes of mustard 
were significantly influenced by boron application. 
The effects of boron were significant on number of 
siliqua/plant, number of seeds/siliqua, seed yield, 
1000-seed weight and harvest index (%). The highest 
number of siliqua/plant (130.13), number of seeds/
siliqua (25.90), and 1000-seed weight (3.83 g) were 
obtained from the treatment T 6 (2.5 kg/ha boron). 
The highest seed yield (2666.67 kg/ha) was also 
found in the treatment T 6 (2.5 kg/ha boron) but all 
those parameters produced the statistically identical 
data in T 5 (2.25 kg/ha boron) Treatment. The seed 
yield was positively and significantly correlated with 
the yield contributing characters viz. siliqua/plant, 
seed/siliqua, and 1000-seed weight, but not with 
plant height and siliqua length. This result showed 
that boron had positive influence on reproductive 
development. Therefore, application of B @ 2.25 
kg/ha is a good option to increase yield and yield 
contributing characters of BARI Sarisha-18.
Enhancement of zinc and iron micronutrients in 
potato through agronomic biofortification
M. A. H. Khan, S. S. Kakon, J. A. Chowdhury, M. R 
Karim, M.A. K. Mian and M. Z. Ali
Various approaches such as bio-fortification, 
nutrient supplementation, fortification and diet 
diversification have been implemented in order to

158 I Agronomy
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
overcome micronutrient malnutrition. However, 
bio-fortification is considered as a long term and 
efficient method over the others due to the lack of 
socio-economic infrastructure. Agronomic bio-
fortification refers to the use of mineral fertilizers to 
improve concentration of nutrients in edible crops 
and also positively effects the crop yield. The field 
experiment was conducted at the agronomy research 
field of Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute, 
(BARI), Gazipur during Rabi season of 2024-
2025 to assess the influence of foliar application 
of Zn and Fe on yield and nutrient concentration of 
potato. The experiment was laid out in a randomized 
compete block design with three replications. Soil 
sample were collected from the research field and 
soil analysis was determined in the Soil Science 
Division Laboratory, BARI, Gazipur. The treatment 
of the experiment were: T 1= RDF (control), T 2= 
RDF + Chelated Zn 4g/L foliar spray at 25 and 50 
DAP, T3= RDF + ZnSO4 15 kg/ha at basal dose , T4= 
RDF + FeSO4 5g/L foliar spray at 50 DAP, T5= RDF 
+ FeSO 4 5g/L foliar spray at 50 DAP + Chelated 
Zn 4g/L foliar spray at 25 and 50 DAP,T 6= RDF 
+ FeSO4 5g/L foliar spray at 50 DAP + ZnSO 4 15 
kg/ha at basal dose. Chelated Zn and FeSO 4 was 
dissolved in respected amount of water for foliar 
application. The unit plot size was 3.6 m × 3.0 m. 
The crop was fertilized with 135-30-135-15-4-
1 kg/ha of NPKS Zn and B and cow-dung 5 t/ha, 
respectively (FRG,2018). All of organic manure, P, 
S, Zn and B and half of N and K should be applied 
as basal during final land preparation. Remaining 
half N and K should be applied at side dressing at 
30 DAP during earthing up operation. Potato tubers 
were sown on 13 December 2024 with spacing of 
60 cm × 25 cm and harvested on 16 March 2025. 
At harvest the number of tubers/plant, the weight of 
tubers/plant and the tuber weight were evaluated as 
yield components and tuber sample were collected 
for micro-nutrient determination. Ten tubers were 
collected as representative samples from selected 
tubers of each treatment and replicated for the analysis 
of micronutrients and dry matter. During processing 
the fresh weight of potato was recorded and at the 
end of drying the exact weight of the dry samples 
was collected to calculate the dry matter content. 
Data on yield and yield contributing characters 
were taken and statistically analyzed following 
Statistix-10 software package. Means were adjusted 
by LSD test at 5% level of significance. The higher 
tuber yield and higher concentration of Zn and Fe 
was found in T 3 (RDF + ZnSO 4 15 kg/ha at basal 
dose), T 2 (RDF + Chelated Zn 4g/L foliar spray 
at 25 and 50 DAP), T 6 (RDF + FeSO 4 5g/L foliar 
spray at 50 DAP + ZnSO 4 15 kg/ha at basal dose) 
and T5 (RDF + FeSO 4 5g/L foliar spray at 50 DAP 
+ Chelated Zn 4g/L foliar spray at 25 and 50 DAP). 
The result revealed that, the higher tuber yield, the 
higher Zn and Fe concentration of potato tuber was 
achieved in treatment T5 (RFD + FeSO 4 5g/L foliar 
spray at 50 DAP + Chelated Zn 4g/L foliar spray at 
25 and 50 DAP). The result of this study might be 
used to further biofortification efforts and decrease 
nutritional deficiencies.
Effect of agroclimatic factors on BARI Begun-12
M. R. Karim, J. A. Chowdhury, S. S. Kakon, S. T. 
Zannat and M. A. K. Mian
A field experiment was conducted at the Agronomy 
Division, Bangladesh Agricultural Research 
Institute (BARI), Gazipur during the Rabi season 
of 2024-25 to evaluate how variations in sowing 
time and agroclimatic conditions influence the 
growth and yield of BARI Begun-12, and to 
develop a predictive model for yield forecasting 
under changing climates. The experiment consisted 
of four sowing dates-10 October (D 1), 20 October 
(D2), 30 October (D 3), and 10 November (D 4) laid 
out in a Randomized Complete Block Design with 
three replications. Standard agronomic practices 
were followed and detailed phenological events 
and yield data were collected. Climatic data 
(temperature, rainfall, humidity, and sunshine hours 
were collected from the BARI Agro-meteorological 
Station, Gazipur). Results revealed that sowing date 
significantly affected the phenology and productivity 
of BARI Begun-12. Early sowing (10-20 October) 
led to shorter duration to flowering and fruiting set 
but produced the highest fruit yield (746.62 and 
723.47 g/plant, respectively), as these plantings 
coincided with favorable maximum temperatures 
(28-30°C), higher sunshine duration (7-8 h/day) 
and greater thermal time accumulation (Growing 
Degree Days, GDD). In contrast, delayed sowing 
(30 October-10 November) was exposed to cooler 
temperatures at early stage, higher relative humidity 
(>80%) and occasional rainfall (>40 mm), leading to 
delayed flowering, reduced fruit set and lower yields 
(566-568 g/plant), largely due to increased pest

Agronomy I 159
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
and disease pressure. Correlation and regression 
analyses demonstrated that yield was strongly and 
positively correlated with maximum temperature 
(r=0.84), sunshine hours (r=0.77), and GDD 
(r=0.72), while rainfall (r=0.62) had a significant 
negative impact. The regression model developed 
from this study predicted that yield increased by 
approximately 503 g/plant for every 1°C rise in 
maximum temperature (within the favorable range), 
but decreased by 21 g/plant with each additional 
millimeter of rainfall. These findings highlight the 
critical importance of sowing date adjustment to 
synchronize crop growth with favorable weather 
conditions. The study concludes that, sowing within 
10-20th October ensures optimal climatic alignment 
for maximum productivity of BARI Begun-12 
in central Bangladesh. Moreover, the developed 
weather-based yield prediction model provides a 
useful decision-support tool for planning climate-
resilient brinjal production, enabling farmers and 
policymakers to optimize sowing schedules and 
mitigate risks associated with climatic variability.
Yield performance of garlic under different 
integrated nutrient management at AEZ-9
M.R. Ali, J. Rahman and M. M. Kadir
An experiment was carried out at Regional 
Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Jamalpur 
during November 2024 to March 2025 to find out 
yield performance of garlic under different integrated 
nutrient management at AEZ-9. The treatments were 
T1= Recommended fertilizer dose (95-35-75-25-3-3 
kg/ha N-P-K-S-Zn-B), T 2= IPNS+ poultry manure 
(1.5 t/ha), T 3= IPNS+ poultry manure (3.0 t/ha), 
T4= IPNS+ vermicompost (1.5 t/ha), T 5= IPNS+ 
vermicompost (3.0 t/ha), T 6= IPNS+ FYM (1.5 t/
ha), T 7= IPNS+ FYM (3.0 t/ha). The treatments 
were tested in randomized complete block design 
with 3 dispersed replications. The unit plot size 
was 3.0 m × 3.0 m and spacing was 15 cm × 10 
cm. BARI Rosun-2 was used as test material. Rosun 
was sown on 26 November 2024 and harvested on 
27 March 2025. Fertilizer was used as per treatment. 
Fifty percent N was applied as basal at the time of 
planting and remaining 50% N was applied in two 
equal splits during 30 and 45 days after sowing; 
full dose of P and K were applied at the time of 
planting and full dose of S was given fifty days 
before planting per treatments. Weeding, irrigation 
and other intercultural operations were done as and 
when necessary. The yield of garlic was calculated 
in t/ha considering the whole plot as harvest area. 
Ten plants of garlic from each plot were selected 
randomly to collect data on yield components. 
Collected data were analyzed statistically with the 
help of a computer package program STAR and 
the means were adjusted by Least Significance 
Difference (LSD) test at 5% level of significance. . 
The result indicated that garlic yield was increased 
due to integrated nutrient management. The highest 
garlic yield (11.57 t/ha) was found from IPNS+ 
poultry manure (3.0 t/ha) and the lowest yield (5.77 
t/ha) was found from recommended fertilizer dose 
(95-35-25-3-3 kg/ha N-P-K-S-Zn-B) treatment. So 
it is concluded that integrated plant nutrient system 
(IPNS with manure (3.0 t/ha) is the best fertilizer 
combination for garlic production under AEZ-9.

package. The results indicated that the minimum

160 I Agronomy
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
time for germination was recorded from 150 ppm 
GA3 + 60minute soaking time, which is statistically 
similar with 100 ppm GA3 + 60minute soaking time.

statistically similar with 100ppm GA 3+ 30minute
