which received fertilizer through T 3 i.e. Nitrogen 
from urea and Phosphorus from TSP. In case of T 5 
i.e. proposed fertilizer dose recorded highest yield 
of potato (26.34 t ha-1) which was statistically at par 
with T1, T2, T3 and T 4. From the study the highest 
gross return (Tk 577000 ha-1) and gross margin (Tk. 
334791ha-1) were estimated from the treatment T 5. 
The lowest gross return (Tk 309800ha -1) and gross 
margin (Tk 80891 ha -1) were recorded from T 6 
when lowest amount of fertilizers were applied. The 
result led to conclusion that the most effective and 
economic fertilizer application in potato is 150-45-
135-15-10-4-1.6 kg ha-1 NPKSMgZnB along with 5 
ton ha-1 cow dung fertilizer are the promising level 
for excellent results in potato crop under plain land 
conditions at Gouripur, Mymensingh.

Effect of split application of urea and MOP on 
potato production in Rangpur region
U. K. Laily, M. Z. Ferdous, M. K. Islam, M. U. S. 
Khatun, M. Akhter-Ul-Alam, M. A. H. Talukder 
In Bangladesh, the use of chemical fertilizers is 
not balanced. In order to maintain agricultural 
production and increase potato yield while reducing 
adverse effects on soil fertility, proper nutrient 
management is crucial. The aim of the study was 
to observe the effect of spilt application of N and 
K on potato production. A field experiment was 
conducted at OFRD, BARI, Rangpur in the rabi 
season of 2024-25. Three treatments viz. T 1: 
Farmers practices (Basal: 1/3 rd Urea and 1/3 rd MoP, 
1/3rd Urea and 1/3 rd MoP at 28 days after planting 
(DAP), 1/3 rd Urea and 1/3 rd MoP at 42 DAP), T 2: 
Two splits of RFD (Basal: 1/3rd Urea and 1/3rd MoP, 
1/3rd Urea and 1/3 rd MoP at 28 DAP) and T 3: Three 
splits of RFD (Basal: 1/3 rd Urea and1/3rd MoP, 1/3rd 
Urea and 1/3rd MoP at 28 DAP, 1/3rd Urea and 1/3 rd 
MoP at 42 DAP) were evaluated for this purpose. 
Results revealed that the highest number of tuber 
hill-1 (16.92), tuber weight hill-1 (0.644 kg) and tuber 
yield (34.58 t ha -1 ) were found from three splits of 
RFD ( Basal : 1/3 rd Urea and 1/3 rd MoP, 1/3rd Urea 
and 1/3rd MoP at 28 DAP, 1/3rd Urea and 1/3 rd MoP 
at 42 DAP) treatment. Amongst the three treatments 
adopted in the experiment, the highest gross return 
(Tk 518400 ha -1) and gross margin (Tk 275317 ha -
1) were also obtained from the T 3 treatment. The 
lowest tuber yield was obtained from T 1 (Farmers' 
practices) treatment.
Effect of nutrient management on the productivity 
of mustard (canola) in north-west Bangladesh
M. S. Hossain, M. T. Hasan, M. E. Haque, M. A. H. 
Talukder and M. M. Hasan 
The cultivation area of rapeseed mustard in 
Bangladesh is expanding rapidly, driven by the 
development of high yielding varieties and the rising 
market price of edible oil. However, imbalanced 
fertilization remains a key constraint limiting seed 
yield. To determine the optimum and economical 
fertilizer dose for canola type mustard (BARI 
Sarisha-18) a field experiment was conducted during 
the rabi seasons of 2023-24 and 2024-25 under the 
supervision of the OFRD, BAR). The trials were 
carried out across three locations representing 
different agro-ecological zones (AEZs): the Barind 
tract of Godagari in Rajshahi (AEZ-26), the char land 
of Bogura Sadar (AEZ-3), and the BARI research 
station in Rangpur (AEZ-3). The experimental 
treatments included four nutrient management 
packages applied across all sites: T1: Soil test based 
fertilizer (STB) (FRG, 2018), T 2: T1 +25% NPKS, 
T3: T 1 +50% NPKS, T 4: Farmers' practices. An 
additional treatment T5: Khamari App-based Nutrient 
Package was evaluated only at the Rangpur site. The 
experimental layout followed a RCBD with three 
replications. In Rajshahi, T 3 recorded the highest 
seed yield (2.17 and 2.13 t ha−1 in 2023-24 and 
2024-25, respectively) and economic performance 
as highest gross return Tk 188125 ha−1, gross margin 
Tk 159967 ha−1, and a benefit cost ratio (BCR) 3.24. 
In Bogura, T 3 likewise produced the highest seed 
yield (2.12 t ha−1), gross return (Tk 168120 ha−1), 
and gross margin (Tk 116980 ha−1). However, T 2 
was the most economically favorable providing a 
yield of 1.75 t ha−1, gross return Tk 148495 ha−1, and 
gross margin of Tk 94930 ha−1 in Rangpur region.
Effect of nitrogen levels on crop productivity 
and profitability of different rice-based cropping 
systems
M. A. Islam, M. Maniruzzaman, M. Z. Hasan, M. S. 
H. Molla and M. S. Hossain
A field experiment was conducted during 2021-
22, 2022-23, and 2023-24 at the Agricultural 
Research Station, Pabna, Bangladesh, to evaluate 
crop productivity and system performance under 
diversified rice-based cropping systems. Three 
cropping patterns were examined: cereal-based 
system (CBS), oilseed-based system (OBS), and 
legume-based system (LBS), along with four 
nitrogen fertilizer levels: 0% of the recommended 
nitrogen dose (RND) - control (N0), 50% of RND 
(N50), 100% of RND (N100), and 150% of RND 
(N150). The experiment followed a split-plot design 
with three replications. In the 2023-24 season, LBS 
consistently outperformed CBS and OBS across 
all crops and nitrogen levels. For Crop 7 (rice), 
LBS recorded the highest yield (3.2 t/ha), with 
the maximum yield observed under the LBSN100 
combination (4.3 t/ha). In Crop 8, LBS achieved 
the highest rice equivalent yield (REY) of 5.1 t/ha, 
with the LBSN50 treatment yielding the maximum 
at 6.4 t/ha. A similar pattern was observed in Crop 
9, where LBS produced the highest REY (4.4 t/ha),

234 I On-Farm Studies
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
and LBSN50 reached the peak yield of 5.1 t/ha. 
Overall, system REY was highest in LBS (12.8 t/
ha), followed by CBS (8.8 t/ha) and OBS (8.3 t/ha). 
Nitrogen application significantly enhanced system 
productivity, with N100 and N150 treatments 
producing REYs of 12.5-12.7 t/ha, while the control 
(N0) recorded only 5.7 t/ha. The highest system REY 
(14.6 t/ha) was obtained under LBSN100, whereas 
the lowest (3.3 t/ha) was observed in CBSN0. 
Although a slight decline in system productivity was 
noted compared to the previous year, the legume-
based LBS system remained the most productive. 
These findings underscore the importance of 
integrated cropping system diversification and 
optimal nitrogen management for sustainable 
agricultural intensification in rice-based systems.
Effect of phosphorus levels and planting 
techniques on the performance of mustard-
maize-t. Aman rice cropping pattern 
M. Maniruzzaman, M. Z. Hasan, M. A. Islam, M. S. 
H. Molla and M. S. Hossain
The impacts of conservation agriculture (CA) 
practices combined with varying phosphorus (P) 
input levels on soil P availability and P fertilizer 
management are not yet fully understood, 
particularly in short- to medium-term rice-based 
cropping systems. To address this knowledge 
gap, a field experiment was conducted during 
the 2022-23 and 2023-24 cropping seasons to 
evaluate the combined effects of tillage practices 
and P fertilization on system productivity. The 
experiment assessed two tillage methods-strip 
planting (SP) and conventional tillage (CT)-
along with three P fertilizer application rates: 
low dose (LD = 75% of the recommended dose, 
RD), recommended dose (RD = 100% P as per 
FRG-2018), and high dose (HD = 125% of RD). 
The results revealed that SP improved system 
rice equivalent yield by 3-10% compared to CT, 
primarily due to increased yields of the component 
crops. Furthermore, both RD and HD of phosphorus 
application produced comparable system yields, 
significantly outperforming the LD treatment. 
These findings suggest that the mustard-maize-T. 
aman rice cropping system, when managed under 
strip planting with the recommended phosphorus 
rate, holds considerable promise for enhancing 
crop yield and system productivity.
Effects of boron on growth and yield of proso 
millet at char areas of Brahmaputra-Ganges 
floodplains
M. S. H. Molla, M. Maniruzzaman, M. A. Isalm, M. 
Z. Hasan and A. A. Mahmud 
This study evaluated the effects of varying boron 
fertilizer doses on the growth and yield of Proso millet 
(BARI Cheena-1) under the Char land conditions of 
Pabna, Bangladesh. Five boron fertilizer rates: 0.0, 
1.0, 1.25, 1.50, and 1.75 kg B ha−1 were assessed 
using a RCBD with three replications. The results 
revealed that boron application significantly 
influenced key yield components, including the 
number of panicles per plant, panicle length, number 
of grains per panicle, grain yield, and straw yield. 
The highest grain yield (2.82 t ha−1) was recorded at 
1.75 kg ha−1 B, which was statistically similar to 1.50 
kg ha−1 B (2.81 t ha−1), and both were significantly 
superior to the control (0 kg ha−1 B) which produced 
a yield of 1.78 t ha−1. These findings highlight the 
critical role of boron fertilization in enhancing 
Proso millet productivity under the nutrient 
deficient and stress prone conditions of Char land 
ecosystems. Application of 1.50-1.75 kg B ha−1 is 
recommended for optimizing yield performance in 
this environment.

Intercropping of hybrid maize with short 
duration vegetables in Cumilla
M. J. Uddin
The experiment was conducted at a farmer's field 
in Atipara, Daudkandi, Cumilla during the rabi 
season of 2024-25 to identify suitable and profitable 
intercropping systems involving hybrid maize 
(var. BARI Hybrid Maize-16) and short-duration 
vegetables:Jharseem (var. BARI Jharseem-2), 
red amaranth (var. BARI Lalshak-1), coriander 
(var. BARI Dhonia-2), and garden pea (var. BARI 
Motorshuti-3). Sole maize produced grain yield of 
10.65 t/ha, which was reduced under intercropping 
systems. However, maize equivalent yield (MEY) 
increased under intercropping, with the highest 
MEY recorded in maize + garden pea (14.45 t/ha), 
followed by maize + coriander (13.51 t/ha) and 
maize + Jharseem (11.97 t/ha). Maize + red amaranth 
resulted in the lowest MEY (11.02 t/ha). The highest 
gross margin (Tk. 238,283/ha) and benefit-cost ratio 
(2.62) were also observed in the maize + garden pea

Effect of sowing date on the productivity of 
mustard (canola) in north-west Bangladesh
M. S. Hossain and M. E. A. Pramanik
A field trial was conducted at the FSRD site, 
Godagari, Rajshahi during the rabi seasons in 2023-
24 and 2024-25 to evaluate the effect of sowing date 
on yield attributes and yield of mustard (Canola). 
Mustrad var. BARI Sarisha-18 was used as the test 
crop. The experiment included five sowing dates: 25 
October, 05 November, 15 November, 25 November, 
and 05 December. It was arranged in a RCBD with 
three dispersed replications. The crop required 37-
44 days to reach first flowering and 90-104 days 
to attain physiological maturity, depending on the 
sowing date. It was observed that delayed sowing 
resulted in shorter growth duration. In both years, 
the highest seed yield was obtained from the 05 
November sowing, after which the yield gradually 
declined with later planting dates.

Effect of tillage and mulch on the yield 
performance of potato in AEZ-11
M. J. Islam, M. N. A. Siddquie and M. M. I. 
Chowdhury
A two-year field experiment (2023-24 and 2024-
25) was conducted both on-station and on-farm 
to evaluate the effects of different tillage practices 
on potato growth, yield, quality, and profitability. 
The treatments included conventional tillage, strip 
tillage with straw mulch (strip + straw), and strip 
tillage with polyethylene mulch (strip+poly). The 
results revealed that conservation tillage practices 
significantly improved plant height, tuber number, 
tuber weight per plant, and tuber yield compared 
to conventional tillage, particularly on-station. 
Strip tillage combined with straw and polyethylene 
mulches resulted in higher tuber yield (up to 42.6 
t ha−1) and better dry matter content. Potato grade 
distribution was not significantly influenced by 
tillage methods; however, larger tuber sizes tended 
to be more prevalent under conservation practices. 
Economic analysis indicated that conservation 
tillage practices led to higher net returns and benefit-
cost ratios (up to 2.57 on-station and 2.51 on-farm), 
demonstrating their economic viability. These 
findings suggest that strip tillage combined with 
organic or plastic mulching is a promising strategy 
for enhancing potato productivity and profitability in 
sustainable farming systems.

Effects of seedling age and seedling raised for 
sunflower cultivation in coastal region
H. M. K. Bashar, M. M. Islam and K. N. Islam
The success of sunflower (Helianthus annuus 
L.) cultivation is significantly influenced by 
seedling establishment and early growth vigor. An 
experiment was conducted at the MLT site, Kuakata, 
Patuakhali, during the Rabi season of 2024-2025 
to establish seedling transplanting practices for 
sunflower cultivation in fallow saline coastal areas 
following Aman rice harvest. This study aimed to 
evaluate the effects of seedling age on the growth, 
yield, and overall production performance of 
sunflower. Five treatments were tested: 10-day-old 
tray seedlings, 15-day-old tray seedlings, 10-day-
old seedlings, 15-day-old seedlings, and direct 
seeding. A RCBD with threedispersed replications 
was employed. The results revealed that 15-day-
old tray seedlings exhibited superior growth 
and yield performance compared to the other 
treatments, showing significant increases in head 
perimeter, 1000-seed weight, and seed yield. Direct 
seeding, although simpler, resulted in lower stand 
establishment and yield. The 10-day-old seedlings 
performed moderately but were less vigorous than 
the 15-day-old seedlings. The findings suggest that 
transplanting 15-day-old tray seedlings can be a 
viable strategy for enhancing sunflower productivity 
under optimal management practices.

This study aimed to determine the optimum

Surjomukhi-2, BARI Surjomukhi-3, and the widely 
cultivated hybrid Hysun-33 in the coastal regions 
of Patuakhali and Barguna, Pirojpur and Gopalganj 
during the 2024-2025 growing season. The 
experiment was conducted in farmers' fields using a 
two factorial RCBD with six dispersed replications. 
Three sowing dates in Patuakhali and four sowing 
dates (15 December, 30 December, 15 January and 
30 January) were tested in Pirojpur, Gopalganj to 
evaluate their effect on sunflower growth and yield. 
The highest plant height (132.54 cm and 135.90 
cm), head perimeter (74.23 cm and 76.98 cm), 
number of seeds per head (450.54 and 470.98), and 
seed yield (1.75 and 1.87 t/ha) were recorded for 
the 15 December sowing date at both experimental 
locations. The interaction between sowing date and 
variety showed that the highest values for days to 
maturity (117 and 117.5), plant height (135.98 cm 
and 139.89 cm), head perimeter (71.94 cm and 73.83 
cm), number of seeds per head (443.15 and 468.37), 
thousand-seed weight (87.50 g and 88.00 g), and 
seed yield (1.82 and 1.90 t/ha) were achieved by 
BARI Surjomukhi-2 and Hysun-33 when sown on 
15 December in Kuakata, Patuakhali, and Barguna 
Sadar, Barguna, respectively. Soil salinity levels 
during the study ranged from 0.47 to 9.79 dS/m 
in Kuakata and from 0.67 to 7.65 dS/m in Amtoli. 
The seed yield was significantly influenced by the 
interaction of sowing date and variety, the seed yield 
ranged was from 0.71 to 2.21 t ha -1at Pirojpur and 
Gopalgan. The highest seed yield 2.21t ha -1 was 
found from 15 December with Hysan-33 and it was 
followed by 30 December with Hysan-33 (2.10 ha -
1). The lowest seed yield 0.71 t ha -1 was found from 
30 January with Hysan-33 variety.

Effect of spacing and different variety on 
groundnut production in the coastal region of 
Bangladesh
A field experiment was conducted in Patuakhali 
sadar, Patuakhali, Bangladesh during the 2025 
cropping season to evaluate the effect of different 
plant spacing and groundnut varieties on growth 
and yield performance in the coastal agro-ecological 
zone. The trial was followed a factorial arrangement 
with three spacing levels (30 cm × 15 cm, 30 cm × 20 
cm, and 30 cm × 25 cm) and four groundnut varieties 
(BARI Chinabadam-9, BARI Chinabadam-10,

On-Farm Studies I 249
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
BARI Chinabadam-11, and Dhaka-1). Results 
revealed significant differences in plant height, 
number of pods per plant, 100-seed weight, and 
yield among treatments. Wider spacing increased 
plant height and number of pods per plant, while 
narrower spacing higher plant population density 
and overall yield. The maximum yield (2.52 t ha−1) 
was recorded from BARI Chinabadam-9 at 30 cm × 
15 cm spacing, followed by BARI Chinabadam-10 
(2.19 t ha−1) under the same spacing. In contrast, the 
lowest yield (1.45 t ha−1) was observed in Dhaka-1 at 
30 cm × 25 cm spacing. Among the varieties, BARI 
Chinabadam-9 performed best in terms of both 
yield and agronomic traits. The study concludes 
that closer spacing (30 cm × 15 cm) combined with 
BARI Chinabadam-9 is the most suitable option for 
maximizing groundnut production in the coastal 
region of Bangladesh.

Effect of alternate furrow irrigation strategies on 
potato yield and water productivity
J. A. Mahmud, M. M. Morshed and M. M. Hossain
An experiment was conducted at MLT site, 
Bheramara, Kushtia during the rabi season of 
2024-25. The experiment compared three different 
irrigation strategies for potato cultivation namely: 
Alternate Furrow Irrigation (AFI), Fixed Furrow 
Irrigation (FFI), and Every Furrow Irrigation (EFI). 
Alternate furrow irrigation resulted in a substantial 
decrease in water consumption and a notable gain in 
water productivity. AFI achieved a 35% reduction in 
water usage and a 50% increase in water productivity 
compared to EFI. This approach minimizes water 
consumption without reducing production.
Survey, monitoring and documentation of major 
insect pests of betel leaf in Rajshahi region
M. E. A. Pramanik and M. S. Hossain 
The current study was conducted in a betel leaf garden 
in the Rajshahi district of Bangladesh 2024-25 to 
identify the pests that exist in the research locations. 
During the research period, twelve insect pests 
were identified. Various insect pests were observed 
in betel leaf orchard e.g. blackfly, whitefly, semi 
looper, common cutworm, scale insects, mealy bug, 
snail, trips, red spider mite, betel vine bug, and betel 
vine termite. The betel vine blackfly, semi looper, 
scale insects, whitefly, and red spider mite were 
discovered to be the most harmful pests. Blackflies 
and red spider mites, two dangerous insect pests that 
damage betel vines, peak in infestation between May 
and October and cause significant economic losses. 
Pests cause serious losses by affecting the crop's 
roots and leaves. Documenting the pests is essential 
for creating efficient management strategies.

252 I On-Farm Studies

Screening of fungicides in controlling clubroot 
disease of mustard
M. S. Hossain, M. Monirul Islam and M. E. A. 
Pramanik
A field trial was conducted during the rabi season 
of 2024-25 at the farmers' field under the FSRD 
site, Basantopur, Godagari, Rajshahi, to evaluate the 
efficacy of various fungicides for the management 
of clubroot disease in mustard. The mustard variety 
used in the study was BARI Sarisha-14. The trial 
included eight treatments, consisting of seven 
fungicide applications and one untreated control, 
as follows: T 1 = Secure 600 WG (Fenamidone 
+ Mancozeb) @ 2 mL/L, T 2 = Ridomil Gold 
(Metalaxyl) @ 2 mL/L, T 3 = Dolochune @ 5 t/ha, 
T4 = Luna Sensation (Fluopyram + Trifloxystrobin) 
@ 2 mL/L, T 5 = Amistar Top (Azoxystrobin + 
Difenoconazole) @ 2 mL/L, T 6 = Nativo 75 WG 
(Tebuconazole + Trifloxystrobin) @ 2 mL/L, T 7 
= Blitox (Copper-based fungicide) @ 2 g/L, and 
T8 = Untreated control. A total of three fungicidal 
sprays were applied at seven-day intervals, with the 
first application initiated at the initial appearance of 
disease symptoms. Notably, no incidence of club 
root was observed during the trial period across all 
treatments, including the control. However, plots 
treated with fungicides consistently produced higher 
seed yields compared to the untreated control, 
suggesting a potential yield-enhancing effect of 
fungicide application under field conditions, possibly 
due to the control of other latent or subclinical fungal 
pathogens.

Onion maggot (Delia antiqua), a serious pest of

true seed production in Bangladesh. The study 
was conducted at the On-Farm Research Division

Adaptive trial of coffee at Bandarban hill district 
and hilly area of Sherpur and Mymensingh 
M. Salim, M. T. Islam, F. Arshad, M. I. Hossain, M. 
A. Hossain, A. K. M. Z. U. Noor, M. M. Rahman 
and M. F. Islam 
This five-year adaptive trial (2021-2025) evaluated 
the growth, adaptability and yield of Coffea 
robusta and Coffea arabica across seven upazilas 
in Bandarban Hill District, Gandhigaon, Jinaighati 
(Sherpur) and Haluaghat (Mymensingh) hilly area. 
In Jinaighati, Coffea robusta recorded the highest 
plant height (135.3 cm), leaf length (16.8 cm), and 
leaf breadth (10.2 cm), while Coffea arabica showed 
better performance in yield (7.5 t ha−1), number of 
branches (21.9), base girth (7.5 cm), and canopy 
spread (98.5 × 86.5 cm2). Similarly, in Haluaghat, 
Coffea arabica exhibited higher yield (6.3 t ha−1), 
plant height (131.6 cm), number of branches (90.4), 
and canopy size (105.4 × 92.4 cm2), whereas Coffea 
robusta had longer leaves (19.4 cm) but lower 
yield (2.3 t ha−1). The adaptive trial in Bandarban, 
conducted on 26 farmer fields covering 18.14 acres 
under homogenous cultural practices with RCB 
design. Results revealed that Robusta exhibited 
huge vegetative growth reaching up to 170.9 cm in 
Alikadam and maximum yield of 1807.33 g plant -1 
in Bandarban Sadar. Arabica, whereas slightly 
shorter (126.3 cm), showed consistent growth 
and the maximum yield of 1234.67 g plant -1. Tree 
volume increased by 424% in Robusta and 554% 
in Arabica under favorable conditions indicated 
wider adaptability. These findings revealed the yield 
potentiality and ecological suitability of Coffea 
arabica in northern hill valleys and the broader 
adaptability of Coffea robusta in southeastern hill 
regions, offering strategic direction for sustainable 
coffee expansion in Bangladesh.

Adaptive trial with high yielding potato varieties 
in different locations
M. J. Alam, M. Akhtaruzzaman, A. A. Mahmud, 
M. J. Uddin, M. I. Nazrul, M. Asaduzzaman, M. 
Julfiqar, M. R. Amin, M. Salim, M.T. Islam, M.I. 
Hossain, M. A. Rahaman, T. Tasmima, K. Roy, 
G. Paul, P. Sutradhar, A. K. M. Z. U. Noor, M. 
M. Rahman, M. F. Islam, M. Mohiuddin, M. Y . H. 
Rayhan, M.M Zaman, M. Z. Ferdous, M. E. Haque, 
M. A. U. Alam, and M. A. H. Talukder
Four set of trials were carried out at farmers' fields in 
9 (Nine) locations under four different ecosystems, 
viz. low land/haor, drought/char, plain land and hill 
ecosystem during the rabi season of 2024-2025 
to assess the performance of high-yielding potato 
varieties and learn about farmers' preferences 
regarding the varieties. Considering the low land 
ecosystem, the tuber yield ranged from 18.3 to 46.0 t 
ha-1 across the locations. Sylhet was identified as the 
most favorable environment for potato production, 
with an average yield of 37.6 t ha -1, followed by 
Brahmanbaria with 30.4 t ha -1. On the other hand, 
the environmental conditions in Kishoreganj were 
less conducive to potato cultivation, resulting in

On-Farm Studies I 257
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
an average yield of 28.0 t ha -1. In the plain land 
ecosystem, the potato yield ranged between 20.0 to 
44.5 t ha-1 across different locations. The Manikganj 
region was identified as the most favorable 
environment for potato production, with an average 
yield of 36.6 t ha -1. In contrast Sherpur was found 
to be less productive with an average yield of 30.4 
t ha -1. In the char land ecosystem, the tuber yield 
of potato varied from 10.95 to 38.0 t ha -1 across 
different locations. The char area of Kurigram has 
been founded as the most favorable environment 
for potato production, where the average yield was 
30.8 t ha-1. Conversely, the char area of Tangail was 
found to be less productive with an average yield 
of 16.5 t ha -1. Within the hill ecosystem, the potato 
yield ranged from 21.00 to 33.6 t ha-1 in Bandarban. 
Farmers chose different potato varieties based on 
market price, plant growth, yield potential, tuber 
size and shape, and skin color. This difference was 
noted in various places. However, in lowland and 
haor ecosystems, BARI Alu-47, BARI Alu-62, 
BARI Alu-77, BARI Alu-87 and BARI Alu-90 were 
found to be the best-performing potato varieties. 
For plain land ecosystems, BARI Alu-40, BARI 
Alu-41, BARI Alu-47, and BARI Alu-49 were the 
top performers. For char land ecosystems, BARI 
Alu-7, BARI Alu-62, BARI Alu-72, BARI Alu-73 
and BARI Alu-78 were the top performers. For hill 
ecosystems, BARI Alu-47, BARI Alu-62, BARI 
Alu-63 and BARI Alu-87 were the top performers. 
Considering all ecosystems, the corresponding 
potato varieties were determined to be appropriate 
for growing in the particular ecosystems and might 
be suggested for future cultivation.

On-farm evaluation of BARI-released mustard 
varieties in different agro-ecological zones of 
BANGLADESH
M. S. Hossain, M. E. A. Pramanik, S. Akhtar, N. 
Akther, S. Sultana, N. Sultana, M. A. H. Khan, M. F. 
Islam, M. M. Rahman, A. K. M. Z. U. Noor, M. T. 
Hasan, M. R. A. Mollah, M. M. Hasan, M. S. Alam, 
G. N. Hasan, R. H. Anik and M Islam
The experiments were conducted during the rabi 
season of 2024-25 across diverse agroecological 
zones of Bangladesh, including Rajshahi, 
Mymensingh, Sherpur, Bogura, Cox's Bazar, and 
Bhola, to evaluate the growth, yield performance, 
and economic returns of promising mustard varieties. 
The trials were laid out in RCBD with three to six 
dispersed replications. The tested varieties exhibited 
significant variation in phenological traits, yield-
contributing characters, and economic profitability 
across locations. BARI Sarisha-18 consistently 
demonstrated superior performance, producing the 
highest seed and straw yields in most locations, along 
with excellent reproductive traits such as siliquae 
plant-1, seeds siliqua-1, and 1000-seed weight. BARI 
Sarisha-20 also performed well, particularly in 
coastal and drought-prone regions due to its early 
maturity and higher seed yield. BARI Sarisha-17 
showed notable performance in some locations like 
Bhola and Sherpur. Economic analysis revealed 
that BARI Sarisha-18 recorded the highest gross 
margin and benefit-cost ratio in most environments, 
making it a robust and profitable choice for farmers. 
These results indicate that variety selection should 
be location-specific, and BARI Sarisha-18 and 
BARI Sarisha-20 hold potential for widespread 
adoption under diverse agro-climatic conditions of 
Bangladesh.
Yield performance of advanced lines of brassica 
rapa under on-farm conditions in Bangladesh 
M. Z. Hasan, M. A. Islam, M. M. A. Niruzzaman, 
M. S. H. Molla, S. Akhtar, N. Akther, S. Sultana, N. 
Sultana, Mah Khan, M. M. Rahman, M. F. Islam and 
A. K. M. Z. U. Noor
The experiments was conducted during Rabi season 
of 2024-2025 at farmers' fields across three locations 
Gangarampur (Pabna), Trishal (Mymensingh), 
and Sherpur to evaluate the yield performance and 
agronomic traits of advanced Brassica rapa lines 
compared to the check variety BARI Sarisha-20. 
A total of 4-6 advanced lines, including BC-0835, 
BC-100614(4)2(Y), BC-14031(Y), BC-15015, and 
BC-15022 were tested in RCBD with three to four 
dispersed replications. Significant variations were 
observed in yield-contributing characters such as 
days to flowering, days to maturity, plant height, 
branches plant-1, siliqua plant-1 and 1000-seed weight. 
Across locations, the highest seed yield (1720 kg 
ha−1) was obtained from BC-100614(4)2(Y) which 
exceeded the yield of BARI Sarisha-20 by 12.4%. 
BC-14031(Y) and BC-0835 also demonstrated 
greater performance with yields of 1690 and 1575 
kg ha−1, respectively. BARI Sarisha-20 and BC-
15015 achieved the highest gross returns (Tk. 
105127 ha−1 and Tk. 105000 ha−1). Shorter days 
to maturity (74-80 days) and better adaptability of 
the advanced lines indicated their suitability for 
Mustard-Boro-T. Aman rice cropping pattern. 
Farmers expressed satisfaction with BC-15015 and 
BC-0835 due to their high yield and profitability. 
Further trial is nedded in the upcoming seasons to 
confirm the results.

Adaptive trial of long duration mustard varieties
M. M. Howlader, D. Halder, M. Salim, M. T. Islam, 
and M. I. Hossain
Two adaptive trials were conducted in contrasting 
environments such as low-lying southern region 
(Gopalganj) and hill valleys (Bandarban) during the 
Rabi season of 2024-25 to evaluate the performance 
of long-duration mustard varieties. The varieties 
were BARI Sarisha-11, BARI Sarisha-16, BARI 
Sarisha-18 and BARI Sarisha-19. The trials aimed 
to identify suitable varieties for late sowing in 
water-receding low lands and moisture-retentive 
hill valleys of Banderban. In Gopalganj, BARI 
Sarisha-19 gave the highest yield (1.72 t ha−1) 
followed by BARI Sarisha-16 (1.60 t ha−1). In 
Bandarban, BARI Sarisha-18 outperformed others 
in terms of plant height, siliqua plant -1, seed yield 
(1.53 t ha−1) and economic return (BCR 2.88). 
Farmers at both locations preferred high yialding, 
long duration varieties particularly BARI Sarisha-18 
and BARI Sarisha-19 due to higher grain and stover 
yield. These varieties are recommended for non-
traditional, resource-constrained areas to boost 
oilseed productivity and farmer income.
On-farm trial of BARI sesame varieties in 
Manikganj and Gopalganj region
M. R. Amin, M. M. Howlader, and D. Halder
On-farm trials were conducted during the 2024-
25 Kharif-I and rabi seasons at Chargobindapur, 
Daulatpur upazila of Manikganj and in selected sites 
of Gopalganj and Pirojpur districts to evaluate the 
performance of BARI developed sesame varieties. 
The experiment was laid out in RCBD with three 
dispersed replications. At Manikganj, three BARI 
sesame varieties viz. BARI Til-4, BARI Til-5 and 
BARI Til-6 and at Gopalganj five sesame varieties 
viz. BARI Til-3, BARI Til-4, BARI Til-5, BARI Til-
6 and a local variety were evaluated. In Manikganj, 
BARI Til-4 recorded the highest yield (1.44 t ha−1) 
whereas BARI Til-5 provided the highest gross 
margin (Tk. 87178 ha−1) due to higher market 
price. In Gopalganj and Pirojpur, BARI Til-5 also 
showed superior performance with the highest yield 
(1.67 t ha−1). Farmers at both locations ptreferred 
BARI Til-5 for its high productivity and higher 
market price. These findings indicate the high 
adaptability and economic viability of BARI sesame 
varieties under diverse field conditions.
Regional yield trial of sesame in coastal region of 
Bangladesh
The field experiment was conducted under varying 
saline conditions (2.65-12.98 dS/m) in the coastal 
saline region. The study aimed to identify suitable 
sesame varieties capable of withstanding salinity 
while maintaining satisfactory growth and yield. 
The experiment was laid out in RCBD with three 
dispered replications. The six sesame varieties/lines 
viz. Ses05115, Ses65, Ses05178, Ses031, Ses79 
and BARI Til-6 were included in the study. BARI 
Til-6 exhibited better performance with the highest 
plant height (97.67 cm), number of seeds capsule -1 
(112.98) and yield (1.22 t ha -1) followed by Ses65 
(1.21 t ha-1). Conversely, Ses79 gave the lowest yield 
(1.06 t ha -1). Despite moderate variation in plant 
growth traits, yield stability under salinity stress 
highlighted the potential of BARI Til-6 and Ses65 
for saline-prone regions. The findings suggest that 
these varieties are promising candidates for sesame 
cultivation in saline environments contributing to 
crop diversification and food security in vulnerable 
coastal areas.
Mustard cultivation in association with mango 
fruit tree
M. S. Huda
This study investigates the effects of different 
varieties of mustard in a mango-based agroforestry 
system in Dinajpur, Bangladesh. The agroforestry

260 I On-Farm Studies
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
setup with mango trees aged two to five years, 
presents a favorable microenvironment for mustard 
cultivation, offering partial shade and enhanced 
soil moisture retention. Four different varieties 
viz. BARI Sarisha-14, BARI Sarisha-17, BARI

BARI Sarisha-18 to enhance mustard production

sustainable production practices in mango-based 
agroforestry systems.
On-farm trial of groundnut varieties in 
Bangladesh (Charland, Gopalganj and Bhola 
regions)
M. U. S. Khatun, M. Z. Ferdous, M. K. Islam, U. 
K. Laily, M. A. H. Talukder, M. M. Howlader, D. 
Halder, G. N. Hasan, R. H. Anik and M. Islam
On-farm trials were conducted at three major 
locations in Bangladesh such as Charland of 
Bongram, Chilmari (Kurigram), Gopalganj-Pirojpur 
and Bhola during the rabi seasons of 2022-23, 
2023-24 and 2024-25 to evaluate the performance 
of improved groundnut varieties for yield, yield 
attributes and economic return under farmer field 
condition. The experiment was laid out in RCBD with 
four to six dispered replications. Four BARI released 
groundnut varieties viz. BARI Chinabadam-8, 
BARI Chinabadam-9, BARI Chinabadam-10, BARI 
Chinabadam-11 and one local variety Dhaka-1 as 
check were evaluated. Irrespective of locations and 
years, BARI Chinabadam-9 consistently produced 
the highest pod yield (2.19-2.52 t ha−1) and gross 
margins (Tk. 151200 ha−1). BARI Chinabadam-8, 
BARI Chinabadam-10 and BARI Chinabadam-11 
also gave promising yield and economic return. The 
local variety Dhaka-1 produced the lowest yield 
(1.43-1.63 t ha−1) and return. Farmer preferred BARI 
Chinabadam-9 for its higher yield and profitability. 
Based on the results, BARI Chinabadam-9 is 
recommended for wider cultivation in these agro-
ecological zones.

Evaluation of BARI, SAU, BSMRAU and BAU 
developed rapeseed-mustard varieties at saline 
prone areas 
M. Rahman, M. K. Islam and T. S. Munmun, M. S. 
Islam and M. M. Bashir
Two field experiments were conducted during 
the rabi season of 2024-25 to evaluate the yield 
performance of rapeseed-mustard varieties under 
saline-prone areas of Khulna and Noakhali regions. 
The experiment was laid out in RCBD with three 
replications. Sixteen mustard varieties viz. BARI 
Sarisha-11, BARI Sarisha-14, BARI Sarisha-16, 
BARI Sarisha-18, BARI Sarisha-19; BAU Sarisha-1, 
BAU Sarisha-2, BAU Sarisha-3, BAU Sarisha-4, 
BAU Sarisha-5, BAU Sarisha-6, BAU Sarisha-7, 
BAU Sarisha-8, BAU Sarisha-9; BU Sarisha-1 and 
BHS01 were evaluated in Khulna whereas eighteen 
varieties viz. BARI Sarisha-11, BARI Sarisha-14, 
BARI Sarisha-16, BARI Sarisha-17, BARI 
Sarisha-18, BARI Sarisha-19, BARI Sarisha-20; 
BAU Sarisha-1, BAU Sarisha-2, BAU Sarisha-3, 
BAU Sarisha-4, BAU Sarisha-5, BAU Sarisha-6, 
BAU Sarisha-7, BAU Sarisha-8, BAU Sarisha-9; BU 
Sarisha-1 and BHS01 were evaluated in Noakhali. In 
Khulna, BAU Sarisha-5 produced the highest grain 
yield (2.45 t ha−1) followed by BAU Sarisha-6 (2.31 
t ha−1), BU Sarisha-1 (2.29 t ha−1) and BHS01 (2.29 t 
ha−1) whereas BARI Sarisha-16 gave the lowest yield 
(1.51 t ha−1). In Noakhali, where soil salinity ranged 
from 2.05-6.72 dS m−1 BARI Sarisha-19 yielded the 
highest (0.92 t ha−1) followed by BAU Sarisha-3 (0.84 
t ha−1) and BAU Sarisha-4 (0.80 t ha−1) whereas BARI 
Sarisha-17 gave the lowest yield (0.32 t ha−1). The 
studies revealed that BAU Sarisha-5, BAU Sarisha-6, 
BHS01, BU Sarisha-1 and BARI Sarisha-18 were 
promising for saline soils in Khulna whereas BARI 
Sarisha-19 and BAU Sarisha-3 performed well under 
moderate salinity in Noakhali.

and BARI Barley-8 had the lowest grain yield, 
producing 1.61 t ha -1. However, BARI Barley-7 
produced the highest yield (2.45 t ha -1), while the 
lowest yield (1.97 t ha -1) was recorded form BARI 
Barley-9 under coastal saline environment Kuakata, 
patuakhali. Among the advanced barley lines there 
was significant variation in yield which ranges 1.18 
to 2.35 t ha-1. The highest yield produced from BHL-
33 (2.35 t ha -1) and the lowest was BHL-15 (1.18 t 
ha-1) in coastal area of Koyra, Khulna. 
Project: Integrated Farming
Integrated farming research and development 
for livelihood improvement in the plainland 
ecosystem
M. S. H. Molla, M. A. H. Talukder, Z. Ferdous, M. 
M. Rahman, M. A. Rahman and A. K. M. Z. Nur
The process of improving one's standard of living is 
complex and necessitates acquiring the necessities 
to satisfy one's basic needs. Continuing from the 
previous year, the program was carried out in 
2024-25 in a participatory manner with the goals of 
improving family income and livelihood, developing 
integrated farming technologies, integrating 
component technologies with efficient use of farm

On-Farm Studies I 265
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
resources, and refining innovations created by 
NARS institutes. Atia, Delduar (Tangail), Tarakandi 
(Sherpur), Sholakundu (Faridpur), Gangarampur 
(Pabna), and Ajoddhapur (Rangpur) were the five 
Farming Systems Research and Development 
(FSRD) sites where it was carried out. Members of 
the group included marginal, small, and medium-
sized farmers who partially or fully considered the 
off-farm, cattle, fisheries, field crops, and homestead 
fruits and vegetables as components of farming 
systems. The used components were brought under 
improved technological intervention. The average 
homestead size at the FSRD sites in Pabna, Rangpur, 
Sherpur, Faridpur, and Tangail were 0.14, 0.05, 0.07, 
0.09, and 0.13 hectares, respectively. The average 
amount of vegetables produced per homestead at 
the site was 699 kg following intervention (AI), 
compared to just 170 kg before intervention (BI). 
Compared to BI, the average amount of vegetables 
consumed during AI was 279% higher, at 247 g head-
1day-1. Fruit production per household averaged 585 
kg, compared to 302 kg during BI. During AI, there 
was also an increase in average fruit consumption 
(averaging 118%). Through increased consumption 
of fruits and vegetables from the homestead garden, 
family members' daily nutritional needs were 
significantly supplied, particularly with carotene and 
vitamin C. Animal products from fish, chicken, duck 
and cattle also could help to minimize the protein 
deficiency. A total of 643 fruit trees were brought 
under pest management, and 1061 fruit saplings 
were distributed across several FSRD locations. 
Fruit tree management had a positive effect on farm 
households. The involvement of women (20-80%) in 
various agricultural pursuits rose significantly, which 
had some beneficial effects on gender parity within 
the household. Drip and sprinkler irrigation for 
homestead vegetable production is a cost-effective 
technology, especially for elite farmers who have 
a water pump system for residential use, as it can 
increase water use efficiency and crop productivity. 
Crop land sizes in the Pabna, Rangpur, Sherpur, 
Faridpur, and Tangail areas were, respectively, 0.84, 
0.43, 0.54, 0.64, and 0.61 ha. By incorporating 
improved crops and varieties, improved cropping 
patterns were implemented at the field level. In the 
improved cropping pattern Mustard-Boro-T. Aman 
and Lentil-Sesame-T. Aman, the REY rose by 
28.09% and 11.86%, respectively. In the livestock 
component, the prevalence of major cow diseases 
was lowered to less than 5% following deworming 
and vaccination. The minimal cost required for 
goat rearing made it seem like a potential endeavor. 
Pigeon rearing and the Sonali breed were maintained 
in some homesteads and areas, which had a positive 
effect on farm people as a good source of revenue and 
sustenance for their children. After immunization, 
the mortality rate for chickens decreased and was 
between 3 and 5%. Additionally, the production of 
vermicompost (300 kg/homestead) and farmyard 
manure (3550 kg/homestead) and their use, as 
well as the production of green fodder (60 t/ha) in 
specific homestead areas, had a positive effect on 
the farm families. Over all locations, the average 
pond size was between 0.04 and 0.06 hectares. 
Some farmers maintained their own projects after 
it was discovered that seasonal fish culture using 
carp polyculture in seasonal ponds showed promise. 
The average fish yield from carp polyculture was 
3360 kg per hectare, which was good. Farmers 
also earned some extra money from various off-
farm activities (average gross margin Tk. 11625 
per household). Among the various production 
components, the field crop sector had the highest 
gross margin, while the gross margin improved 
the most in the homestead vegetable production 
sector, where overall gross margin increased by 
100-947% per farm. Local Service Provider (LSP) 
operations (seed and seedling collection, production 
and distribution or sell, immunization, spraying, 
and other activities) were found to be promising for 
home gardening at the FSRD site in Gangarampur, 
Pabna. It was discovered that partially integrating 
farm components was a cost-effective approach. 
Integrated farming for improving livelihood of 
resource poor farm households in drought and 
rainfed ecosystem
M. S. Hossain, M. Asaduzzaman, M. I. Nazrul, M. 
E. A. Pramanik and M. Zulfiqar
Agricultural production in drought-prone and 
rainfed ecosystems faces mounting challenges 
due to prolonged drought, elevated temperatures, 
irregular rainfall patterns driven by climate 
change, soil acidity, and declining fertility. 
These environmental constraints are further 
exacerbated by socio-economic pressures, 
including the shrinking availability of cultivable 
land, especially for resource-poor households.

266 I On-Farm Studies
BARI Annual Report 2024-25
To address these multifaceted challenges, an 
integrated and resource-efficient farming systems 
approach was implemented during 2024-2025 at 
the Farming Systems Research and Development 
(FSRD) sites in Basantapur, Godagari, Rajshahi, 
and Kamalbazar, Sylhet. The primary objectives 
were to optimize on-farm resource use, enhance 
homestead land utilization, improve year-round 
vegetable availability, and empower women and 
children through active participation in homestead-
based agriculture. The research focused on two core 
components: (i) Homestead Production Systems and 
(ii) Crops and Cropping Systems. Technological 
interventions introduced high-yielding varieties 
and improved cropping patterns, such as Tomato-
Boro-T. Aus, which proved to be both productive 
and economically viable. The integration of fruits, 
vegetables, and cereal crops significantly increased 
yields and income. On-farm validation of improved 
crop varieties-including BARI Alu-41, BRRI 
dhan48, Bina dhan7, and BARI Sarisha-14 resulted 
in higher economic returns compared to traditional 
practices. Notably, homestead vegetable production 
increased by 5.45 times following intervention, 
with average household outputs reaching 632 kg of 
vegetables and 526 kg of fruits. Corresponding gross 
margins were Tk. 8,015 and Tk. 12,640, respectively. 
Vegetable and fruit consumption rose by 230% and 
133%, respectively, contributing to improved dietary 
diversity and nutritional intake. Enhanced farmyard 
manure uses improved soil health and sustainability. 
Active involvement of women and children in 
homestead gardening maximized resource use and 
contributed to food security and income generation. 
Overall, the integrated farming systems approach 
demonstrated substantial potential to enhance the 
resilience, productivity, and livelihoods of resource-
constrained households in the High Barind Tract 
and northeastern regions of Bangladesh. These 
findings underscore the value of coordinated, site-
specific, and inclusive interventions in transforming 
smallholder agriculture.

Project: Socioeconomic Studies
Adoption status of BARI mustard varieties in 
selected areas of Cumilla district
M. J. Uddin
Mustard is an important oilseed crop valued for its 
edible oil, high protein content, and diverse uses in 
food, medicine, and industry. Therefore, an attempt 
was made to assess the adoption status of BARI 
improved mustard varieties and their management 
practices at farm level. The study was conducted 
in three upazilas namely Barura, Chandina and 
Debidwar in Cumilla district covering 155 mustard 
growers. Among them 122 BARI mustard adopters 
and 33 non-adoters were selected randomly for 
the study. Mean, percentage, standard deviation 
and Probit regression model was used. Analysis 
revealed that the rate of adotion of BARI Sarisha-14 
(73.82%), BARI Sarisha-15 (2.0%), BARI 
Sarisha-17 (14.3%), BARI Sarisha-18 (4.45% ) and 
Local (Tori-7), 2.78% irrespective of all locations.
The adotion of different management techniques 
is found to be low compared to the recommended 
practiced by BARI. Probit model showed that 
education of the farmer, farm size, availability of 
seed and contact of SAAO enhanced the adoption 
of BARI mustard improved varieties. Results 
revealed that farmers showed positive attitude 
towards adoption of improved mustard varieties 
since about 61.18% for the adopters wanted to 
increase area under improve mustard cultivation in 
next growing season considering the high yielding 
ability, low cultivation cost, high profit, less labour 
requirements and market demand. Availability of 
improved mustard seeds were also important factors 
for adoption it at farm level. 
Adoption and profitability of mandarin in Sylhet 
district
M. Akhtar Hossain, M. Asaduzzaman, M. I. Nazrul 
and K. U. Ahmad
This study explores the adoption, production 
practices, cost structure, and profitability of 
Mandarin cultivation in the Sylhet district with a 
specific focus on the Golapganj Union of Sylhet 
Sadar Upazila as a Mandarin growing area. Data 
were collected from 40 purposively and randomly 
selected Mandarin farmers through structured 
interviews conducted in February-March 2025. 
Results reveal that Mandarin cultivation in 
Sylhet is predominantly a secondary farming 
activity practiced with limited formal education 
and average landholdings of 1.32 hectares. The 
majority (80-90%) have adopted the improved 
BARI Multa-1 variety, though cultivation 
practices remain semi-traditional and low-input. 
Initial investment and input use are highest 
during the establishment year, with profitability 
emerging only after the fifth year of cultivation. 
Mature orchards (5-10 years) yield 15,825 kg/
ha and generate a net return of Tk. 395,566/ha, 
indicating long-term economic viability. BCR 
was found 1.99 in 5-10 year period while gross 
return was found zero during 1-4 year period. Key 
challenges include climate variability, pest and 
disease infestations, inadequate access to quality 
inputs, lack of modern farming knowledge, and 
water scarcity. The study recommends enhanced 
extension services, improved access to certified 
planting materials, adoption of improved 
agronomic practices, and better market linkages 
to support sustainable Mandarin production and 
improve farmer livelihoods in the Sylhet region.

Production program of sesame variety at 
Gopalganj
Sesame (Sesamum indicum) is grown in Bangladesh 
during both the kharif and autumn seasons, with 
about two-thirds of the crop produced during kharif. 
The ideal time to sow seeds is February to March, 
and the crop can be harvested after 120 to 140 days. 
Sesame is a crop that prefers hot, dry climates with 
temperatures between 25-30°C, and it can't tolerate 
waterlogging. Well-drained, loamy soil is also best 
for sesame cultivation, Average sesame yield in 
Bangladesh is about 957 kg ha -1. Currently, about 
38,923 ha of land are under sesame cultivation and 
annual production is about 37,260 m tons. BARI Til-
4 is a high yielding variety of sesame. It should be 
disseminated and popularize to farmers. With this 
point of view, production program of BARI Til-4 
was done at farmer's field of Tungipara, Gopalganj 
and Nazirpur, Pirojpur. The sowing date of crop was 
on 06 to 15 March 2025. The crop was harvested 
in 15 to 26 June 2025. The average yield and gross 
return of BARI Til-4 were 1.38 t ha-1 and Tk. 124200 
ha-1, respectively.

Pilot production program of BARI brinjal variety 
at different locations 
Eggplant (Solanum melongena L.) is a crucial 
vegetable crop in Bangladesh, significantly impacting 
the national economy and dietary needs. This study 
evaluates the performance of BARI Begun-12, an 
improved variety developed by the Bangladesh 
Agricultural Research Institute (BARI), known for 
its high yield potential, pest and disease resistance, 
and adaptability. Conducted across three districts- 
Manikganj, Faridpur and Gopalganj covering the 
land area 0.81 hectares. The multi-location trial 
assessed regional variations in yield, pest and disease 
resistance, and economic benefits. Transplanting dates 
varied across locations, ranging from late September 
to November 2024. Harvesting commenced in late 
December 2024 and continued until mid-April 2025. 
Results indicated an average yield of 44.67 t ha-1, with 
the highest in Gopalganj (61.40 t ha -1) and the lowest 
in Faridpur (31.78 t ha -1). The highest gross return 
was (Tk. 1535000 ha -1) in Gopalganj and lowest in 
Faridpur (Tk. 794500 ha -1). These variations were 
attributed to differences in soil fertility, climate, 
and farming practices. Farmer feedback highlighted 
BARI Begun-12's high yield, disease resistance, 
and market demand. The study concludes that while 
BARI Begun-12 is promising, its success depends 
on regional growing conditions, necessitating 
improvements in soil fertility and farming practices to 
enhance productivity and economic returns.

Production program of BARI linseed at Noakhali
The production program was conducted in four 
farmers' field at Companiganj and Sadar upazila 
in Noakhali district during rabi season of 2024-25 
to increase crop productivity through fallow land 
utilization. BARI Tisi-1 was used to address Fallow-
Fallow-T.Aman cropping pattern. Soils of the field 
was silty-clay loam under the saline area of AEZ 18 
with low organic matter content. Six hectare was 
covered at Companiganj by three farmers and 0.8 
hectare by one farmer at Sadar upazila. Seeds were 
sown from one to 18 November 2024 at Companiganj 
and 25 November 2024 at Sadar upazila. Seed rate 
was 7 kg ha-1. Seeds were sown with two ploughing. 
No weeding or irrigation was done. Harvesting was 
done from 15-22 March 2025. Yield of BARI Tishi-
1was higher at Companiganj (820 kg ha -1) whereas 
it was 780 kg ha -1 at Sadar upazila. Average yield 
was 815 kg ha -1. Total variable cost (TVC) was Tk. 
33600 ha-1 and it was lower than other winter crops 
as there was less fertilizer use and no pest or disease 
infestation and no weeding. Both gross return (GR) 
and gross margin (GM) was satisfactory though 
yield was low. GR at Companiganj and Sadar was 
Tk. 82000 and Tk. 78000 ha-1, respectively. As TVC 
was same for both the locations GM followed the 
seed yield. GM at Companiganj and Sadar was Tk. 
48400 and Tk. 44400 ha-1, respectively.

Pilot production program of zero tilage garlic at 
Pabna

Atghoria, Pabna during the rabi season of 2022-
23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. Farmers cultivated local 
garlic variety under zero tillage mulch condition. 
Immediately after receding of water from the field 
during the winter, the bulbs of garlic were planted 
on November 1-15, 2022; 25 November to 25 
December 2023 and November 7-15, 2024 in the 
muddy soil maintaining spacing of 15 cm x 10 cm.

farmers, 150 bighas of land involving 70 farmers 
in 2023-24 and 150 bighas of land involving 100 
farmers in 2024-25 were included in this program.

March to 15 April, 2024 and 18 March to 7 April, 
2025. Bulb yield of zero tillage garlic (10.9 t/ha, 
11.5 t/ha and 11.2 t/ha in 2022-23, 2023-24 and 
2024-25) was higher as compared to conventional 
tillage system in 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25, 
respectively.

Production of lentil as relay crop with T. Aman 
rice at Pabna
The production program was conducted at MLT site, 
Baoikhola, Atghoria, Pabna during rabi season in 
2023-24 and 2024-25. BARI developed improved 
variety BARI Masur-8 was demonstrated through 
block approach at MLT site, Baoikhola, Atghoria, 
Pabna during rabi season, 2023-24 and 2024-
25. The total size of the demonstration plot was 
about one hectare of six farmers in 2023-24 and 
four hectares of twenty farmers in 2024-25 were 
involved. The cooperative farmers were selected 
after a joint group discussion organized by OFRD, 
ARS, Pabna. Different inputs (Seed, fertilizers and 
fungicides) were supplied from OFRD, Pabna. 
The selected farmers received one day training on 
management of relay lentil production. The seeds of 
relay crops were sown on 5-15 November, 2023 and 
1-10 November, 2024, 10-12 days prior to T. Aman 
harvest. Seeds were soaked overnight in fresh water 
for seed priming. The seed rate of lentil was 45 kg 
ha-1. The crop was harvested on 17-22 March, 2024 
and 15-22 March, 2025. The mean yield obtained 
from BARI Masur-8 was 1778 kg ha-1 which ranged 
from 1751-1828 kg ha-1 in 2023-24 and 1921 kg ha-1 
which ranged from 1801-2125 kg ha-1 in 2024-25.

Upscaling of IPM package of mungbean flower 
thrips and pod borer in Barishal
The upscaling program has been conducted over four 
locations of Barishal district (Babuganj, Bakerganj, 
Rajapur and Kathalia) during Late rabi 2024-25. 
Application of bio-pesticides, chemical and blue 
sticky traps were considered as treatment of the up-
scaling program. IPM package of Blue sticky trap 
(3 numbers/decimal) + chlorfenapyr (benapore) 
1ml/L at 35-40 DAS + 2 times spray of spinosad 
(Success 2.5 EC)/coragen which was compared with 
farmers practice (voliam flexi) two-time spray at 30-
35 DAS and 45-50 DAS. Flower thrips population 
data were collected before every spray application 
and after 24 hrs of each spraying. Thrips population 
was assessed from 20 opened flower randomly 
collected from the field. The infested (bored) and 
total number of pods were counted and the percent 
pod infestation was determined using the following 
formula: % Pod infestation = (Number of infested 
pod/ Total number of pod) x 100. The grain yield was 
obtained from each plot converted into per hectare. 
The compiled data were analyzed by statistical 
software R and mean differences has been recorded 
at 5% level of significance. The effectiveness of 
IPM packages on thrips population and bod borer 
infestation was represented in Table 1. Flower thrips 
reduced drastically from number 10.50 to number 
1 and 90.12 % reduction happened after 24 hrs of 
spray. Whereas from the farmers practice, it can be 
observed from % reduction for thrips population 
was 43.21%. From four different locations, mean 
pod infestation by pod borer from IPM package was 
3.12 % and from farmers practice 10.60 %. Percent 
reduction over treatment was 74.8%. The highest 
yield can be observed from, IPM packages 1290 
Kg/ha and yield increased over control was 27.72%. 
Farmers were reluctant to use bio pesticides at first, 
but after seeing the impact of insect reduction at their 
field they become eager to use the IPM technology. 
They also opined that, biopesticides are not easily 
available at local market.

PLANT
PATHOLOGY
Executive Summary
Diseases are the main concern in crop production. 
Plant Pathology Division (PPD) mainly focus on 
basic and applied research of plant pathogens, 
disease diagnosis, monitoring and management of 
BARI mandated crops caused by different biotic 
(fungi, virus, bacteria and nematode) and abiotic 
factors. The division also work on seed pathology, 
crop loss assessment, pre-registration trial of new 
fungicides, clinical services to the growers, post-
harvest losses etc. A total of 107 experiments were 
reported during the cropping season 2023-2024 
including division centers, RARS, ARS and OFRD. 
All the research works were prioritized on the basis 
of rapporteurs reports of different reviews and 
the opinion of expert's panel on current issue and 
importance of plant pathogens (Fungus, Bacteria, 
Virus and Nematode). This cropping season we had 
conducted research programs on 30 different crops 
under Tuber crops, Pulse crops, Oilseed crops, Spice 
crops, Vegetable crops, Fruit crops, Flower crops 
and others. 
Tuber crops 
Fifteen experiments were conducted on tuber crops 
(Potato and Sweet potato) mainly focus on resistant 
screening, varietal evaluation, disease management 
and survey against fungal, bacterial and viral 
diseases. Also study the hybrid clones against viral 
disease. Several potato and sweet potato lines were 
found resistant against late blight and viral diseases. 
BARI alu-90 was selected late blight resistant where 
BARI alu-77 and 46 were moderately resistant. 
In case of fungicidal management, Cypa 52.5 
WG (Cymoxalin 30% + Famoxadone 22.5%) @ 
2mg/L was found better against late blight disease. 
According to disease survey, late blight was found 
more prevalent and PLRV , PVY , PVX etc. were 
found low to medium incidence range. 
Pulse crops 
Nine research works were executed on three pulse 
crops like lentil, chickpea and field pea regarding 
pathogen characterization, resistant screening and 
bio-chemical management of foot and root rot, 
fusarium wilt, stemphylium blight and rust disease. 
Root rot disease mainly caused by Fusarium spp. 
Rhizoctonia spp Sclerotium spp. Seed treatment 
with Provax 200 WP (Carboxin + Thiram) @ 0.3% 
also Bioderma (Trichoderma harzianum) @ 3% 
presented better performance to control foot and 
root rot disease. Fungicides Luna sensation (1ml/L), 
Navara (1ml/L), and Stromin (2g/L) successfully 
reduced the stemphylium blight disease. Seed 
treatment + Spraying with Tricomax and Soil 
amendment with tricho-compost + spraying with 
tricho-leachate in the rhizosphere performed better 
against foot and root rot disease of lentil. On the 
other hand, seed treatment with Provax 200 WP @ 
3 g/kg showed better performance + Spraying with 
Goldazim 500 SC @ 0.1% at 25 DAS and Dynamic 
WP ( Bacillus amyloliquefaciens) @ 5 g/kg seed 
to control Fusarium wilt disease of Chickpea. 
Under screening of field pea against rust disease, 
121germplasm were showed resistant and 3 were 
Moderately resistant. Nativo 75 WP as well as 
Azonil 56 EC @ 1 ml/L was found effective against 
rust disease of field pea.
Oilseed crops
Under Oilseed crops nine research programs were 
reported on mustard, groundnut and sunflower to 
find out resistant lines and manage of different 
fungal diseases. Five mustard lines (NAP-20002, 
NAP-16036, BJ-2014-Y-04, BJ-10-10104(Y), and 
BJ-1110(12)-1 were reported moderately resistant 
against Alternaria blight disease. Rovral, Amister 
top and Navara were found better for managing 
Alternaria blight and Rovral and Amistar Top for

PATHOLOGY
white mold disease. No groundnut germplasm or 
variety were found resistance against Tikka/leaf spot 
disease. Clubroot disease caused by Plasmodiophora 
brassicae was found newly emerging disease of 
oilseed crops in many areas. 
Spice crops
Eleven research works were reported on spice crops 
including onion, black cumin, chilli and turmeric 
mainly focus on varietal screening, fungicidal, 
bio-fungicidal and integrated disease management 
of fungi and viruses. Four onion lines viz. AC-
GAZ-384, AC-GAZ-380, AC-Bog423-AF5 and 
AB4(379) were preliminarily selected as promising 
against purple blotch disease. Bio-fungicide 
Lycomax was found effective against purple blotch 
disease of onion. Fungicide Luna sensation and 
Amistar top were found effective against purple 
blotch and Alternaria of onion. Black mould and 
soft rot diseases of onion were found predominant 
in the storage. Eleven different diseases were 
recorded from 8 different spice crops (Onion, 
chilli, black cumin, celery, ginger, plum, chaba, 
and vanilla). Thirty different isolates of Fusarium 
spp. were identified as a causal agent of wilt of 
black cumin. The rhizome rot (wilt) of turmeric by 
Ralstonia solanacearum was found predominant at 
different areas in Bangladesh. Plants treated with 
Trichoderma harzianum showed induced systemic 
resistant against CMV of chilli.
Vegetable crops
Thirty different experiments were executed on 
different vegetable crops like Tomato, Cucumber, 
Brinjal, Pumpkin, Bottle gourd, Okra and Country 
bean. The research works focus on resistant 
screening of different vegetable germplasm, 
fungicidal, bio-rational and integrated management 
of Fungal, Bacterial, Nematode and Viral diseases. 
Luna sensation 50 SC, Nativo 75 WG, Amistar Top 
325 SC @, Indofil M 45 @ and Rovral 50 WP were 
effectively reduced stem rot & leaf blight of tomato. 
Most of the cases integrated approach was found 
better in controlling early and late blight disease of 
vegetables. BARI Tomato-11, A V-135, A V-1616, 
1008, A VTO-1315, A V-1306, A VTO-1921 and 1903 
showed resistant reaction bacterial wilt of tomato. 
Stable Bleaching Powder @ 25kg/ha+ Burning of 
rice husk @ 4.18 t/ha (in pit) + Bacillus based bio-
fungicide was found effective against bacterial wilt 
of vegetables. One spray of Imidacloprid 0.1% at 
5 Days before transplanting + Sticky yellow trap 
in the plot + 3 sprays of Imidacloprid /Phytomax 
at 15 days' interval was reported effective against 
ToLCV of tomato. A VTO-1315, BARI Tomato-11, 
A VTO-1010, A V-1907, A VTO-1921and A V-195 
were found resistant against root-knot nematode. 
Different composts and bio-chars were effective for 
reducing root-knot nematode of vegetables. Tricho-
compost and Rugby 10G were found effective for 
reducing root-knot disease of cucurbits. Country 
bean germplasm DLST 0032 was performed the 
best to the multiple viral disease complex of country 
bean. 
Fruit crops 
Eighteen research works were executed on seven fruit 
crops like mango, guava, banana, citrus, strawberry, 
watermelon and papaya. Most of the experiments 
focus on management of fungal, bacterial and viral 
diseases. Goldazim 500 SC and NAA was found 
better for reducing mango floral malformation.
Fungicide Arba 50 WP, Goldazim 500 SC, Knowing 
50WP, Amister top and Cabrio top were selected as 
best for controlling Anthracnose of mango. Rovral 
and Poly mulch before planting + Rugby 10G @ 25 
kg/ha + Mul care @ 10 g/pit (during planting and 25-
30 DAP) + Indofil M 45 (Mancozeb) @ 2 g/l were 
found effective in controlling leaf spot, root rot and 
anthracnose disease of strawberry. Autostin 50WDG 
@ 2 g/L effectively controlled the Fusarium wilt 
of watermelon. The endophytes Iso-16 and Iso-37 
were found effective in controlling wilt disease of 
guava. Bacillus velezensis GL6 and B. tropicus K3 
and their EMOs, BHAT-03 WP showed consistent 
disease suppression to fungal wilt in BARI Kala 1.B. 
subtilis GBO3, Bacillus oryzicola YC7007, Bacillus 
velezensis were selected as a strong endophytic 
for controlling bacterial black spot of mango. 
EMOs, BHAT-02 WP made by strains YC7007 and 
YC7012 showed the good grafting projection and 
showed significantly consistent disease suppression 
to greening disease of citrus. The RB genotype of 
CTV in sweet orange was identified in Bangladesh 
by using molecular tools. Spraying of Imidacloprid 
(0.1%) 4 times at 15 days interval + sticky yellow 
trap or spraying of Phytomax (0.2%) 4 times at 
15 days interval + sticky yellow trap was found 
effective against PRSV of papaya.

Flower crops 
Five experiments were reported on flower crops 
including Marigold, Gerbera, Lilium and Aloe Vera 
mainly focus on fungal disease diseases management. 
Fungicides Novera 28SC showed good performance 
controlling botrytis blight disease of marigold and 
in case of white mold disease neem oil cake @ 800

Others

reported on characterization of pathogens and 
disease survey. Two entomopathogenic fungi were 
isolated and characterized like Cordyceps javanica 
and Beauveria sp. Morpho-physiological study was 
conducted on different isolate of S. sclerotiorum. 
Molecular identification was done for root-knot

okra, red amaranth and spinach in Bangladesh. 
Thirty-two endophytic colonizing bacterial strains 
were isolated from two solanaceous vegetable 
crops, brinjal and chilli. Two isolates were found 
antagonistic to Ralstonia Solanacearum. Different 
crops diseases were monitoring under various 
survey reports. 
Activities: Tuber crops: Potato
Evaluation of new fungicides against late blight 
of potato 
Md. Iqbal Faruk and Md. Haider Hossain
Twenty five different new fungicides were tested 
against late blight disease of potato and their 
influence on the crop was compared with a control 
(water spray). The experimental was conducted in the 
field of RARS of BARI, Cumilla during Rabi season 
of 2024-25. In this cropping season and locations, 
incidence of late blight disease was not appeared in 
the experimental field. However, fungicidal spray 
influenced the tuber yield to some extent. Among the 
25 fungicides evaluated in the present experiment, 
only 3 caused significant increase in tuber yield 
over control. The highest tuber yield was obtained 
with fungicide having code no. 1391 (45.46 t ha -1) 
followed by Melody Duo (46.11 t ha -1) and Code 
no. 1363 (45.46 t ha -1). Tuber yield in the rest 22 
fungicide were statistically similar to that of control, 
where code no. 1371 showed the lowest yield (31.15 
t ha-1), which was followed by the fungicides code 
nos. 1371 (31.28 t ha -1), 1370 (31.97 t ha -1), 1374 
(32.22 t ha -1), 1443 (32.62 t ha -1) and1387 (35.97 t 
ha-1). 
Efficacy of new fungicides in controlling late 
blight of potato
H. Rahman and M. M. Rahman 
An experiment was conducted to evaluate 25 
new chemical fungicides with a view to find out 
appropriate ones to control the late blight disease 
of potato. The experiment was conducted at the 
Regional Agricultural Research Station of BARI, 
Jamalpur during Rabi season of 2024-25 under 
natural inoculum pressure. The fungicides were 
supplied by the Pesticide Technical Advisory 
Committee (PTAC). A standard fungicide (Ridomil 
Gold 68 WG) and a control (water) were included in 
the experiment. Efficacy of new fungicides ranged 
from 9.74 to 98.82% where fungicide encoded 1615 
demonstrated the lowest efficacy as highest in the 
fungicide encoded 1669 followed by 1660 (97.37%), 
1666 (96.06%), 1718 (92.51%) and 1656 (90.82%), 
respectively. More than 95% disease suppression 
was observed due to the spray with 1660, 1666, 
1669 encoded fungicide. On the other hand, 1656 
& 1718 encoded fungicide suppressed the disease 
90.82% and 92.51%, respectively. There was over 
80% disease suppression because of the 1684, 
1686.1687, and 1711 encoded fungicide application. 
Fungicides No. 1626-1669, 1687, 1699, 1708, 1714, 
1718, 1740, 1757 and 1762 yielded significantly 
larger tuber compared to control. Except 1531, 
1615, 1622, 1740 and 1743, other 20 fungicides 
significantly increased tuber yield per hectare over 
control

Screening of potato genotypes against bacterial

M. Nazneen, F. Elahi, R. Islam, M. M. Islam, M. H.

An experiment was conducted to evaluate 36 BARI 
released potato varieties for resistance to bacterial 
wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum under pot 
conditions in the net house of the Plant Pathology 
Division, BARI, Gazipur, during the 2024-2025

were artificially inoculated with virulent isolates

Screening of antagonistic bacteria from potato 
plants and rhizosphere for their efficacy to 
control bacterial wilt 
M. Nazneen, F. Elahi, R. Islam, M. M. Islam, M. H. 
Rashid and M. H.Hossain
An experiment was conducted in the laboratory of 
plant pathology division, BARI during 2024-2025 
potato growing season to isolate bio-antagonistic 
bacteria from potato plant and rhizosphere 
to investigate their antagonistic effects on R. 
solanacearum, the causal agent of bacterial wilt 
in potato. Apparently healthy plant samples parts 
such as the tuber, root, stem, leaf, and rhizospheric 
soil were collected and isolation of bio-antagonistic 
bacteria was carried out following dilution plate 
technique on different selective media. The purified 
bacterial isolates were tested for antagonism 
against R. solanacearum through duel culture 
plate technique and streaking method. A total of 
26 different probable antagonistic bacterial strains 
were isolated. Among these, 11 isolates were found 
to possess antagonistic effects on R. solanacearum, 
showing inhibition zone ranging from 1.8 to 19.62 
mm in diameter and suppressing the pathogen 
population in agar disc diffusion assays.

Activities: Pulse Crops
Lentil
Identification and characterization of root rot 
pathogens of lentil of ishurdi
D. Sarkar, M. Z. Rahman, M. A. A. Momin, M. 
Akhterruzzaman, M. Hossain, J. Hossan, M. and R. 
Humauan 
Root rot disease is one of the major threats to 
production of the lentil in Bangladesh. It is very 
complex to identify which soil-borne pathogens 
are associated with root rot disease on lentil and to 
determine their prevalence, a survey was conducted 
from November 2024 to March 2025 at different 
pulse-growing regions in Bangladesh. Lentil root 
rot symptoms were obtained from seven Research 
plots in various Agri-ecological Zones. Rotted roots 
were washed, potential pathogens were cultured, 
and isolates were putatively identified into the major 
pathogen groups based on morphology and cultural 
variation. The percentage of Fusarium spp during 
the survey was the most dominant (38%) compared 
to other pathogens. where Rhizoctonia, Sclerotium, 
and Oomycetes & unidentified isolates recovered 
ranged from 18%, 13%, and 31% respectively. 
From the pathogenicity test, Rhizoctonia and 
unidentified isolates were attacked early compared 
to the Fusarium and Sclerotium isolates. This survey 
provided baseline information on the prevalence 
of critical soil-borne pathogens. In the future, 
additional genetic markers will be utilized to further 
identify organisms, a species characterization will 
be conducted to assess pathogenicity and virulence, 
and lentil germplasm will be screened for resistance.

Evaluation of biosynthesized AgNPs against foot 
and root rot pathogens of lentil
M. Z. Rahman, D. Sarkar, A. K. M. Sahfiqul Islam 
and A. K. M. Alam
Foot and root rot disease caused by Sclerotium 
rolfsii, Rhizoctonia solani, and Fusarium sp, 
which inflicts significant yield losses of about 
100 %. To address this, the green synthesis of 
AgNPs using Azadirachta indica (Neem), Moringa 
oleifera (Moringa) leaf extract, and silver nitrate 
(AgNO3), examined their efficacy against foot and 
root rot disease. The biosynthesized AgNPs were 
characterized through various analytical techniques. 
The results of UV-visible spectrophotometers 
revealed an absorption peak ranging from 421 to 
434 nm, validating the synthesis of AgNPs in the 
solution. In vitro assays demonstrated the significant 
inhibitory effects of AgNPs on mycelial growth of 
F . oxysporum, R. solani, and S. rolfsii particularly 
at Ag:N (10:3) and Ag:NM (10:1) concentrations. 
The findings highlight the potential of AgNPs as a 
sustainable and effective alternative for managing 
foot and root rot disease in lentil, offering a safer 
solution amidst environmental concerns associated 
with conventional fungicides.

The root rot disease is one of the major threats to the

Screening of fungicides in controlling clubroot 
disease of mustard
H. Rahman, M. M. Rahman and M M Islam
The experiment was conducted to find out the efficacy 
of fungicides against clubroot disease and for yield 
and yield contributing characters of Mustard at the 
research field of Plant Pathology Division, RARS 
Jamalpur, during the Rabi season of 2024-2025. 
The experiment was conducted under natural field 
conditions. The study consists of 8 (eight) treatments 
viz., T1= Acrobat MZ (Dimethomorph+ Mancozeb) 
@ 2 g/L, T2= Ridomil Gold (Metalaxyl) @ 2 g/L, T3= 
Dolochune @ 5 t/ha, T4=Luna sensation (Fluopyrum 
+ Trifloxystrobin) @ 2 ml/L, T 5 = Amistar Top 
(Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole) @ 2 ml/L, T 6= 
Nativo 75 WG (Tebuconazole + Trifloxystrobin) 
@ 2 ml/L, T 7= Blitox (Copper fungicide) @ 2 g/L 
and T 8= Control. BARI Sarisha-14 was used in 
this study as variety. Only 0.59% of infected plants 
were found in the control treatment (T8) where 
disease severity is 1 and disease status was a few 
small clubs in the infected plants. Other treatments 
had no infection (no clubbing). These findings 
indicate that fungicides application for controlling 
clubroot disease of BARI Sarisha-14 is not effective 
because very few percentage infections were found 
in control treatment under natural field conditions. 
Artificial inoculation of clubroot inoculum in the 
plants afterwards application of fungicides would 
be effective. The highest seed yield per hectare 
(1768.52 kg) noted in the T 7 treatment followed by 
the T8 treatment (1720.37 kg), T 1 and T2 treatments 
(1703.70 kg). These findings indicate that although 
seed yield performance exhibits significant 
variations among the treatments but only one 
treatment showed better performances compared to 
control. On the other hand, two treatments showed 
at par seed yield performance with the control and 
four treatments showed inferior performance to 
control that might be due to the uneven population 
and land heterogeneity.

Management of seed borne mycoflora on 
mustard, soybean and field pea seed and their 
pathogenic potential
R. Momotazm. Arifunahar, S.T.Nira, F.Elahi, M. 
Monir, M. H. Rashid and M.H.Hosain
The experiment was conducted during the 2024-
2025 cropping season in the laboratory and pot 
house of the Plant Pathology Division, Bangladesh 
Agricultural Research Institute (BARI), Gazipur, 
to evaluate effective seed treatment for managing 
seed-borne fungal pathogens of mustard (Brassica 
campestris L.), soybean (Glycine max), and field 
peas (Pisum sativum). Six treatments were tested: 
T1-Detergent (0.1%), T2-Kerosene/paraffin 
(0.1%), T3-Bleaching powder (5000 mg/ml), 
T4-Provax 200 (2500 mg/ml), T5-Soft drinks 
(0.1%), and T6-Untreated control. Laboratory 
results in three seed crops revealed that the detergent 
treatment (T1) consistently achieved the highest 
seed germination rates, seedling vigor, and the most 
effective reduction in seed-borne fungal infections 
across all crops, followed by T3 and T4. In contrast, 
untreated seeds (T6) showed the highest levels 
of infection and lowest germination. In the pot 
house trial with mustard, detergent treatment also 
resulted in the highest vigor index (1864.25), lowest 
infection rate (9.59%), and highest plant survival 
(98.08%). Fungal pathogens isolated from seeds 
and seedlings included Fusarium spp., Aspergillus 
spp., Penicillium spp., Alternaria spp., Rhizoctonia 
solani, and Sclerotium rolfsii, each characterized 
by distinct colony morphology and associated 
symptoms.

Sunflower
Evaluation of some fungicides against leaf blight 
of sunflower
N. A. Sultana and K. Jahan 
A field experiment was conducted at the Oilseed 
Research Centre (ORC), Gazipur, during the 
2024-2025 cropping season to evaluate the efficacy 
of seven fungicides in managing Alternaria leaf 
blight of sunflower (Helianthus annuus L.) and 
their impact on yield and yield-contributing traits. 
The study followed a Randomised Complete Block 
Design with eight treatments, including a control. 
Fungicides were applied at disease onset and 
repeated at 10-day intervals. Results revealed that 
Rovral (0.2%) was the most effective, significantly 
reducing disease incidence by 65.49% over the 
control and achieving the highest seed yield (1722.3 
kg/ha), representing a 34% yield increase. Amistar 
Top (0.1%), was the second highest, significantly 
reducing disease incidence by 58.89% over the 
control and achieving the seed yield (1673 kg/ha), 
representing a 32% yield increase. Score (0.1%), 
and Folicure (0.1%) also provided moderate 
disease control and yield enhancement. In contrast, 
Mancer, Tilt, and Mancozeb were less effective. 
The untreated control exhibited the highest disease 
severity and the lowest yield. These findings suggest 
that Rovral, followed by Amistar Top and score, can 
be effectively integrated into disease management 
strategies to control Alternaria blight and improve 
sunflower productivity. Considering the benefit cost 
ratio, the fungicide Amistar Top (0.1%), was found 
to be highly economic (BCR 3.8).
Effect of sowing date on the Alternaria blight 
diseases severity and yield contributing 
characters of sunflower
K. Jahan and N. Sultana
A field experiment was carried out during winter 
season, 2024-25 at Oilseed Research Centre, BARI, 
Gazipur to find out Alternaria leaf blight incidence 
and severity in sunflower varieties sown at early, 
mid and late sowing dates in November, December 
and January. Alternaria leaf blight caused by 
Alternaria helianthi is considered as most dangerous 
that reduce productivity. A survey has revealed that 
losses due to this in seed yield ranging from 27-
80%, oil yield from 17-33%.The experiment was 
conducted in randomized block design with three 
replications. Two varieties BARI Sunflower-3 and 
Hysun-33 and nine sowing dates were used in this 
field trial. Disease severity, under natural conditions 
in the field, was evaluated at four growth stages 
of the crop, with reference to "0-5" scale of this 
disease. Marked plants were harvested individually 
according to their maturity for evaluation of 
yield and yield contributing characters. The 
results showed significant effects of sowing dates 
and varieties on yield and yield components of 
sunflower. BARI Sunflower-3 always showed higher 
disease severity e.g. 41.8% at vegetative stage at 30 
January compared to Hysun-33 where severity was 
21.8%. Lowest percent diseased leaf area (10%) 
was observed in December sowings, whereas higher 
percent diseased leaf area (40-45%) in late January 
sowings. November sowings also show moderately 
high percentage of leaf area covered by the disease 
(30-35%). Hysun-33 gave the highest seed yield at 
10 November followed by 20 November with 272 
gm and 230.33gm/5plants seed weight, respectively. 
Whereas, BARI Sunflower-3 showed higher seed 
yield (151.33 gm/5plants seed) at 20 November. The 
higher plant height, stem diameter, head diameter, 
500-seed weight and no. of mature seed/head were 
also observed in mid-November to early-December 
sowings. Delayed sowing also shortened the 
crop duration of sunflower in the field. For BARI 
Sunflower-3 and Hysun-33, crop duration reduces 
by about 34 and 26 days when sowing is delayed 
from early November to late January, respectively. 
The study recommended mid-November to early-
December as optimal sunflower planting dates For 
BARI Sunflower-3 and Hysun-33.
